patterns.title: Target and flags
patterns.body:
- Target: ARM946E-S (ARMv5TE), primarily Thumb mode
- Flags: `-O4,p -enum int -lang c99 -char signed -inline on,noauto -interworking`
- `-O4,p` means level 4 optimization with peephole; this aggressively reorders code
- `-inline on,noauto` means inlining is allowed but only when explicitly requested (via `inline` keyword or `__attribute__((always_inline))`)

patterns.title: Register allocation follows declaration order
patterns.body:
- MWCC allocates registers in order: r0-r3 for arguments, r4-r7 for locals (Thumb), r4-r11 for locals (ARM); arguments beyond 4 on the stack; return values in r0 (r0-r1 for 64-bit).
- MWCC assigns callee-saved registers based on variable declaration order in the function. Reordering declarations can swap registers and break matching.
- When the asm uses r6 for variable A and r7 for variable B, try declaring B before A (MWCC sometimes allocates in reverse declaration order).
- Moving a declaration from block scope to function scope changes register lifetime and can affect allocation — match the original variable scoping as closely as C89 allows.
- Functions with many locals: register pressure causes spills to stack in specific order; declaration order is load-bearing.

patterns.title: Stack frame shape
patterns.body:
- `push {r4-r7, lr}` / `pop {r4-r7, pc}` is typical Thumb prologue/epilogue.
- `sub sp, #N` for local variables; `add sp, #N` before return; stack variables accessed via `sp + offset`.

patterns.title: Control flow lowering
patterns.body:
- `if/else` compiles to `cmp + bCC`; `switch` compiles to branch table or cascading compares depending on density.
- Loops compile test-at-top or test-at-bottom; MWCC often hoists loop-invariant loads outside the loop body.
- MWCC sometimes emits `bx` to switch between ARM/Thumb for interworking.

patterns.title: Data access shapes
patterns.body:
- Global data accessed via `ldr rN, =address` (literal pool).
- Struct member access: `ldr rN, [rBase, #offset]`; array access: index * element_size + base.
- Load width reveals the type: `ldrb`=u8, `ldrh`=u16, `ldrsh`=s16, `ldrsb`=s8, `ldr`=u32/pointer.

patterns.title: Common MWCC idioms
patterns.body:
- `mov r0, #0` / `mov r0, #1` for FALSE/TRUE returns.
- `add rN, rM, #0` is `mov rN, rM` in Thumb; `lsl r0, r0, #0` is a NOP MWCC sometimes emits.

patterns.title: Small source changes that move codegen
patterns.body:
- Variable declaration order affects register allocation.
- `u32` vs `int` can change sign-extension instructions; `size / 2` vs `size >> 1` can differ at -O4 — try both.
- Ternary `a ? b : c` can produce different code than `if/else`.
- Assigning to a temp variable vs direct use changes register lifetimes.
- `NELEMS(array)` (sizeof/sizeof) matches constant folding.
- Casting to `(void)` suppresses warnings without changing codegen.

patterns.title: u16 parameter narrowing tells you the original type
patterns.body:
- A `u16` param makes MWCC insert `lsls rN,rN,#16; lsrs rN,rN,#16` narrowing at function entry; `int` params skip it. No narrowing at entry but `ldrh` use inside → the original param was likely `int` (or the caller's header said `int`).
- Calling a `u16`-declared function with an `int` argument inserts narrowing at the call site. No narrowing in the asm → the callee's prototype used `int`.
- Tail-call wrappers must forward argument types exactly — changing `int` → `u16` inserts unwanted narrowing before the tail call.

patterns.title: Switch case bodies are emitted in source order
patterns.body: MWCC emits switch case code blocks in **source order**, not numeric order. Jump-table entries are always numeric, but the code they point to follows source layout — reorder the C cases to match the asm's block order. Fall-through patterns also depend on case order.

patterns.title: Branch polarity reveals || vs &&
patterns.body:
- `if (a || b) { body }` → `cmp a; bne body; cmp b; beq skip`
- `if (a && b) { body }` → `cmp a; beq skip; cmp b; beq skip`
The branch direction (beq vs bne after comparisons) tells you which logical operator was used; getting it wrong produces same-size code with different branch instructions.

patterns.title: GF_ASSERT and if/else direction
patterns.body: `GF_ASSERT(cond)` expands to `if (!cond) GF_AssertFail()` — the assert-fail path is the else branch. `cmp; beq over_assert; bl AssertFail` corresponds to `if (flag == 0) { GF_AssertFail(); }`, not `GF_ASSERT(flag != 0)` — both are logically equivalent but produce different branch polarity. Swapping which path comes first changes encoding.

patterns.title: lsls/lsrs pairs are bitfield extractions
patterns.body: `lsls rN,rN,#K; lsrs rN,rN,#K` extracts the low (32-K) bits. Use a bitfield struct member (e.g. `u32 fileId : 24`) rather than `& 0x00FFFFFF` — the mask may generate `ldr + and` with a literal-pool constant instead. `(x << 8) >> 8` can also produce the pattern but may not match. Bit packing order is compiler-specific: use bitfield structs, not masks.

patterns.title: Loop shape selection
patterns.body:
- `for (i = 0; i < N; i++)` may compile as test-at-bottom (do/while shape) at -O4; if the count can be zero there's an early-exit check.
- Byte-clearing loops (`strb; adds; subs; bne`) need C that puts decrement+branch at the bottom: `do { } while (--n)` vs `while (n != 0) { n--; }` produce different patterns — trial and error is sometimes required.

patterns.title: cmp r4 vs cmp r0 after a parameter copy (copy propagation)
patterns.body: When a parameter (r0) is copied to a callee-saved register (`adds r4, r0, #0`), MWCC copy-propagates: comparisons on the copy are substituted back to r0. `adds r4,r0,#0; cmp r4,#N` ONLY occurs when r0 is a **function return value** saved before a later call would clobber it. If the target asm shows the cmp-on-copy pattern at function entry with no preceding bl, pure C cannot produce it — use NONMATCHING (seen in unk_0200B150.s OamManager_Create).

patterns.title: Shared-header signatures are load-bearing across compilation units
patterns.body: MWCC `-ipa file` analyzes at file scope: changing a function's return or parameter types in a shared header causes cascading codegen changes in ALL functions in any compilation unit that calls it — even callers that discard the return value. If matched file A.c includes header H.h, you cannot change any declaration in H.h that A.c uses (even `void PlayBGM(u16)` → `BOOL PlayBGM(u16)`) without risking A.c's match. Workarounds: decompile header-sharing files as a group (sound.h family), fix all signatures in one coordinated commit, or NONMATCHING the conflicting functions.

patterns.title: Non-static does NOT prevent IPA
patterns.body: Making functions non-static does **not** stop `-ipa file` from optimizing across them — IPA analyzes all bodies in the compilation unit regardless of linkage. The objdump symbol table showing 'g' (global) on asm objects just means the assembler defaults labels to global, not that the original C was non-static. static vs non-static does slightly change register allocation in some cases, but never disables IPA CSE.

patterns.title: IPA CSE caches repeated literal-pool addresses
patterns.body: When a caller passes the same static-data address to a callee multiple times, MWCC may cache those addresses in callee-saved registers across calls, displacing other variables to the stack. The original binary may not do this if the original source structure prevented it (structure unknown). This is the blocking issue in unk_0200FA24 (BeginNormalPaletteFade calls sub_0200FE84 twice with identical pointer args).

patterns.title: Section ↔ C mapping
patterns.body:
- `.rodata` = const arrays/tables (use `const`); `.data` = initialized mutable globals; `.bss` = zero-initialized globals.
- Global variable order matters: declarations must match the asm order, and `.rodata` array order must match the section layout (an all-functions-match file can still fail ROM SHA1 on rodata order — see unk_0201010C).
- `.balign 4, 0` pads to 4-byte boundary — use struct padding or explicit alignment.
- ARM is little-endian: `.byte 0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00` = u32 `0x00000025`.

patterns.title: Data-only files
BSS sizing with raw byte arrays
patterns.body: When asm BSS symbol sizes don't match `sizeof(StructType)`, use a raw `u8 array[0xNN]` and cast at usage sites: `*(StructType *)array`. Multiple BSS variables become separate `.bss` sections in the object but the linker merges them — the total size must match.

patterns.title: Contiguous data arrays accessed via base+offset
patterns.body: When multiple data labels are accessed from a common base pointer (e.g. `ldr r0, =_0210F64C; str r1, [r0, #0x10]` targeting `_0210F65C`), the labels are contiguous. Declare them as separate static arrays in order — MWCC lays them out contiguously. Stores use base symbol + offset while call arguments use the target symbol directly; both produce correct literal pools as long as the arrays are separate declarations (not one big array with #defines).

patterns.title: Task callback pattern (field system)
patterns.body:
1. A public `sub_XXXX` allocates a work struct via `Heap_AllocAtEnd`, fills it, calls `TaskManager_Call(man, callback, env)`.
2. A static callback uses `TaskManager_GetFieldSystem` + `TaskManager_GetEnvironment`, implements a state machine (switch on `env->state`), returns TRUE when done after `Heap_Free`.
- The callback is referenced by literal pool (`_XXXX: .word sub_YYYY`) in the caller.
- Work struct fields can be inferred from how the caller stores arguments and the callback reads offsets.

patterns.title: Save chunk pattern
patterns.body:
1. `sub_XXXX_sizeof(void)` returns `sizeof(StructType)` — trivial.
2. `sub_XXXX_init(StructType *a0)` clears with `MI_CpuClear32`/`MI_CpuClear8` then sets defaults.
3. A getter calls `SaveArray_Get(saveData, SAVE_INDEX)` and returns the pointer; field getters/setters are trivial.
- `save_arrays.c` registers these via `DECL_CHUNK_EX` — replace the macro with an `#include` of the new header and remove the `DECL_CHUNK_EX` line. Check the index in `include/constants/save_arrays.h`.

patterns.title: Overlay specifics
patterns.body:
- Overlay functions are named `ovNN_XXXXXXXX` (NN = overlay number, XXXXXXXX = address); overlay code loads at specific VMAs visible in labels.
- Overlay dependencies are declared in main.lsf (`After` clauses); each overlay has its own .sbin SHA1.

patterns.title: Public vs static visibility
patterns.body: Always check `asm/include/<file>.inc` `.public` declarations before marking functions static. Public functions must NOT be static (overlays call static-module functions by name → linker Undefined errors otherwise) and belong in `include/<file>.h`. The `.public` list mixes exports and imports — cross-reference with `thumb_func_start`/`arm_func_start` to split them.

patterns.title: Enum casts required by -W noimplicitconv
patterns.body:
MWCC rejects implicit int→enum conversions:
- `NarcId`: `GfGfxLoader_LoadCharData((NarcId)0x26, ...)`
- `GFPalSlotOffset`: cast computed expressions like `(enum GFPalSlotOffset)(palette_num << 5)`
- Any computed integer passed to an enum parameter needs an explicit cast.

patterns.title: NONMATCHING inline asm syntax (MWCC)
patterns.body:
When using `asm void FuncName(...)`:
- `ldr rN, =0xVALUE` for literal-pool constants (NOT `ldr rN, label` + `label: .word`); `ldr rN, =FuncName` for function pointers.
- `bl FuncName` works directly; local labels (`_0201013A:`) work for branches.
- `.balign` directives are NOT supported — remove them.
- Wrap in `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on`, and gate the C version with `#ifdef NONMATCHING`.

patterns.title: objdiff.py usage and reliability
patterns.body:
```bash
cp build/heartgold.us/asm/foo.o /tmp/foo_asm.o   # before flipping main.lsf
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py /tmp/foo_asm.o build/heartgold.us/src/foo.o
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py ... --summary      # also checks .rodata/.data/.bss
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py ... --bytes sub_X  # per-function byte diff
```
- Plain function MATCH is based on **size**, not bytes — same-size functions with different registers report as MATCH. Verify critical functions with `--disasm FN`/`--bytes FN`.
- `--summary` checks data sections too; use it when pre-existing build errors block full-ROM `make compare`.

patterns.title: Build workflow on macOS
patterns.body:
- Always `chiri pkg -- build` (or `-- compare`), never raw `make -C` — Wine CWD resolution breaks through symlinks and `.d` files get stale `Z:` paths (make spins at 100% CPU).
- Fast iteration: `chiri pkg -- build --target main --no-compare` (ARM9 only), then `chiri pkg -- compare`.
- Corrupted `.d` files: `find build -name "*.d" -delete` then `chiri pkg -- tidy` and rebuild.
- Prerequisites: `brew install gnu-sed arm-gcc-bin` (osx-cross/homebrew-arm tap).

patterns.title: recomp.sh build recovery
patterns.body: `./tools/decomp_harness/recomp.sh` handles build recovery: `--kill` (stale make/wine/mwcc), `--fix-d` (corrupted .d files), `--full` (clean rebuild), no args = kill + fix .d + tidy + rebuild main. Use when builds hang at 100% CPU, error after an asm→C switch in main.lsf, or won't restart after an interrupt.

patterns.title: Other known difficult patterns
patterns.body:
- Nested struct initialization may need exact field ordering to match.
- Inline functions from headers must match exactly as the compiler would expand them (e.g. MI_CpuClearFast/MI_CpuCopyFast wrappers inline into MIi_* tail calls — call the wrapper, not MIi_* directly).
- Functions with a `_` prefix are often compiler-generated or SDK functions (`_s32_div_f`).

patterns.title: Verify a single object when the full build is blocked
patterns.body: When an unrelated pre-existing error aborts make main (e.g. a dup-decl in a shared header), you can still compile+verify ONE file: cp the asm reference first (build/heartgold.us/asm/<name>.o to /tmp), switch main.lsf, then build just that object via the chiri make-target passthrough: chiri pkg -- build --no-compare -- build/heartgold.us/src/<name>.o (default --target all => empty make target, so the bare object path is the only thing built). Then objdiff.py --summary /tmp/<name>_asm.o build/heartgold.us/src/<name>.o. Isolates your file from the broken TU; gives function+data .o-level verification without the full ROM SHA1.

patterns.title: Cast a signed param to unsigned to force bhs/blo branches
patterns.body: When a function param is declared signed (e.g. int) per its fixed header, but the asm compares it with an UNSIGNED branch (bhs/blo/bhi/bls) against a u16 table value, force the comparison unsigned by casting at the comparison site: if ((u32)mapsec < p[1]). The cast is free (no instruction) and flips bge/blt -> bhs/blo. A signed int vs u16 promotes both to int and yields signed branches, so the cast is required. Distinguish per-comparison: the loop counter (int i) can stay signed (blt) in the same function while the value comparison is unsigned.

patterns.title: MWCC errors on int->enum implicit conversion (use named enum constants)
patterns.body: MWCC -W error treats passing an int literal to an enum-typed parameter as an illegal implicit conversion (e.g. Heap_Create(3, 0x30, ...) where params are enum HeapID -> illegal implicit conversion from int to HeapID). Fix: use the named enum constant (HEAP_ID_3, HEAP_ID_48) or an explicit (enum X) cast. Codegen is identical (mov #imm), so this is purely about getting it to compile. The enum HEAP_ID_<N> names are sequential = value N.

patterns.title: Raw pointer casts to magic hardware addresses match byte-for-byte
patterns.body: For files touching fixed DS addresses (0x027FFxxx ROM-header/system-work region), *(u32 *)0xADDR (direct) gives ldr =0xADDR; ldr [r0]; *(u32 *)((u8 *)BASE + off) gives ldr =BASE (loaded once, reused); ldr [rN,#off]. The SAME address can appear both ways in one function (flag check *(u32*)0x027FF00C and header->gamecode at base 0x027FF000 +0xC) -> use both forms. Named HW_ consts (HW_ROM_HEADER_BUF, HW_CARD_ROM_HEADER, HW_CARD_ROM_HEADER_SIZE) match identically to raw literals. A stack struct of size 0xN (FSFile=0x48) gives sub sp,#0xN; read field via *(u32*)((u8*)&s+off).

patterns.title: objdiff bl-placeholder diffs are benign; chiri pkg -- compare is authoritative
patterns.body: objdiff.py can report DIFF on a function whose disassembly is byte-identical except the UNRELOCATED bl placeholder bytes: the assembler (mwasmarm) emits f7ff fffe for an external call, MWCC emits f000 f800. objdiff sees these as real halfword diffs (and may not pair them as bl-reloc diffs), but the linker overwrites both with the same relocated offset, so the final ROM is identical. Always confirm with chiri pkg -- compare (full ROM SHA1) before rejecting OR accepting: compare is the only authoritative test. objdiff also MISSES section-level diffs (alignment/padding/rodata). Use objdiff --disasm to confirm a flagged diff is only bl placeholders, then trust compare.

patterns.title: Force a jump table: list ALL dense cases explicitly (sparse -> if-else)
patterns.body: When the asm uses a Thumb jump table (cmp rN,#max; bhi default; add rN,rN; add rN,pc; ldrh [rN,#6]; add pc,rN; then a halfword offset table), the C switch must cover the range 0..max DENSELY. Listing only the cases with bodies (e.g. case 1, case 4) plus default makes MWCC emit an if-else comparison chain instead (shorter, wrong). Fix: list EVERY case 0..max explicitly, giving the empty ones a bare break (case 0: break; case 2: break; ...). MWCC then sees a dense 0..max switch and emits the jump table. Body blocks are emitted in source order, so order the non-empty cases to match the asm block layout. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm (if-else cmp chain vs add pc,rN). Note: objdiff may report a spurious SIZE diff on a matching jump-table function because it disassembles the data-region table as code ($d/$t mapping symbols differ) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare.

patterns.title: Save-chunk decomp IPA-safe: dedicated header, LEAVE save_arrays.c DECL_CHUNK_EX
patterns.body: To decompile a save-chunk module (SaveArray_Get + MIi_CpuClear32, sizeof/init + field accessors) without IPA cascade: (1) put the struct + all prototypes in a NEW dedicated include/<name>.h that ONLY the new .c includes. (2) DO NOT modify save_arrays.c — leave its DECL_CHUNK_EX(sizefn, initfn) macro in place. Replacing the macro with #include <name>.h (the old pre-IPA-discipline move) recompiles save_arrays.c against a changed header set and IPA-cascades its codegen -> ROM mismatch. The DECL_CHUNK_EX extern decls and the new header decls coexist fine (separate TUs). sizeof fn: return sizeof(Struct); init: MI_CpuClear32(ptr, <sizeoffn>()) then set defaults; getter: return SaveArray_Get(saveData, SAVE_UNK_NN). Verify with chiri pkg -- compare (objdiff bl-placeholder diffs on the init are benign). Supersedes the earlier save-chunk-pattern that said to replace the macro.

patterns.title: Declaration order controls r2/r3 allocation for same-lifetime locals
patterns.body: When two locals share a live range and compete for low Thumb registers (r2/r3), MWCC -O4,p assigns the FIRST-DECLARED variable to the LOWER register. If objdiff shows two functions identical except a consistent r2<->r3 (or rN<->rM) swap, reorder the local declarations to flip the allocation. Example: unk_02017FAC sub_02017FAC needed int i=0 declared before const u16 *p=table so i->r2 (counter/return reg) and p->r3 (walked pointer), matching asm.

patterns.title: Frozen struct-only shared header: use a self-sufficient _internal.h in the defining TU
patterns.body: When a save-chunk struct lives in a SHARED header frozen to struct-only (no global.h, no prototypes) so save_arrays.c stays byte-matched, that header cannot serve as the defining .c file main header: clang-format (IncludeBlocks Regroup + main-header-first) forces the same-stem header to the very top, ahead of global.h (priority 2), so u8/u16 are undefined when the struct parses. Fix: create include/<name>_internal.h that #includes global.h then re-declares the identical struct, and include THAT in the .c (its different stem dodges the main-header rule, so global.h sorts first). Leave the frozen header and save_arrays.c (DECL_CHUNK_EX) untouched; give public fns local forward declarations. Verify save_arrays.o is byte-identical (cmp) to confirm no IPA cascade. Example: unk_0202E41C.

patterns.title: Hoist a reused computed size into a local so it lives in a callee-saved register
patterns.body: When the asm computes a value once (e.g. count*4 via a single lsls) and keeps it in a callee-saved register (r4-r7) across multiple calls that reuse it (Heap_Alloc size AND FS_ReadFile len), the source declared an explicit local for it. Recomputing inline (header.a*4 written at each Heap_Alloc/FS_ReadFile site) makes MWCC reload+recompute each time -> function grows (asm 164B, naive C 170B) and the value never occupies a persistent callee-saved reg. Fix: u32 sizeA = header.a*4; pass sizeA to both the alloc and the read. Diagnose via objdiff size diff + extra ldrh/lsls before each use. Reg pick (r6 vs r4) follows usual decl-order/param-reuse: a dead param register (path in r4) is reused for the later-born size local. Example: overlay_01_021EA6C4 ov01_021EA73C.

patterns.title: Use a private struct + cast when a shared param struct is incomplete (IPA-safe)
patterns.body: When a function must allocate/fill a struct that an EXTERNAL matched function takes by pointer (e.g. PokeathlonCourse_LaunchApp(.., PokeathlonCourseArgs*)), but the shared struct in its header is incomplete/placeholder (filler bytes, more-fields-to-discover) and is included by other already-matched files: do NOT edit the shared header to name the fields (recompiles those TUs -> IPA cascade risk). Instead define a fully-typed PRIVATE struct in your .c with the exact byte layout you need and cast to the real type only at the external call: PokeathlonCourse_LaunchApp(fs, (PokeathlonCourseArgs *)work->app). sizeof(private)==sizeof(real) so the alloc size literal matches; field offsets you control reproduce the exact ldrb/ldrh/strb. Zero shared-header change = zero IPA risk. Example: unk_02095DF4 sub_02095E30.

patterns.title: A u16 value loaded via ldrh compares unsigned (bcc/blo) against a constant without a cast
patterns.body: When a function param/value is u16 and is read via ldrh (zero-extended), a bounds check like GF_ASSERT(index < 4) compiles to cmp + bcc (unsigned blo) WITHOUT needing an explicit (u32) cast — MWCC knows the ldrh-zero-extended value is non-negative and emits the unsigned branch. This is distinct from the signed-int-vs-u16 case (cast-unsigned-for-branch) where a value already widened to int needs an explicit (u32) cast to flip bge/blt to bhs/blo. Rule of thumb: keep the param u16 (matches the ldrh) and write the plain comparison; only add the (u32) cast when the value is int-typed. Example: overlay_80_02239AF8 ov80_02239AF8 (u16 index).

patterns.title: MWCC collapses a deliberately-redundant double zero-load; NONMATCHING after a couple tries
patterns.body: Some asm loads the SAME constant 0 into two registers (e.g. a byte-clear fill in caller-saved r1 + a separate i/state 0 in callee-saved r4), i.e. it is LESS optimal than necessary. Pure C re-converges: MWCC -O4 constant-coalesces the two zeros into one callee-saved register (the fill merges into i), producing one fewer movs -> a 2-byte SIZE diff. Source tricks that do NOT break the coalesce: block-scoping the clear, a named u8 fill var, tying state=i (manager->state = i; for(;i<2;i++)), C99 for-scoped i, do-while vs for. If you see a function that is identical except the asm has an extra movs #0 (redundant constant load) that your C optimizes away, do not burn many build cycles -- NONMATCHING that one function (asm static, keep C under ifdef NONMATCHING) and move on. Example: overlay_01_021FB4C0 ov01_021FB55C (struct byte-clear + slot-init).

patterns.title: Frozen prototype header (u32 sigs, no global.h) also needs the _internal.h split
patterns.body: Generalizes frozen-struct-header-split to plain PROTOTYPE headers. If include/<name>.h declares the module funcs (e.g. u32 ov01_xxx(u32,u32)) but does NOT include global.h (relies on callers including global.h first), and it is included by already-matched files: when YOU write src/<name>.c, clang-format IncludeBlocks=Regroup + main-header-first force the same-stem <name>.h to the very top, ABOVE global.h. u32 is then undefined while the header parses -> MWCC treats u32 as implicit int -> later types.h redeclares u32 as unsigned long -> error: identifier u32 redeclared / function has no prototype. Fix: do NOT include the same-stem header in the .c; create include/<name>_internal.h (different stem dodges the main-header sort, sorts AFTER global.h) that #includes global.h then declares the same prototypes; include THAT. Leave the frozen <name>.h untouched so the matched callers do not recompile. Example: overlay_01_021F467C.

patterns.title: Include NNS via global.h, never the leaf <nnsys/...> headers directly
patterns.body: NNS SDK leaf headers (e.g. <nnsys/g3d/binres/res_struct_accessor.h>, res_struct_accessor_inline.h, kernel.h, gfd VramMan types) do NOT include their own prerequisite type headers -> including them directly gives MWCC declaration syntax error (NNSG3dResMdlSet etc. undefined). The umbrella nnsys/g3d.h includes them in the correct dependency order, and global.h -> nitro/nnsys pulls the whole chain. Fix: rely on #include global.h for ALL NNS types AND inline accessors (NNS_G3dGetMdlByIdx, NNS_G3dGetResDataByIdx live in res_struct_accessor_inline.h which g3d.h includes). Do not add explicit <nnsys/...> includes; clang-format also sorts angle-bracket system includes to the TOP (above global.h), compounding the undefined-type failure. Example: unk_02069660.

patterns.title: Force an unsigned loop branch (bcc/blo) with a 2u literal, keeping the counter int
patterns.body: When a loop counter is int but the asm uses an UNSIGNED branch (bcc/blo) for its bound check (cmp #N; bcc), changing the counter type to u32 fixes the branch BUT can shuffle the whole functions register allocation (u32 changes how MWCC allocates the counter and dependent temps). Instead keep the counter as int and make ONLY the comparison unsigned with an unsigned literal: for (i = 0; i < 2u; i++). The int->unsigned promotion at the compare site flips blt->bcc with zero extra instructions and leaves register allocation identical to the int version. Use this when the int version matched everything EXCEPT signed-vs-unsigned loop branches. Example: overlay_80_022384D8 ov80_0223857C (2x2 fill loops).

patterns.title: Force MWCC to batch field loads before arithmetic with explicit operand locals in load order
patterns.body: When a function reads several struct fields then does arithmetic on them (e.g. a point-in-rect test computing right=x+width-1, bottom=y+height-1), MWCC -O4,p's scheduler chooses whether to BATCH all the loads up front or INTERLEAVE load-compute-load-compute. Writing `int right = zone->x + zone->width - 1; int bottom = zone->y + zone->height - 1;` (named result locals, or fully-inline exprs) made MWCC compute right completely (load x, load width, add, sub) BEFORE loading y/height -> a same-SIZE-but-byte-different mismatch plus a consistent rN<->rM swap (right/y landed in swapped registers). The original loaded ALL four fields first (x, width, y, height) then did both adds then both subs. Fix: introduce one explicit local PER OPERAND, declared in the asm's load order, assigned before any use: `int x=zone->x; int width=zone->width; int y=zone->y; int height=zone->height; int right=x+width-1; int bottom=y+height-1;`. The upfront assignments make the scheduler emit the 4 loads consecutively (decl order = load order x,width,y,height) and the operand-reuse registers fall out exactly (x=r5, right=r3 reusing width's reg, y=r4, bottom=r2 reusing height's reg). Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: identical instructions/branches, only load positions + 2 cmp operand regs differ. Example: overlay_01_021FB368 ov01_021FB368 (static rect-contains helper).

patterns.title: Chained field assignment stores RIGHT-first; add a local to stop a struct-store alias reload
patterns.body: Two related store/CSE tricks seen in overlay_01_021FCD2C ov01_021FCD2C. (1) STORE ORDER of a chained assignment a = b = expr: MWCC evaluates expr once, assigns to the RIGHTMOST target first, then propagates left. So `work->unk10 = work->unk20 = X;` stores unk20 THEN unk10. If the asm stores the lower offset first (str r0,[r4,#0x10] then str r0,[r4,#0x20]), you must write the chain the other way: `work->unk20 = work->unk10 = X;` (rightmost = unk10 stored first, then unk20). Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: two adjacent str of the same reg with swapped offsets. (2) ALIAS RELOAD: `work->ptrField = obj->field; ... f(obj->field);` made MWCC RELOAD obj->field for the call because the intervening store to work->ptrField may alias obj->field (it cannot prove work != obj) -> an extra ldr (SIZE +2). The asm loaded obj->field ONCE into a reg, stored it, and reused that reg for the call. Fix: hoist into an explicit local: `Camera *camera = obj->field; work->ptrField = camera; f(camera);` -> single load, register reused, no reload. The local lives in a caller-saved reg (dies after the call) so it adds no push.

patterns.title: Stack-slot OFFSET assignment is reverse declaration order (first-declared = highest sp+offset)
patterns.body: Distinct from register-allocation decl-order tricks: when a function has MULTIPLE stack-resident locals (arrays or structs that must live at sp+offset, i.e. their address is taken or they're too big for a reg), MWCC -O4,p assigns the stack SLOTS in REVERSE declaration order — the FIRST-declared local gets the HIGHEST sp offset, the LAST-declared gets the lowest. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: same instructions but `add rN, sp, #X` / `str rN, [sp,#X]` offsets are permuted between two equal-size stack locals. Fix: reorder the C declarations so the wanted layout falls out. Examples from unk_0201F990: (a) sub_0201F990 needed `s16 box[6]; VecFx32 trans; VecFx32 scale;` in that order to get scale@sp+0x10, trans@sp+0x1c, box@sp+0x28 (box first-declared -> highest). (b) sub_0201FAC8 needed `int result; u32 polyAttr; u32 begin;` to get result@sp+8 (highest), polyAttr@sp+4, begin@sp+0. Scalars that stay in registers (pointers, ints used immediately) do NOT participate — only the spilled/addressed locals do. Related but separate from [[decl-order-regalloc]] and [[regalloc-order]] which govern which REGISTER, not which stack offset.

patterns.title: Reassign a dead parameter in-place to reuse its register and steer which local spills
patterns.body: When several values must survive a sequence of calls and there are more survivors than callee-saved registers, MWCC -O4,p must spill some. If objdiff shows the SAME instructions but a DIFFERENT value spilled (e.g. asm computes `subs r5,r6,r5` keeping structSize in extraSize's register and spills tableSize, while your C spills structSize and keeps tableSize in a reg -> a ~2-byte size delta), steer the allocator by REUSING a now-dead parameter's storage: write `extraSize = heapSize - extraSize;` instead of introducing a fresh `u32 structSize = heapSize - extraSize;`. The in-place reassignment makes MWCC reuse extraSize's callee-saved register for the new value (matching the asm's in-place `subs`), freeing the allocator to spill the other competing long-lived local instead. Seen in overlay_01_021FC4C4 ov01_021FC4C4 ctor. Related to [[decl-order-regalloc]] but the lever here is operand identity (reuse vs new variable), not declaration order.

patterns.title: Local frozen extern when a callee's header narrowed its params (int->u16) after this caller was matched
patterns.body: Split-header discipline applies to CALLEE prototypes too, not just shared struct headers. If a function was originally compiled with a wider arg type for a callee (e.g. int) and the callee's header was LATER refined to a narrow type (u16/u8/s16), including that refined header makes MWCC emit an integer-narrowing the original asm lacks: a u32/int value passed to a u16 param gets a `lsls rN,#16; lsrs rN,#16` (zero-extend) or `lsls;asrs` (sign) truncation at the call site. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: extra lsl/lsr #16 pairs around a bl that the asm doesn't have. Fix: do NOT include the refined header; declare a local `extern <ret> Fn(... int a2, int a3 ...);` with the wider (matched) arg types so no narrowing is emitted. Only works if the refined header is not force-included (grep its includers first; global.h chain must not pull it). Seen in unk_02097BE0 calling LegendaryCinematic_LaunchApp (launch_application.h has u16 a2/a3; matched int). Contrast [[frozen-prototype-header-split]] (struct/decl header) — same principle, applied to an imported function signature. NB: MWCC DOES narrow u32->u16 for outgoing args (confirmed: unk_020551B8 Sound_SetSceneAndPlayBGM seqNo), so a missing truncation in asm means the param was wider at match time.

patterns.title: objdiff.py misreports SIZE/section for functions with inline Thumb jump-table data
patterns.body: MWCC emits Thumb switch dispatch as `add r0,r0; add r0,pc; ldrh r0,[r0,#6]; lsl;asr; add pc,r0` followed by inline .short/.word offset-table data embedded in .text. objdiff.py's function-boundary/size heuristic can't tell this inline data from code, so it reports a spurious `SIZE N vs M` (often +8) for such functions and a small nonzero section-size delta — even when the bytes are IDENTICAL. The asm side disassembles the table as `.short`/`.word` (it has the source directives) while the C .o side shows the same bytes as bogus instructions (e.g. `movs r0,r1` = 0x0008). Verify with --disasm: if the instruction stream AND the table halfwords match (only bl relocs differ: asm fff7/feff vs c 00f0/00f8), the function matches. ALWAYS confirm with `chiri pkg -- compare` (authoritative) rather than trusting objdiff SIZE for jump-table functions. Seen in unk_02097BE0 (sub_02097BE0 5-case, sub_02097C50 4-case).

patterns.title: Cast index to (u32) in a GF_ASSERT range check to get the asm's unsigned (bcc/blo) compare
patterns.body: Range-check asserts like `GF_ASSERT(idx < N)` (e.g. before a table lookup) compile to a SIGNED compare (cmp; blt/bge) when idx is `int`, but MWCC's array-bounds idiom in the retail code uses an UNSIGNED compare (cmp rN,#N; bcc/blo). objdiff shows a single conditional-branch opcode diff: asm `bcc/blo` (0xd3.. / unsigned-lower) vs C `blt` (0xdb.. / signed-less). Fix: cast the index to unsigned in the assert -> `GF_ASSERT((u32)idx < N);` -> emits cmp; bcc. The table index access itself (table[idx]) is unaffected by the cast. Seen across the lookup fns of unk_02077678 (sub_02077678/0207769C/02077800/02077818). Header may force the param to stay `int`, so cast at the comparison rather than changing the param type.

patterns.title: Packed lookup tables (VALUE | (code<<N)) are bitfield structs; access via members emits the asm's shift extraction
patterns.body: A rodata table whose entries are `KEY | (CODE << N)` (e.g. `SPECIES_X | (22<<10)`) and whose readers extract fields with SHIFT PAIRS (`lsl #(32-N); lsr #(32-N)` for the low field; `lsl #16; lsr #(16+N)` style for the high field) is, in the original source, an array of a BITFIELD struct: `typedef struct { u16 key : N; u16 code : (16-N); } E;` with initializers `{ KEY, CODE }`. Accessing `tbl[i].key` / `tbl[i].code` makes MWCC emit the exact shift-pair extraction. Writing it as `static const u16 tbl[]` + `(tbl[i] & MASK)` / `(tbl[i] >> N)` instead emits AND-with-a-loaded-mask-register and asr — which (a) differ instruction-for-instruction and (b) consume an extra register for the mask, forcing a callee-saved reg + push/pop (function SIZE grows). Seen in unk_020517A4 (_020FC3B4 species table, _020FC3CA trainerclass table; both `{u16 id:10; u16 param:6}`). Diagnose: objdiff shows asr/and+mask vs lsl/lsr pairs, often with a spurious push {..} the asm lacks.

patterns.title: Shared store + return as the function fall-off block: hoist value to a temp and store AFTER the switch
patterns.body: When several switch cases each compute a new value, store it to a struct field, and return the same code, MWCC in the retail build often emits ONE shared store+return block as the function LAST/fall-off block (both if/else arms `b` to it), with the cold `default: return 1;` laid out immediately BEFORE it. Three wrong C shapes: (1) store+return inside each case duplicates the store; (2) `break` with the store still in the case body splits the store into its own block plus an extra `b`; (3) `return 0` inside the last case makes MWCC place the cold default block AFTER the return-0 block (wrong order). RIGHT shape: hoist the value to a function-scope temp (`int newState;`), assign it in each arm, then `break`; do the shared store (`st->field = newState;`) and `return 0;` AFTER the switch as the trailing statements. MWCC then merges them into a single fall-off block (`strb; movs r0,#0; add sp; pop`) reached by branches, and places the cold `default: return 1` just before it. Note: `add sp,#N` lands at the END of the last/fall-off block but at the START of a non-last branched return block. Seen in overlay_80_02239BF0.c (ov80_02239C80 state-machine tail). Diagnose: function body matches byte-for-byte except the last ~14 bytes; objdiff shows a SIZE mismatch (inline-jumptable miscount masks it) — disassemble both .o with arm-none-eabi-objdump and compare the tail block order + add-sp placement.

patterns.title: Header declares a narrower return type than the field (u8 vs u32) -> MWCC masks; if asm does not mask, the real return type is the wider one — use split-header
patterns.body: Symptom: a getter that just does `ldr r0,[p,#off]; bx lr` (no lsl/lsr/and mask) but the existing/public header declares it returning u8 (or u16). With that header, MWCC appends a truncation (`lsls r0,#24; lsrs r0,#24`) and the function is 4 bytes too big (objdiff SIZE 10 vs 14). The asm proves the real return type is u32/int (the value is returned full-width; any narrowing is the CALLERs job). Fix WITHOUT editing the shared header (it is frozen at the matching-time state its callers were built against — changing the return type would alter caller codegen and break their match / cascade via IPA): do NOT include that public header in the defining .c. Instead include the underlying data/struct header (here friend_group.h) and forward-declare the affected functions LOCALLY with the correct (wider) return type. Different TUs may legitimately see different return-type declarations for the same symbol in a matching decomp — the linker only matches by name. Seen in unk_0202C730.c: Save_FriendGroup_GetGroupId declared u8 in unk_0202C730.h (5 matched callers) but defined u32 locally to drop the mask. Verified: full ROM SHA1 still passes, callers unaffected.

patterns.title: x >> n on a u8/u16 emits asr (signed); retail lsr means the operand is u32/unsigned
patterns.body: A right shift `x >> n` where x is u8 or u16 promotes x to signed int per C integer promotion, so MWCC emits an arithmetic shift (asr). If the asm shows a logical/unsigned shift (lsr) at that spot, the original operand was an unsigned type that does NOT promote to signed — i.e. u32 (or unsigned int). Fix: declare/cast the operand as u32 (e.g. change a derived param type from u8 to u32, or write ((u32)x >> n)). Left shifts (<<) are unaffected (lsl either way). Seen in unk_0205BFF0.c sub_0205C0A0: `b >> 1` with b as u8 emitted `asr r0,r1,#1` (0x1048); retail had `lsr r0,r1,#1` (0x0848); changing b to u32 fixed it. Note u16 also promotes to signed int, so u16 does NOT give lsr — only u32/unsigned does.

patterns.title: When chiri compare fails but objdiff shows only jump-table SIZE mismatches, diff main.sbin built both ways
patterns.body: For files full of inline-jump-table functions, objdiff reports SIZE mismatches for every function (it miscounts the inline .short tables) and refuses byte-level diffs, hiding any real 1-byte error. To pinpoint: build main with the C version (chiri pkg -- build --target main --no-compare) and `cp build/heartgold.us/main.sbin /tmp/main_c.sbin`; flip main.lsf back to the asm object, rebuild, `cp ... /tmp/main_asm.sbin`; then `cmp -l /tmp/main_asm.sbin /tmp/main_c.sbin` (asm baseline matches retail). cmp -l prints offsets+values in OCTAL and is 1-based. Convert: address = 0x02000000 + (byteno-1). `xxd -s <off> -l 48` both sbins to see context, then map to the function via the asm listing. This isolates a single differing byte (e.g. an asr-vs-lsr opcode) that objdiff masked. Used to find the lsr/asr bug in unk_0205BFF0 sub_0205C0A0.

patterns.title: Don't cache base->ptr in a local when the asm RELOADS it across calls (inverse of hoist-size-local)
patterns.body: Counterpart to [[hoist-size-local-callee-saved]]. When a function holds a base pointer (e.g. fieldSystem in r4) and repeatedly dereferences base->ptr->field across several bl calls, MWCC RELOADS base->ptr after each call because a call may invalidate that memory (it can't prove base->ptr is unchanged). The original source therefore accessed base->ptr->field INLINE each time. Introducing a readability local `T *p = base->ptr;` breaks the match: a local is NOT invalidated by calls, so MWCC keeps it live in a CALLEE-SAVED register across the whole function, which (a) consumes an extra callee-saved reg and (b) WIDENS the push/pop (e.g. asm `push {r4,lr}` becomes C `push {r3,r4,r5,lr}`) — and the base pointer it displaces gets its own reg too. Diagnose via objdiff: many 'real byte diffs' that are actually just the wider push/pop + shifted reg numbers, and a SIZE delta of a few bytes. Fix: delete the local, write base->ptr->field inline at every use; CSE still collapses multiple derefs WITHIN a call-free span into one load (matching the asm's per-region single reload). Seen in overlay_01_021F3D38.c (ov01_021F3E10, ov01_021F3E4C: fieldSystem->unk68 reloaded 2-3x across BgSetPos/sub_0205B63C/sub_0205B6A0 calls). Contrast: cache the pointer in a local ONLY when the asm keeps it in a callee-saved reg across calls (D98 in the same file DOES cache fieldSystem->unk68 because fieldSystem itself is dead after the first load).

patterns.title: A flags/bitmask param compared by magnitude with signed blt/bge is int, not u32
patterns.body: A parameter you'd instinctively type `u32` because it is used as a bitmask (`flags & (1<<n)`, `tst`) may actually be a signed `int` if the asm ALSO does a magnitude comparison on it with a SIGNED branch. Symptom: `if (flags >= (1<<N))` emitted as `cmp rX, #imm; blo/bcc` (unsigned) in your C, but the target asm uses `cmp rX, #imm; blt` (signed) at that gate. The bitwise tests (`tst`) are sign-agnostic, so they give no clue — only the magnitude compare reveals the signedness. Fix: declare the param `int` (or s32). The `&`/`tst` codegen is unchanged; only the `>=`/`<` flips from unsigned `blo/bhs` to signed `blt/bge`. This is the INVERSE of [[cast-unsigned-for-branch]] (which adds a (u32) cast to a signed param to FORCE unsigned branches) and [[u16-from-ldrh-unsigned-branch]]. Seen in overlay_01_021EA8E0.c ov01_021EA910 (the `flags >= 0x1000` gate before NNS_G3dGlbPolygonAttr): u32 flags emitted bcc, int flags emitted the matching blt.

patterns.title: A down-counting loop with subs;bne needs an UNSIGNED counter (signed int -> hoisted decrement + cmp;bgt)
patterns.body: A fixed-count copy/fill loop whose asm is `movs rN,#K; .L: <body>; subs rN,#1; bne .L` (decrement LAST, branch-if-nonzero) must use an UNSIGNED counter in C. Writing `int i = K; do { body } while (--i);` does NOT match: MWCC -O4,p proves a signed `i` stays >= 0 (range analysis), converts the `!=0` test to a signed `> 0`, and HOISTS the `subs` up into the body — which then forces a separate `cmp rN,#0; bgt` at the bottom (the intervening pointer `adds` clobber the Z flag). Result: function is 2 bytes too big (objdiff SIZE +2). FIX: make the counter `u32` (or any unsigned): `u32 i = K; do { body } while (--i);`. Unsigned forbids the signed `bgt` form, so MWCC keeps the decrement at the bottom and emits `subs;bne` reusing the Z flag. Also: declare the source/walker pointers in the SAME order the asm sets them up (e.g. `p=src` before `dst=base+off` if asm does `adds rSrc` then `adds rDst`) — decl order drives the two setup `adds` order. Seen in frontier_system.c ov80_0222AAD8/AAF8 (8x u16 copy of FrontierSystemWork+0x24).

patterns.title: Force a dedicated `sub sp` frame slot by making a small discarded-read local >4 bytes
patterns.body: When a function reads a value into a stack local that is then discarded, and the asm reserves a DEDICATED frame slot for it (prologue is `push {r3,...}` for 8-byte alignment AND a separate `sub sp,#8`, with the local accessed at `sp+0`), a scalar or any <=4-byte local does NOT match: MWCC -O4,p coalesces an address-taken local of <=4 bytes into the spare 4-byte alignment-push slot (the dummy r3 in `push {r3,r4,r5,lr}`), emitting NO `sub sp`. The function comes out 4 bytes too small (objdiff SIZE -4; prologue missing `sub sp,#N`; the rest of the body is byte-identical modulo bl placeholders). Even a 4-byte array (`u8 buf[4]`) still coalesces. FIX: declare the local LARGER than 4 bytes so it cannot fit the push slot, forcing `sub sp,#8` with the local at sp+0 — e.g. `u32 magic[2];` and read into it `NARC_ReadFile(narc, 4, magic);` (keep the read SIZE operand a literal so it is unchanged; do not use sizeof which would change #4 to #8). Seen in overlay_01_021FB04C ov01_021FB04C (discarded 4-byte NARC archive-header magic before six 2-byte count reads). Related to [[stack-slot-reverse-decl-order]] (which governs ordering of multiple stack slots) but the lever here is the local's SIZE forcing a slot to exist at all.

patterns.title: Own-header-first + non-self-sufficient frozen header: make the .c self-contained
patterns.body: clang-format sorts a .c file's OWN header (matching basename, e.g. text_0205B4EC.h for src/text_0205B4EC.c) to the very top, before all other includes. If that frozen shared header is NOT self-sufficient — it uses a type it doesn't include (e.g. text_0205B4EC.h declares a fn taking FontID but only includes bg_window.h/options.h/pm_string.h, not font_types_def.h) — then including it first leaves that type undefined and MWCC mis-parses the declaration ('illegal function definition' + 'identifier redeclared' with a truncated signature + cascading 'illegal access to local variable from other function'). Other files that include the header compile only because, for THEM, it's not the main header so it sorts alphabetically AFTER something that pulls the type in (e.g. font.h). You hit this on the FIRST file decompiled from that module. Fixes: (a) add the missing include to the shared header — usually IPA-safe since every existing includer must already have the type before it, so it's a guard no-op — but it still edits a frozen header; (b) PREFERRED: make the new .c self-contained — do NOT include the shared header at all, instead write local prototypes for every function the file defines (matching the header's frozen signatures exactly for the exported ones, plus any .public fns missing from the header), and include the concrete headers that provide the called fns/types. Zero risk to other TUs; the shared header stays untouched for its callers. Example: src/text_0205B4EC.c (FontID via text_0205B4EC.h). Related: [[enum-casts]], [[frozen-struct-header-split]].

patterns.title: Frozen struct field is s16 but asm reads ldrh: cast (u16)field
patterns.body: When a frozen shared struct declares a field as s16 (e.g. COORD_EVENT.x/.z in map_events_internal.h) but the target asm reads it with ldrh (unsigned, zero-extend) rather than ldrsh, don't change the shared struct (IPA risk + may be right for other files). Instead write (u16)event->field at the read site: MWCC emits a single ldrh for (u16)(s16 lvalue) (low halfword, zero-extended), matching. Plain event->field on an s16 emits ldrsh. Diagnose: objdiff/disasm shows ldrsh where retail has ldrh, often with a following sign/zero-extend mismatch. Example: src/unk_0203DB6C.c sub_0203DE04 comparing player coords (int, from u32 getters) against COORD_EVENT x/z+w/h. Note signed-vs-unsigned of the OTHER operand still controls blt vs blo: here player coords held as int and (u16)field promotes to positive int, so cmp + blt (signed). Related: [[enum-casts]].

patterns.title: In a clamp/limit if-else, the NON-clamping (pass-through) arm is the if-true (fall-through) block
patterns.body: A frame-advance / clamp helper with shape `if (cond) { x = limit; flag = 1; } else { x += step; }` can match the BODY byte-for-byte yet lay the two arms out in the wrong order. The asm reveals which arm falls through: e.g. `adds r1,r3,r1; cmp r1,r4; bge CLAMP; str r1 (x+=step); b END; CLAMP: str r4 (=limit); movs r2,#1`. Here the branch (`bge`/`bmi`) targets the CLAMP block and the pass-through `str r1` is the FALL-THROUGH — so the source wrote the pass-through case as the IF-TRUE block: `if (x+step < limit) { x += step; } else { x = limit; flag = 1; }` (positive dir) and `if (x+step >= 0) { x += step; } else { x = 0; flag = 1; }` (negative dir). Writing it the intuitive way (`if (x+step >= limit) { clamp }`) inverts the polarity: MWCC emits `blt ELSE` with the clamp as fall-through — same total size but a 2-byte-shorter function and swapped bcc/blt opcodes (objdiff: N real byte diffs, function -2 bytes, but `0` flag-store reuse via movs still works). Fix: negate the condition so the asm fall-through arm is your `if` body. Seen in unk_02018000 sub_0201815C. Related: [[branch-or-vs-and]], [[gf-assert-direction]] (all about branch polarity / which path is laid out first).

patterns.title: Trailing .balign 4,0 in asm inflates per-function symbol size by 2 vs MWCC; benign section -2N delta
patterns.body: Hand-written asm functions that end on a 2-byte (Thumb) boundary often carry a trailing `.balign 4, 0` before `thumb_func_end`, which the assembler folds INTO the function symbol (size rounded up +2, padding zeros counted as part of the function). MWCC does NOT pad the tail of a function; it 4-byte-aligns the NEXT function instead, so the same 2 bytes of zero padding exist between functions but are attributed OUTSIDE the symbol. Result: objdiff reports each such function as MATCH (body bytes identical) yet shows the function 2 bytes shorter in C, and a `.text` section delta of -2 per affected function (e.g. unk_02018000: 7 functions x -2 = -0xe). This is a layout-attribution artifact, NOT a real diff: the linker word-aligns each function so the final linked .text is byte-identical. ALWAYS confirm with `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) — it passed for unk_02018000 despite the -14 objdiff section delta. Diagnose: arm-none-eabi-objdump -t both .o; the asm functions with -2 are exactly the ones whose asm source has a trailing `.balign 4, 0`. Distinct from [[objdiff-size-miscount-inline-jumptable]] (which is inline jump-table data miscounted as code).

patterns.title: MI_CpuFill32/inline wrappers that REORDER args can cache a simple-load arg across a call arg — extract the call to a temp
patterns.body: MI_CpuFill32(dest, data, size) is a static inline that forwards to MIi_CpuClear32(data, dest, size) — it SWAPS the first two args so `data` becomes arg0. When you call MI_CpuFill32(callResult(...), self->field, N) with dest being a CALL and data a simple field load, MWCC evaluates arg0 (=data, the field) FIRST and must keep it live across the dest call → it lands in a callee-saved reg, widening push {..} and adding instructions (objdiff: function a few bytes too big, extra pushed reg). The asm computed the call first, then loaded the fill value after. Fix: hoist the call into its own statement so it is sequenced before the field load: `void *p = callResult(...); MI_CpuFill32(p, self->field, N);`. Now neither survives a call → both caller-saved, push narrows to match. Note: plain memset(callResult, val, N) does NOT hit this (memset is a real extern, args eval left-to-right so the call/dest is arg0 and evaluated first). Only inline wrappers that permute arg order trigger it. Seen in unk_02014A08 sub_02014C08 (MI_CpuFill32 of sub_02014A4C result). Related: [[no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls]], [[hoist-size-local-callee-saved]].

patterns.title: A u8/u16 loop counter narrows on ++ and may force an unsigned branch; use int when the asm increments full-width with a signed/range compare
patterns.body: A loop counter typed u8 or u16 makes MWCC (1) NARROW it on each increment (`adds rN,#1; lsls#24/#16; lsrs#24/#16` for u8/u16 — 2 extra bytes per loop), and (2) pick an UNSIGNED branch for its bound test. If the target asm increments the counter full-width (`adds rN,rN,#1` with no narrowing) AND/OR compares it with a SIGNED branch (cmp; bgt/ble), the counter was `int` (or s32). Switching the counter to `int` drops the narrowing and makes `counter <= someU8Field` a signed compare (the u8 field promotes to int; the int counter keeps it signed). Conversely, if the asm shows an UNSIGNED bound branch (bcc/bls) with NO narrowing on the counter, use `u32` (a u16 field on the other side promotes to u32, unsigned compare, and u32++ does not narrow). Seen in unk_02014A08: sub_02014C60 loop index needed u32 (unsigned bcc bound, no narrow); sub_02014CBC scanline counter needed int (signed bgt/ble vs u8 start/end fields, full-width ++). Diagnose: objdiff SIZE +2 per loop from the lsls/lsrs narrow, plus a blt<->bcc or bgt<->bhi opcode swap. Related: [[downcount-copy-loop-needs-unsigned-counter-for-subs-bne]], [[param-narrowing]].

patterns.title: NONMATCHING inline asm: declare compiler-runtime callees as extern, and use explicit [rN, #0] (bracket-only assembles wrong)
patterns.body: Two mwasmarm gotchas when transcribing a function to MWCC inline asm (`static asm void f(...) { ... }`) for a NONMATCHING fallback: (1) `bl _s32_div_f` (or any compiler-runtime/IPA helper: _s32_div_f, _ll_mul, _u32_div_f, etc.) fails to assemble with `undefined label`. Fix: add a C prototype before the function so the symbol is known to the linker — e.g. `extern int _s32_div_f(int numer, int denom);`. Named callees that are already declared (your own sub_*, SDK fns) work directly. (2) Bracket-only load/store addressing assembles with a WRONG offset: `ldr r2, [r5]` came out as `ldr r2, [r5, #8]` (one stray instruction, objdiff 1 real byte diff at that halfword). Always write the explicit zero offset: `ldr r2, [r5, #0]`. (Curiously `strh r0, [r4]` assembled fine as [r4,#0] in the same function, so it is inconsistent — just always write #0.) Literal loads: use `ldr rN, =0xVALUE`; mwasmarm auto-dumps the pool at function end in first-use order with dedup (matched the retail pool 0x798/0x78c/0x60c/0x78d exactly). bl placeholders match the original asm .o byte-for-byte (both assembled by mwasmarm), so objdiff shows them as benign BL-reloc diffs, not real diffs. Wrap the body in // clang-format off/on and gate the readable C under #ifdef NONMATCHING. Seen in unk_02014A08 sub_02014CBC. Related: [[nonmatching-inline-asm-syntax]].

patterns.title: MWCC fills a load-use delay slot with an independent extraction; retail does not — same instrs, reordered, often unmatchable from C
patterns.body: After a load (e.g. `ldrsh sine`), MWCC -O4,p schedules an INDEPENDENT ready instruction into the 1-cycle load-use delay slot to avoid a stall — typically a halfword extraction from a still-live value (e.g. `lsrs hi, v, #16`). The retail build sometimes does NOT do this fill (it issues the dependent op immediately, accepting the stall). The two builds then have IDENTICAL instructions in a DIFFERENT order (objdiff: same SIZE, N real byte diffs that are all reordered shifts/extractions, no opcode changes). This ordering is the scheduler reacting to the IR shape; it resists C-level control. Tried (unk_02014A08 sub_02014CBC, packing `(hi<<16)|(u16)newLow` where hi=(u16)(v>>16)): inline vs separate temp, `u16 hi` vs inline cast, `(v>>16)<<16` (becomes AND-mask + literal), in-place `v>>=16;v<<=16` (folds to AND-mask), and OR-operand swap. The operand swap `(u16)newLow | ((u16)(v>>16)<<16)` got CLOSEST (20->9 diffs) but never to 0 — MWCC kept slotting the hi-extract before newLow. When a same-size all-reordered-instruction diff survives ~4-5 expression rewrites, stop and NONMATCHING (the asm transcribes cleanly: 18/19 other fns stayed clean C). Related: [[redundant-double-zero-load-coalesce-wall]], [[nonmatching-inline-asm-mwasmarm-gotchas]].

patterns.title: Bitfield extract for a switch/index: (v & (k<<n)) >> n emits mask-first (mov;lsl;and;lsr); (v >> n) & k emits shift-first — match the asm form
patterns.body: Extracting a sub-field `(v >> n) & mask` has two equivalent codegen shapes MWCC picks based on source SYNTAX, not value: (1) `(v >> n) & k` -> shift-first: `lsrs rA, v, #n; movs rB, #k; ands rA, rB` (3 insns). (2) `(v & (k << n)) >> n` -> mask-first: `movs rB, #k; lsls rB, #n; ands rB, v; lsrs rB, #n` (4 insns; builds the shifted mask via mov+lsl rather than a literal-pool load when k<<n is a shifted small constant). If the asm shows the 4-insn mask-first form (common for a switch discriminant or a packed-field read), write the masked form `(v & 0xMASK) >> n` with the literal mask spelled out (e.g. `(v & 0x1C000000) >> 26` for bits 26-28). Writing `(v >> 26) & 7` gives the shorter shift-first form and a byte mismatch. MWCC builds the mask 0x1C000000 = 7<<26 as `movs #7; lsls #26` (no pool word). Seen in unk_0202068C sub_0202094C (texture-format switch on bits 26-28). The width/height field reads in the same function used the SAME masked form `(v & 0x700000) >> 20`. Related: [[bitfield-lsls-lsrs]], [[packed-lookup-table-is-bitfield-struct]].

patterns.title: An init loop that fills count items should bound on the STORED field (obj->count), not the param — the field reloads each iter and frees the param register
patterns.body: A constructor that stores a count then loops to init each slot — `obj->count = count; for (i = 0; i < ???; i++) init(&obj->items[i]);` — must use `obj->count` (the stored field) as the loop bound, NOT the `count` parameter. The asm reloads `obj->count` from memory every iteration (because the init() call may invalidate it) and REUSES the count parameter register for the walking byte-offset, so only 3 callee-saved regs are needed (push {r4,r5,r6,lr}). Writing `i < count` (the param) keeps the param live in a callee-saved register across the whole loop, needing a 4th callee-saved reg -> wider push (push {r3,r4,r5,r6,r7,lr}) and a 2-byte size delta. Fix: bound on `obj->count`. Diagnose: objdiff SIZE -2 with a wider push and an extra adds r5,r6,#0-style reg copy. Seen in unk_0202068C sub_0202068C (vs its sibling sub_02020740 which already looped on manager->count and matched). Related: [[no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls]].

patterns.title: A by-value small-struct param whose address is taken forces `push {r0-r3}` arg-homing; pass the fields as scalars + a coalesced local struct to avoid it
patterns.body: When a function takes a small (<=16-byte) struct BY VALUE in arg registers and then takes its ADDRESS (e.g. passes &param to a helper), MWCC homes ALL incoming arg registers with a leading `push {r0,r1,r2,r3}` plus a matching heavy epilogue at every return (`pop {r4,r5,r6,r7}; pop {r3}; add sp,#16; bx r3`), inflating the function by 16+ bytes and shifting every stack offset. The retail build avoids this: it passes the struct's COMPONENTS as separate scalar params and declares a LOCAL struct that MWCC COALESCES onto the scalar params' spill slots (so the only stores are the normal arg spills, e.g. `str r2,[sp,#0x30]; str r3,[sp,#0x34]`), then takes the address of that local. No push {r0-r3} appears because the addressed object is a genuine local, not a register param. Fix: change `f(.., MeshPoint query, ..)` to `f(.., fx32 x, fx32 z, ..)` + `MeshPoint query; query.x = x; query.y = z;` and pass `&query`; use `query.x`/`query.y` (not x/z) at later use sites so they reload from the coalesced slot across calls. Diagnose via objdiff: prologue `push {r0,r1,r2,r3}` + sub sp smaller by 0x10, and the multi-instruction `pop;pop;add sp;bx r3` epilogue at each return. Seen in overlay_01_021FAD1C ov01_021FAE50 (the (x,z) query point). Related: [[stack-slot-reverse-decl-order]].

patterns.title: A local struct zeroed then passed by address: use aggregate-init `T x = {0,...}` (base-register stores reused for the call), not field-by-field assignment (sp-direct stores)
patterns.body: When a function zeroes a small stack struct (e.g. VecFx32) and immediately passes its address to a callee, the retail build computes the struct address ONCE into a register (`add r1,sp,#off`), stores the zeros THROUGH that register (`str r0,[r1]; str r0,[r1,#4]; str r0,[r1,#8]`), and reuses r1 as the call's pointer arg. Writing the zero-init field-by-field (`v.x=0; v.y=0; v.z=0;`) — or even via an explicit `T *p=&v; p->x=0;...` (MWCC folds p back to the constant address) — instead emits sp-DIRECT stores (`str r0,[sp,#off]`) plus a separate `add` for the call arg. Same byte SIZE (it's a scheduling tie) but different bytes. FIX: use an aggregate initializer `VecFx32 zero = {0, 0, 0};` then `f(work, &zero);`. MWCC lowers the whole-object initializer as base-register stores and keeps the address live for the call, matching. Seen in unk_020689C8 sub_02068A08 (the else branch that supplies a zero position to sub_02068DA8). Related: [[chained-assign-store-order-and-alias-reload]].

patterns.title: When a frozen shared header declares cluster-partner fns with PLACEHOLDER return/param types, a client accessing fields beyond those types must declare them locally (don't include the header)
patterns.body: A shared header (e.g. overlay_01_021F1348.h) sometimes declares a still-asm module's exported functions with PLACEHOLDER types that are link-correct but structurally wrong for some callers — e.g. `TaskManager *ov01_021F1468(FieldSystem*)` where the real returned struct is larger and a new client reads `ret->field@0x24` (out of bounds for TaskManager). The existing matched callers only touch the declared fields, so the placeholder works for them and the header is frozen. A NEW client that needs the extra fields canNOT include that header (the placeholder types won't compile the field access, and editing the header IPA-cascades the other callers). Fix (extends [[frozen-prototype-header-split]] / [[frozen-callee-proto-for-narrowed-args]]): do NOT include the shared header; declare the needed cluster-partner functions LOCALLY in the .c with your own accurate struct types (all pointer/int args → identical call ABI, so codegen matches), and define the structs you need locally. The linker resolves by name. Also applies to same-module accessors split across headers (e.g. sub_02068D74/D90/DA8 not in unk_020689C8.h → declare locally). Seen in overlay_01_02203E40.c (a 3D-model-on-mapobject effect): local decls for ov01_021F1430/146C/1468/1450/1620/1448/1AB8 + sub_02068D74/90/98/DA8/DB8 + VEC_MultAdd/VEC_Distance, custom UnkOv01_02203E40 object (NNSG3dRenderObj@0x4, f32 scale@0x64) and a renderer struct with Camera*@0x24. Verified full ROM SHA1 (existing header callers untouched).

patterns.title: For small (u8) array loops, use the real struct-array field / a typed pointer so MWCC keeps [base, index] addressing; a raw ((u8*)p)[i] cast plus a separate loaded temp can trigger pointer strength-reduction
patterns.body: In a `for (i=0;i<N;i++)` loop over u8 arrays where element size is 1, indexed addressing `ldrb rD,[base,i]` is already optimal (no scaling), so the matching codegen keeps the base pointers loop-invariant and reuses the counter `i` as the index. Writing the body as `((u8*)a2)[i]` together with a separate `u8 v = ((u8*)a2)[i];` temp pushed MWCC sp2p2 onto its induction-variable / strength-reduction path: it introduced two extra `adds rBase,#1` per iteration (walking pointers) AND flipped the `cmp` operand order — +4 bytes, no match. Fix: access through the actual struct array field (`ribbons->ribbons[i]`) and a typed local pointer (`u8 *src = a2;`), and compare directly (`ribbons->ribbons[i] != src[i]`) with no intermediate temp. That restored `ldrb r1,[r5,r2]` / `ldrb r0,[r4,r2]` / `cmp r0,r1` / `strb r1,[r4,r2]`. Lesson: prefer genuine array-subscript expressions over raw-cast subscripts + hoisted temps when you need indexed addressing to survive. (unk_0208F658.s sub_0208F74C)

patterns.title: sub_0203410C command-table registrar files (e.g. unk_02091564.c, unk_0208F658.c): a .rodata table of {handler, sizeGetter, recordGetter} triples registered by a tail-call to sub_0203410C(&table, NELEMS, arg)
patterns.body: A recurring module shape: an exported registrar `void reg(void *arg){ sub_0203410C(&sTable, NELEMS(sTable), arg); }` that TAIL-CALLs sub_0203410C (loads addr, `bx r3`, since the callee is far). The .rodata `sTable[]` is N triples; columns are func1 = `void handler(int a0, int a1, void *a2, ctx *a3)` (dispatched by sub_02034170 with a3 = (*globalCtx)->field8 or NULL), func2 = `u32 sizeGetter(void)` (commonly sub_020342C4/020342C0 returning 0xFFFF/0), func3 = `void *recordGetter(int idx, ctx *a3)` or NULL. In the handlers, `a0` is a link/player id compared against `sub_0203769C()` for an early return; `a3->0xc` is a `SaveData*`, `a3->0x88` is a per-category mixing buffer (set by a sibling setter that does `*(void**)((u8*)a3+0x88)=buf`). Define a file-local struct typedef for the table (exact func-ptr types) instead of reusing UnkStruct_02091564 to avoid func3 return-type (void* vs void(*)()) warnings — rodata bytes are identical either way. Access the big buffer via raw `*(T*)((u8*)buf+off)` casts. (template: src/unk_02091564.c)

patterns.title: Data-only files in a custom abs32 section with multiple ordered symbols (e.g. .version SDK version strings) have no known matching C form under MWCC sp2p2 — keep as asm
patterns.body: asm/middleware.s is 7 NUL-terminated SDK version strings in ONE .version section (define_section VERSION ".version" abs32 RWX in <nitro/section.h>), each .balign 4, total 224 bytes, in source order. No C incantation reproduces a single ordered 4-aligned .version section: (1) bare `VERSION x[]` declspec prefix -> "declaration syntax error"; (2) `const` data IGNORES `#pragma section VERSION begin/end` and lands in the merged .rodata (correct order, packed, WRONG section); (3) NON-const data WITH the begin/end pragma reaches .version but MWCC -O4 emits each symbol as its OWN .version sub-section SORTED BY SIZE (not source order) — `__attribute__((aligned(4)))` fixes the per-object 4-byte alignment (algn 2**2) but cannot fix the order; full compare FAILs main.sbin + OVY_45.sbin. Also: objdiff.py does NOT track custom sections (it reports asm .rodata=0), so only `chiri pkg -- compare` can verify these. Verdict: defer / keep asm. Triage ranks it #1 (data-only, 36 lines) but that is a false-easy.

patterns.title: objdiff.py can falsely report a function SIZE mismatch when the function has an inline Thumb jump-table (data) region — verify byte-identity manually + via full compare
patterns.body: A Thumb switch emits an inline jump table (e.g. `.short case0..caseN` after `add pc, r1`) inside .text. objdiff delimits functions by symbol size; the asm .o marks the table with a $d data mapping symbol and may report a different symbol size than the C .o (e.g. sub_02096260 reported 176 vs 184), flagging a SIZE mismatch even though every instruction byte (and the table words 0008/0026/003c/0052/0090) is identical. The only real differences in the raw dump were the bl placeholders (fff7feff in the asm .o vs 00f000f8 in the C .o) which are unresolved relocations that link identically. Resolution: dump `arm-none-eabi-objdump -s -j .text` for both, compare non-bl bytes; then trust `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) as authoritative. (unk_020961D8.s)

patterns.title: A triage gated_by:[ipa-shared-headers] can be a FALSE POSITIVE when the shared symbols are common library IMPORTS, not exports of a mutable shared header
patterns.body: triage flags a file as gated when it shares symbols with a blocked file. But check WHICH symbols: unk_020961D8.s was gated against unk_0200FA24.s, but the only shared .public symbols were Heap_Free and IsPaletteFadeFinished — ubiquitous imports, not a shared mutable header (the real ipa-shared-headers risk is the sound.h family). Confirm with: comm -12 of the two .inc .public lists; if the overlap is just common imports (Heap_*, memcpy, MI_*, palette/fade helpers), the gate is spurious and the file is safe to do alone. Bonus tell here: include/unk_020961D8.h already existed and a matched file (scrcmd_c.c) already called it, so the header was frozen — implement the .c only.

patterns.title: When two calls use the same logical value via different access paths, match the exact source expression: `obj->ptr->field` reloads from memory; a local `T *p=...; p->field` uses the cached register
patterns.body: In sub_020961D8, EasyChat_CreateArgs(...) takes saveData as `work->fieldSystem->saveData` -> MWCC emits `ldr r2,[r4](=work->fieldSystem); ldr r2,[r2,#0xc]` (reload the pointer from the struct), while the very next Save_Misc_Get(...) takes `fieldSystem->saveData` -> `ldr r0,[r5,#0xc]` (uses the local FieldSystem* kept in r5). Both are the same pointer value, but the source expression differs and so does the codegen (extra reload vs cached reg). If a call site is 4 bytes short and the asm has an extra `ldr rN,[base]` before the field load, the source went through the struct member (obj->ptr->field), not the local variable. Pick per-call to match.

patterns.title: Match the asm return-block placement: `if(x==NULL) return A; body; return B;` emits the A-return INLINE; the asm form with the early-return at the END (beq-to-end) comes from `if(x!=NULL){ body; return B; } return A;`
patterns.body: For a guard like null-check, MWCC lays out the return blocks by source structure. `if(p==NULL){return 0;} body; return 1;` -> `cmp;bne body; movs r0,#0; pop; body...; return1` (the return-0 is inline right after the branch). The asm often instead has `cmp; beq END; body; return1; END: return0` (the failure return is a block at the very end, reached by branch). To reproduce that, invert: `if(p!=NULL){ body; return 1; } return 0;`. Same logic, but the body is the fall-through and the failure-return is last. Seen in unk_020379A0.s sub_02037C0C (u32, return 1/0) and sub_02037C44 (ptr, return entry/NULL).

patterns.title: For a 2-byte-stride pair store, use u8 arr[N][2] + arr[i][0/1] so the +1 folds into the str immediate ((base+i*2)+#1); a flat u8 arr[2N] + arr[i*2+1] can instead emit base+(i*2+1) via a register index
patterns.body: unk_020379A0.s unk00 is 8 two-byte slots. Flat `u8 unk00[0x10]` with `unk00[a0*2+1]=v` produced `adds rIdx,rRow,#1; strb [base,rIdx]` (the +1 went into the index) in sub_02037B6C, mismatching the asm `adds r0,base,rRow; strb [r0,#1]` (+1 in the store immediate). Switching to `u8 unk00[8][2]` and `unk00[a0][1]=v` makes MWCC compute the row base (base+a0*2) then use immediate #1 -> match. Subtlety: the READ in sub_02037BA0 matched with BOTH forms (same bytes), but the WRITE-with-reload context in sub_02037B6C only matched with the 2D array. When a pair/tuple store is off by the +1 placement, model the data as [N][k] not [N*k].

patterns.title: MWCC -W error rejects a non-static function definition with no prototype ("function has no prototype"); for exports kept out of a frozen header, add LOCAL prototypes in the .c
patterns.body: This build uses -W error, so every non-static (exported) function needs a visible prototype before its definition. When a file exports many functions but the shared header is frozen at a subset (only the symbols matched callers use), do NOT add the rest to the header (IPA cascade into those callers). Instead declare the extra exports as plain (non-static) prototypes at the top of the .c itself. unk_020379A0.s exports 19 fns; include/unk_020379A0.h has 6; the other 13 got local prototypes. Codegen is identical whether the prototype lives in a header or the .c, as long as the types match. Relatedly: never mark them static (they ARE exported and other asm files call them).

patterns.title: For a branchy float->fx32 conversion ((cond)?(x+0.5f):(x-0.5f) then cast), compute a `f32 tmp` in the if/else and apply ONE (fx32)tmp after the merge so _ffix is shared, not duplicated per branch
patterns.body: sub_0205BED8 converts u16 args to fx32 with rounding: `(fx32)((a!=0) ? 0.5f+(f32)(a<<12) : (f32)(a<<12)-0.5f)`. Writing the (fx32) cast inside each branch (`env->x = (fx32)(...)` in both arms) duplicates the _ffix call (and the store) -> +8 bytes. The asm instead does `_fflt`/`_fadd` or `_fsub` per branch, then a SINGLE `_ffix` at the merge, then one store. Reproduce with a float temp: `f32 t; if(a){t=0.5f+(f32)(a<<12);}else{t=(f32)(a<<12)-0.5f;} env->x=(fx32)t;`. The (f32)(a<<12) IS duplicated per branch (matches asm) — only the trailing cast/store is shared. MWCC soft-float intrinsics: (f32)int=_fflt, +/-= _fadd/_fsub, (s32)f32=_ffix, f32*f32=_fmul; FX_Mul = FX_MulInline = ((s64)v1*v2+0x800)>>12 (= _ll_mul + shift).

patterns.title: When a count/index loop is off only by which callee-saved register holds the counter vs the bound, swap the local DECLARATION order (declare the loop index before the count)
patterns.body: Save_GetPartyLead mismatched by 7 bytes that were purely register fields: asm had count=r5,i=r4 but `u16 count=..; u16 i;` gave count=r4,i=r5. Declaring the index first (`u16 i; u16 count=Party_GetCount(..);`) flipped MWCC register assignment to match. (The near-identical Save_GetPartyLeadAlive matched as-is because its extra `mon` local shifted the allocation.) General lever: when two same-lifetime locals land in swapped registers, reorder their declarations; the names are irrelevant, the order drives MWCC callee-saved assignment.

patterns.title: A function that InitBgFromTemplate()s N backgrounds from N different static const BgTemplates uses N SEPARATE stack BgTemplate locals (struct-copy each), not one reused local
patterns.body: ov33_0225D720 copies sBgTemplate_4/5/6 (each via ldmia/stmia) into THREE distinct stack slots (sp+0x38, +0x1c, +0) and passes &each to InitBgFromTemplate — stack frame 0x54 (3*0x1c), not 0x1c. Reusing a single `BgTemplate template; template=sBgTemplate_4; Init(..&template); template=sBgTemplate_5; ...` collapses to one slot (frame 0x1c) and mismatches. Declare `BgTemplate template1, template2, template3;` (first-declared -> highest offset sp+0x38). Related landed fixes for touchscreen-menu overlays: GX_SetBankForSubBG uses GX_VRAM_SUB_BG_32_H (0x80=GX_VRAM_H) / GX_VRAM_SUB_OBJ_16_I (0x100=GX_VRAM_I) — the H/I banks, NOT 128_C/128_D (C/D=0x80? no: C=4,D=8); count-bounded window loops use `u32 i` (unmasked, bcc) when the body strength-reduces &windows[i] to a walking pointer; a u8 struct field passed straight to a u8 fn param should be declared u8 (not int) to avoid a (u8) truncation.

patterns.title: When a precondition assert path RETURNS (does not fall through to the function body), use explicit `if (assertFails) { GF_AssertFail(); return; }` — NOT GF_ASSERT(cond)
patterns.body: GF_ASSERT(expr) = ((expr) ? (void)0 : GF_AssertFail()) and GF_AssertFail is `void GF_AssertFail(void)` (NOT noreturn). So `GF_ASSERT(cond); body;` compiles to `cmp;bne L; bl GF_AssertFail; L: body` — the assert-fail path FALLS THROUGH to body. If the asm instead shows `cmp; b<skip> body; bl GF_AssertFail; pop(return); body:` (the assert path returns and body is a separate block reached only when the assert passes), the source was an explicit `if (cond==0){ GF_AssertFail(); return; } body;` (or `if(cond!=0){...}` for an inverted assert). unk_02055244.s: CallTask_LeaveOverworld/PaletteFadeUntilFinished/FadeFromBlack assert sub_0203DF7C(fs)!=0 (if(==0){fail;return;}); CallTask_RestoreOverworld asserts it ==0 (if(!=0){fail;return;}). All 11 fns matched first build with this form. (If GF_AssertFail WERE noreturn, GF_ASSERT would be correct — check the prototype.)

patterns.title: If a frozen header uses fx32/VecFx32/MtxFx33 but #includes nothing for them, global.h may NOT provide them and clang-format pins the .c-matching header first — wrap `#include <nitro/fx.h>` before it in // clang-format off
patterns.body: global.h (force-included) does NOT reliably define fx32/VecFx32 — files that use them include <nitro/fx.h> explicitly (e.g. camera.c, and self-sufficient headers like camera.h include it themselves). unk_02020B8C.h is frozen and uses fx32 but includes nothing, so the includer must define fx32 BEFORE it. clang-format forces the header matching the .c filename to be the first include, so a plain `#include <nitro/fx.h>` gets reordered AFTER unk_02020B8C.h -> `undefined identifier fx32` (cascading parse errors into mi/memory.h, mi/dma.h). Fix: pin the order with `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on` around `#include <nitro/fx.h>` then `#include "unk_02020B8C.h"`. (The fx/fx.h guard isnt pre-set, so the explicit include really does define the types.) Symptom signature: first error is fx32 undefined at the frozen header line, then a flood of undefined-identifier errors in unrelated nitro headers.

patterns.title: Overworld 2D geometry uses the XZ plane (Y is up), not XY
patterns.body: For overworld vector math (angle-between, point-to-line, segment intersection on the ground), the '2D' computation uses the .x and .z components of VecFx32, not .x and .y. Y is the up axis. In CalcAngleBetweenVecs (unk_02020B8C.s) the matching dot/cross are dot = FX_Mul(na.z,nb.z)+FX_Mul(na.x,nb.x) and cross = FX_Mul(na.z,nb.x)-FX_Mul(na.x,nb.z) (note the .z lead term and the XZ-handed cross sign, which is the negation of a naive y->z substitution). If a vec-math function diffs only in the ldr stack offsets (e.g. reading sp+44/sp+32 where you read sp+40/sp+28), suspect a .y<->.z field swap. Symptom: identical _ll_mul structure, only 4 load-offset bytes differ.

patterns.title: && (all-pass->return 1) vs || (any-fail->return 0) controls return-block placement
patterns.body: A multi-term bounds/validity check compiled by MWCC places the two return epilogues in an order that depends on how you write it. `if (A||B||...||H) return 0; return 1;` puts the shared `return 0` block inline right after the checks and forces the LAST term to be inverted (ble vs bgt) to branch over it to `return 1` at the end. The asm form that keeps `return 1` as the inline fall-through with a single shared `return 0` block at the very end (all N checks forward-branch blt/bgt to it) is produced by the && form: `if (A2 && B2 && ... && H2) return 1; return 0;` where each term is the negation (maxX>=out->x, minX<=out->x, ...). Match the source to whichever return is the fall-through in the asm. Saw this in sub_02020F4C (8-term AABB check).

patterns.title: MWCC assigns local stack slots in declaration order, first-declared at highest address
patterns.body: When a function is byte-identical to the asm EXCEPT the sp+N offsets in every load/store (and the VEC_* out-pointer args), the cause is local declaration ORDER. MWCC lays out stack-homed locals so the first-declared gets the highest sp offset, each subsequent one lower. To match, reorder the C declarations so (high->low) = asm's (highest-offset-local ... lowest). Example: GetDistanceFromPointToLine matched once declarations were reordered to lineDir, toPoint, diff, proj, zero (asm slots 68,56,44,32,20).
