Corollary: two FX_Modf integer-part outputs need two distinct named locals (intPartX, intPartY) to get two stack slots rather than one reused slot (sub_02020F4C).

patterns.title: MWCC -ipa file emits consecutive file-scope const STRUCTs in reverse definition order
patterns.body: When a file has multiple file-scope `static const` struct objects (e.g. several OverlayManagerTemplate launch templates) plus a const array (a jump/function-pointer table), MWCC -ipa file lays out .rodata with the const structs in REVERSE source-definition order, with the array kept last. Symptom: all functions match in objdiff but `main.sbin`/full ROM SHA1 FAILS, and `objdump -t -j .rodata` shows the struct objects at swapped offsets vs the asm (e.g. you defined _02108EA0 then _02108EB0 but MWCC emitted EB0@0x00, EA0@0x10). Fix: define the const structs in the OPPOSITE order to how you want them emitted (define EB0 then EA0 to get EA0@0x00, EB0@0x10). Verified in unk_02097024.c: two OverlayManagerTemplate + one state-func jump table. The jump-table array stayed last in both orderings. Always run `chiri pkg -- compare`, not just objdiff — this is a section-layout diff objdiff cannot see.

patterns.title: Unsigned countdown loop counter -> subs/bne; signed int -> cmp/bgt
patterns.body: For a `do { ... } while (--i)` countdown loop, the counter's signedness changes the loop epilogue. A SIGNED `int i` lets MWCC use the i>0 shortcut and emits `subs i,#1; <other body op>; cmp i,#0; bgt` — the decrement floats away from the branch and needs a separate cmp (extra 2 bytes + possible nop). An UNSIGNED `u32 i` forces a plain nonzero test, emitting `<body op>; subs i,#1; bne` with the decrement adjacent to the branch (no cmp). If a countdown loop is ~4 bytes too big with a cmp+bgt where the asm has bne, switch the counter to u32. Saw in ov01_021FD3F8 (overlay_01_021FD1B8.s). Pair with caching loop-invariant struct fields (e.g. mgr->count) in locals so they survive calls in callee regs instead of being reloaded each iteration.

patterns.title: objdiff 'SIZE mismatch' false positive: inline Thumb jump table + cross-section relocations
patterns.body: A function with an inline Thumb switch jump table (add pc,r0 then .short offset entries) can show as an objdiff SIZE/byte mismatch even when it is byte-identical after linking. Two causes: (1) the asm reference object has one merged .text so local `bl` targets are PC-encoded directly (f000 fXXX), while the MWCC -ipa file object emits per-function sections so every `bl` is a relocation placeholder (f000 f800) — these resolve to the same bytes at link; (2) objdump renders the jump-table bytes as a .word in the asm but as two .short/instructions in the C object, confusing objdiff's size measurement. Verify by normalizing reloc operands (sed 's/[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>/X/') before diffing, and ALWAYS trust `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) over objdiff for these. Saw in ov01_021FB6C4 (overlay_01_021FB5D4.s): objdiff said 'SIZE 134 vs 138' but the full ROM matched.

patterns.title: Split a nested call into a local to force a struct-field reload across the call
patterns.body: When code is f(g(s->ptr->a), s->ptr->b, ...), MWCC may evaluate the non-call argument s->ptr->b BEFORE the call g(), caching s->ptr in a callee register so it survives g - using an extra callee reg and shifting the whole function register allocation. The asm instead RELOADS s->ptr after g() returns. To match, hoist the call into its own statement: T x = g(s->ptr->a); f(x, s->ptr->b, ...). Now s->ptr->b is evaluated after g() returns so MWCC reloads s->ptr (cannot prove g did not modify it) - no extra callee reg, allocation matches. Saw in unk_020192D0.c case 4.

patterns.title: ipa-shared-headers (sound.h): pass u16 funcs as int locally when a wider value is passed
patterns.body: The sound functions PlaySE/StopSE (unk_02005D10.h, sound.h family) are declared with u16 params in the current headers, but at matching time several callers were compiled against int-param declarations. A file that passes a WIDER value (e.g. FrontierScript_ReadVar returns u32) to PlaySE(u16) gets an MWCC truncation mask (lsls r0,#16; lsrs r0,#16) that the retail asm does NOT have - because the asm saw an int param (no conversion). Fix with the split-header pattern: do NOT include unk_02005D10.h/sound.h; declare the SE/fanfare functions locally with int params [void PlaySE(int); void StopSE(int,int); etc.]. Callers passing u16 values are unaffected (u16->int and u16->u16 both emit no mask), which is why only u32-passing files trip the gate. Note the BGM funcs (PlayBGM, Sound_SetFieldBGM) genuinely take u16 - a value passed to them DOES get masked if stored in a wider local (use u32 seqNo). Saw in overlay_80_02235390.c.

patterns.title: Use a switch (shared cases) to stop MWCC fusing `x==c1 || x==c2` into a (unsigned)(x-c1)<=N range check
patterns.body: MWCC -O4,p compiles `if (x == 2 || x == 3)` (consecutive constants) into a RANGE check: `subs rN,#2; cmp rN,#1; bhi` (or `adds #0xfe; lsls#24; lsrs#24; cmp #1; bhi` for a u8). If the target asm instead does EXPLICIT compares `cmp #2; beq IN; cmp #3; bne OUT` (the literal `||` short-circuit, no subtract/mask), rewrite the C as a switch with shared cases: `switch (x) { case 2: case 3: <body>; break; }` (for a value, `case 2: case 3: return TRUE;` then `return FALSE;`). MWCC emits the shared-case body via the same beq/bne fall-through as the `||`, but does NOT apply the range peephole — giving the exact `cmp #2; beq; cmp #3; bne` the asm has. Verified in overlay_80_02238034: BattleArcade_MultiplayerCheck (was 14 bytes range-opt -> 16 bytes explicit, matched) and the inline `ctx->type == 2 || ctx->type == 3` block guard in BattleArcade_NewBattleSetup. Diagnose: objdiff/disasm shows `subs;cmp;bhi` (C) vs `cmp;beq;cmp;bne` (asm), function 2 bytes too small. Related: [[branch-or-vs-and]], [[switch-jumptable-density]].

patterns.title: Compute `range = hi - lo` INSIDE each if/else branch (not after the merge) to get the subtract before a following call
patterns.body: For `return lo + LCRandom() % (hi - lo)` where lo/hi are assigned in an if/else, MWCC evaluates the modulus operands left-to-right: it calls LCRandom() FIRST, then computes `(hi-lo)` AFTER the call (keeps both hi and lo live across the call, subtracts after -> `bl; subs r1,r5,r4`). If the target asm computes the range BEFORE the call (`subs r5,r0,r4; bl LCRandom; ...`), it kept only {lo, range} live across the call. To match, compute the range inside EACH branch using the just-loaded values: `if (cond) { lo = t[i].c; range = t[i].d - lo; } else { lo = t[i].a; range = t[i].b - lo; } return lo + LCRandom() % range;`. The subtraction then sits in each branch (before the merge/call), exactly like the asm, and only lo+range survive the call. A single post-merge `range = hi - lo;` statement does NOT force this — MWCC still sinks the subtract past the call. Verified in overlay_80_02238034 ov80_02238034 (random level in [lo,hi)).

patterns.title: Parenthesize `(a2+1) + 7*a1` to control which addend is the final-add's first operand (MWCC preloads the mul constant)
patterns.body: MWCC evaluates `(a2 + 1) + 7 * a1` as: `mov r0,#7` (preload mul constant early), `adds r3,r2,#1` (the (a2+1) addend), `muls r0,r1` (7*a1), `adds r0,r3,r0` (range r3 first). Writing `7 * a1 + a2 + 1` instead parses as `((7*a1)+a2)+1` -> `muls; adds r0,r2,r0; adds r0,r0,#1` (different schedule, +1 is a separate trailing add). The grouping of the constant-fold determines the final `add` operand order (`add r0,r3,r0` vs `add r0,r0,#1`). Match by grouping the source exactly as the value is built in asm. Verified in overlay_80_02238034 ov80_02238034. Combine with making the multiplied index `u32` so `if (a1 >= 8)` and the array index use unsigned `blo` not signed `blt` (see [[cast-unsigned-for-branch]]).

patterns.title: Assign a u32 function return to an int local before signed arithmetic, or `(a - b)/2` becomes an unsigned shift (lsr)
patterns.body: `(width<<3) - FontID_String_GetWidth(...)` then `/2`: FontID_String_GetWidth returns u32, so the subtraction promotes to unsigned and `/2` compiles to a single `lsrs #1` (logical). If the target asm does SIGNED division (`subs; lsrs rX,#31; adds; asrs rY,#1` — the sign-bit round-toward-zero idiom), the original kept the value SIGNED: store the u32 return into an `int` local first (`int width = FontID_String_GetWidth(...); x = ((win->width<<3) - width)/2;`). `int - int` is signed, so `/2` emits the signed-div idiom and matches. A plain subtract (no division) is unaffected (same bytes signed/unsigned), so this only bites on `/`, `%`, `>>` of the difference. Also for the align dispatch in the same function (ov01_021F4234): a `switch (align) { case 1:..; case 2:..; }` emits the asm's `cmp #1;beq;cmp #2;beq;b` jump-to-body dispatch, whereas `if/else if` emits interleaved `cmp;bne` skips. Seen in overlay_01_021F3F50 ov01_021F4234. Related: [[switch-form-avoids-equality-or-range-opt]].

patterns.title: Zero a small stack struct with an aggregate initializer `{0,0,0}`, not field-by-field, to get base-pointer stores
patterns.body: `VecFx32 v; v.x=0; v.y=0; v.z=0;` makes MWCC emit sp-DIRECT stores (`movs rZ,#0; str rZ,[sp,#off]; str rZ,[sp,#off+4]; str rZ,[sp,#off+8]`). The retail code for the same zero-init uses a BASE POINTER (`add rP,sp,#off; movs rZ,#0; str rZ,[rP]; str rZ,[rP,#4]; str rZ,[rP,#8]`) — produced by an AGGREGATE INITIALIZER: `VecFx32 v = {0,0,0};`. Switching field-assignments to the initializer flipped overlay_01_021FE780 ov01_021FE7DC from 38 diffs to 7 and ov01_021FE8B0 from 6 to ~2 (the rest fixed by also loading the first call arg into a local before the init so &v lands directly in the arg register r1). Use the initializer whenever the asm zeroes a VecFx32/MtxFx/struct local through a held base pointer. Combine with [[decl-order-regalloc]] for which stack slot the struct gets.

patterns.title: Hoist a function-call argument that must occupy r0 ABOVE a sibling computation, via a temp, to match the asm's register choice
patterns.body: `sub_0206121C(MapObject_GetFieldSystem(obj), &pos)` preceded by `pos.x = (a<<16)+k; pos.z=(b<<16)+k;` — MWCC evaluates the position stores FIRST (using r0/r1), then calls MapObject_GetFieldSystem as the 1st arg. If the target asm calls MapObject_GetFieldSystem FIRST (r0=fieldSystem, held across the position math, so the math uses r1/r2), hoist it into a temp BEFORE the computation: `FieldSystem *fs = MapObject_GetFieldSystem(obj); pos.x=...; pos.z=...; sub_0206121C(fs, &pos);`. The temp keeps fieldSystem in r0 across the position math, shifting the math up one register (r0/r1 -> r1/r2) to match. Diagnose: same instructions, every register shifted by one. Seen in overlay_01_021FE780 ov01_021FE7DC (fixed the last 7 diffs).

patterns.title: VRAM key->address `(key<<16)>>13` IS NNS_GfdGetTexKeyAddr/PlttKeyAddr `((0xFFFF&key)<<3)`
patterns.body: When a function returns `lsl rN,#16; lsr rN,#13` applied to an NNSGfdTexKey/NNSGfdPlttKey (from NNS_GfdDefaultFuncAllocTexVram/PlttVram), that is the library inline NNS_GfdGetTexKeyAddr(key)/NNS_GfdGetPlttKeyAddr(key) = `(u32)((0x0000FFFF & key) << NNS_GFD_*KEY_ADDR_SHIFT)` (SHIFT=3). MWCC fuses the mask+shift `(x&0xFFFF)<<3` into `lsl#16; lsr#13`. Use the macro (include nnsys/gfd.h), not a hand-written shift. Also: a 16-bit `enum HeapID` stored in a u16 struct field (strh/ldrh) must be cast `(enum HeapID)field` at each use (MWCC errors on implicit u16->enum); the cast is free (ldrh already zero-extends). And `(NarcId)0xNN` for a literal NarcId arg. Seen in overlay_80_02239960 ov80_02239AB0/AD4 (SPLEmitter particle manager).

patterns.title: Match double-math (_dflt/_dadd/_dmul/_dfix) by writing the exact decimal literal and (double) casts in evaluation order
patterns.body: A function calling _dflt/_dadd/_dmul/_dfix is doing double-precision arithmetic on ints. Decode the double constant from its two pool words (high,low) with python struct.unpack('>d', bytes.fromhex(HItHEN LO)) -> e.g. 0x40C19999_9999999A = 9011.2. Write that exact decimal literal in C; MWCC re-encodes it to the same 64-bit pattern. `_dflt(x)` = `(double)x`, `_dfix(d)` = `(int)d`. Operand order follows source: `_dmul(a,b)` with a in (r0,r1) means `a*b`; `_dadd(CONST, y)` with the const loaded into (r0,r1) AFTER y is computed means `CONST + y` (MWCC evaluates the cheap const operand last but keeps it as the left operand). Verified: overlay_01_021F3378 ov01_021F33B8/348C matched on the FIRST build with `position.y = (int)((double)counter * (9011.2 + (double)(counter << 11)))`. Also `counter % 2` for the `lsr#31; lsl#31; sub; ror#31; add` idiom (signed mod-2). The jump-table function in the same file is an objdiff SIZE false positive ([[objdiff-false-positive-inline-jumptable-reloc]]) -- confirm with chiri pkg -- compare.

patterns.title: `&work->member->field` after `work->member = src` reuses the stored value; avoids re-reading src (but read ORDER may still differ)
patterns.body: In a callback that does `work->unk7c = data->manager; ...(&data->manager->unk4)...`, MWCC RE-READS data->manager for the second access (+2 bytes, aliasing-conservative after the store). Writing `&work->unk7c->unk4` instead (the member just stored) makes MWCC reuse the stored register value -> no re-read, size-correct. CAVEAT: this can leave a read-ORDER difference -- the retail code reads BOTH data fields (manager@4, fieldSystem@0) into regs FIRST, then does all the stores; the natural C `work->unk78=data->fieldSystem; work->unk7c=data->manager;` reads offset 0 first. Neither caching `manager` in a local (reorders fieldSystem to r0 + materializes work early) nor swapping the assignment order (breaks the store order / reloads work->unk7c) reproduces the batched read-then-store schedule. Seen identically in overlay_01_021FED9C ov01_021FEE64 and overlay_01_021FEC38 ov01_021FED14 (8/9 each) -- the camera/3D-effect family's data-copy cb1.

patterns.title: Stack-passed u16 params stored to wide fields: declare them int/u32, not u16 (Thumb ldrh can't use sp, forcing an extra base-pointer add)
patterns.body: A function whose 5th/6th args are passed on the stack and just copied into u32 struct fields: if you declare those params `u16`, MWCC reads them with `ldrh`, and because Thumb `ldrh Rd,[Rn,#imm]` requires a LOW base register (sp/r13 is illegal), it must first emit `add rN,sp,#k` then `ldrh [rN,#off]` -- an extra instruction and a wrong register schedule. The retail asm reads them with `ldr rN,[sp,#off]` (sp-direct word load), i.e. the params are int/u32-width. Declare the stack params `u32` (or int) so MWCC emits the sp-direct `ldr`. When the public header (used by the CALLER) declares them `u16`, keep that header frozen and use a LOCAL prototype with the int/u32 types in the defining .c (split-header / IPA discipline). Verified on unk_020979A8 (sub_020979A8 constructor: a4/a5 sp[24]/sp[28]). See [[ipa-split-header]].

patterns.title: A u16->u32 widening store of a register param inserts a cast node that changes the MWCC list-scheduler tie-break; declare the param u32 to match
patterns.body: Even a REGISTER-passed param (not just stack) can break matching purely by type width. unk_020979A8's `a3` (u16) stored to a u32 field `work->unk4=a3` compiled with every instruction correct but TWO swapped: the asm hoists the LoadArea-arg base copy `adds r1,r4,#0` and the `a3` reload ahead of the `unk2` store, mine emitted them after. The cause was the u16->u32 widening cast node in the IR perturbing the list scheduler's tie-break between equally-ready instructions. Declaring `a3` as `u32` (no widening cast; the spilled r3 is already a full word) removed the cast and reproduced the asm's exact instruction order -> full match. Rule: when a param is only ever stored to a wider field and the asm shows no zero/sign-extend, declare the param at the field's width. Pairs with [[u16-stack-param-as-int-avoids-ldrh-basepointer]].

patterns.title: Public headers often over-widen params to int; stack params stored to byte fields are read ldrb/ldrsb (sp-illegal -> negative-base trick). Declare them u8/s8 via split-header.
patterns.body: Mirror image of [[u16-stack-param-as-int-avoids-ldrh-basepointer]]. A shared public header (e.g. include/unk_0201956C.h, used by a matched caller) frequently declares params as `int` for convenience, but the FUNCTION reads narrow stack params at byte width. Tells: the asm reads a 5th/6th stack param with `ldrb`/`ldrsb` AND uses the negative-base trick `ldr r3,=0xFFFFFFF8; add r3,sp; ldrb r2,[r3,#0x10]` (because Thumb ldrb/ldrsb/ldrh cannot use sp as base, just like ldrh). If you declare such a param `int`, MWCC emits a plain `ldr [sp,#k]` (word) and the bytes diverge. Fix: declare the defining function's param at the field's width (u8 if stored to a u8 field / read ldrb; s8 if stored to an s8 field / read ldrsb) using a LOCAL prototype, and DON'T include the public header (keep it frozen at int for the caller). On unk_0201956C this fixed sub_020198FC (a4->u8), sub_02019B70 (a4,a5->s8). Related: struct velocity fields read via ldrsb in `x += field` are s8 not u8 (sub_02019978); for-loop counters with `blo` compare and no 16-bit wrap are u32 not u16 (sub_02019934, sub_020195C0).

patterns.title: Place a VecFx32 zero-init exactly where the asm zeroes it by declaring it mid-block (C99) — aggregate init gives the base-pointer store form, the declaration point gives the position
patterns.body: Two separate facts combine. (1) [[aggregate-init-zeroes-vec-via-base-pointer]]: `VecFx32 v = {0,0,0}` emits `add rN,sp,#k; str r0,[rN]; str r0,[rN,#4]; str r0,[rN,#8]` (base-pointer), whereas field stores `v.x=0;v.y=0;v.z=0` emit sp-direct `str r0,[sp,#k]`. (2) MWCC emits the aggregate initializer AT the declaration point, not hoisted to function entry. So when the retail asm zeroes the vec in the MIDDLE of the function (e.g. between two struct-field stores), declare the vec with a mid-block/nested-scope declaration there: `... data.unk8 = f(); { VecFx32 vec = {0,0,0}; data.mapObject = x; g(&vec,&data); }`. Declaring it at the top with aggregate init gives the right FORM but the wrong POSITION (hoisted up); field assignments in the right position give the right position but wrong form. The nested block gets both. Verified on ov01_02200730 (overlay_01_022006A8). Project builds -lang c99 so mid-block decls are legal.

patterns.title: Camera/3D-effect family (ov01_021F1348 cluster): a cb1 that BLOCK-copies the data struct (work->sub = *sub_02068D98(p)) matches cleanly, unlike the field-by-field re-read cb1 that is the family holdout
patterns.body: The map-object 3D-effect family (constructor via ov01_021F1430, spawn via ov01_021F1620 with a const template {sizeof(work), cb1, cb1, cb2, cb2}, data fetched in cb1 via sub_02068D98) comes in two cb1 shapes. The FIELD-BY-FIELD shape (work->unk78=data->fieldSystem; work->unk7c=data->manager; ...(&data->manager->unk4)) is a persistent MWCC read-order/scheduling holdout (overlay_01_021FEE64/021FED14 etc.). The BLOCK-COPY shape — where cb1 does a whole-struct assignment `work->copiedData = *(MyData*)sub_02068D98(param0)` (4 words -> 2x ldmia/stmia) then reads members out of the copy — matches with zero fuss. overlay_01_022006A8 (9 fns) matched fully this way. When picking the cb1 C shape, prefer the single struct-assignment when the asm shows ldmia/stmia (not N field loads/stores). Define per-file manager/work/data structs and use LOCAL externs for the cluster fns (do NOT include overlay_01_021F1348.h / overlay_01.h — they conflict). [[reuse-just-stored-member-avoids-source-reread]]

patterns.title: Data file with many exported const arrays that contain RELOCATIONS (e.g. function pointers): MWCC -ipa file emits one .rodata section per symbol, grouped by size and PERMUTED within each size-group by a fixed positional permutation. Reorder the source to invert it.
patterns.body: scrcmd_mart-style const arrays of plain immediates (ITEM_*, no relocations) stay in source order and match. But exported const arrays that hold cross-TU symbol refs (function-pointer step tables like gMovementCmdSteps_NNN -> MapObjectMovementCmd*_Step*) are emitted by MWCC as one separate .rodata section EACH, then ordered: first bucketed by section size (all 8-byte arrays, then all 0xc-byte arrays, ...), and within each bucket permuted by a fixed positional permutation Q that depends only on the count, NOT on the names/content. The linker preserves the .o section order, so a per-symbol objdiff PASSES while `chiri pkg -- compare` FAILS on rodata order (cf the unk_0201010C warning). RECIPE to match: (1) write arrays in asm-label order and build; (2) read the placed order `O = objdump -t obj.o | grep 'O .rodata' | awk '{print $NF}'`; (3) for each source index i, Q[i] = index of asmOrder[i] within O; (4) rewrite the source definitions as S[i] = asmOrder[Q[i]]; rebuild and confirm objdump order == asm order, then `chiri pkg -- compare`. Verified on unk_data_020FD978 (17 arrays: 8-byte Q=[2,3,0,4,5,1,9,8,7,6], 0xc-byte Q=[0,1,3,4,2,5,6]). The source ends up in a non-obvious order; that's expected and load-bearing. See [[section-mapping]].

patterns.title: A flags byte written via manual mask at bit0 + bitfields at other bits needs a union {u8 raw; struct bits}
patterns.body: When a byte holds several 1-bit flags set by different functions and the asm shows NO (u8) narrow for the bit-0 flag (just ldrb; bic #1; and #1(val); orr; strb) but DOES narrow for bits 1-4 ((u8)val via lsls#24/lsrs#24 then the <<31>>(31-pos) insert), the bit-0 write is a MANUAL mask `b->raw = (b->raw & ~1) | (val & 1)` while the others are bitfield assignments. A bitfield assignment of an int value ALWAYS narrows to the u8 storage first; at bit position 0 that yields a spurious (u8) the retail build lacks. Model as union { u8 raw; struct { u8 flag0:1; u8 flag1:1; ... } bits; } and use raw for the bit-0 manual mask, .bits.flagN for the rest (those match plain `= val`). Seen in unk_02068FC8: sub_020692A0 a0->bit0 (manual) vs sub_020692C4/308/3AC gender/dexEnabled/a1/sigExists->bits.

patterns.title: `x &= ~1; x &= 1;` as TWO separate load-modify-stores = a bitfield struct {u32 a:1; u32 b:31}, not a plain u32
patterns.body: An array element zeroed with the asm emitting TWO full RMW (ldr;bic #1;str; ldr;and #1;str) — not one merged ldr;bic;and;str — is a bitfield struct: `struct { u32 bit0:1; u32 rest:31; } arr[N];` written `arr[i].bit0 = 0; arr[i].rest = 0;` (bit0=0 -> bic #1; rest=0 -> and #1 keeping bit0). A plain `u32 arr[N]` with `arr[i] &= ~1; arr[i] &= 1;` makes MWCC merge the two ops AND strength-reduce the index to a walking pointer; the bitfield-array form keeps &arr loop-invariant with [base, i*4] indexing and two distinct stores. Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_0206940C (rec->unk48[8]).

patterns.title: An intervening store to a sibling field through the same base pointer invalidates MWCC's cached value -> forces a reload
patterns.body: Clamping consecutive fields: the asm RELOADS a field for its check (ldr field; cmp) for some fields but compares the source register directly for others. The reload appears when another store through the same base sits BETWEEN the field's store and its check (MWCC drops the cached value after any same-base store, conservative aliasing). To get the reload form: emit both stores first then both checks (`s->a=x; s->b=y; if(s->a>M)..; if(s->b>M)..;`). To get the no-reload form: keep store and check adjacent with no intervening same-base store (`s->a=x; if(x>M)..;`). Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_020693AC (unk3c/unk40 reload via the in-between store; unk38/unk44 compare the param).

patterns.title: Task/state-machine fns: break to ONE trailing `return FALSE` for a shared return-0 epilogue; keep `return TRUE` inline
patterns.body: A switch(state) task fn where every non-terminal case ends return FALSE and one case ends return TRUE: writing `return FALSE;` per case makes MWCC emit a separate movs r0,#0; pop for each. Retail has ONE shared return-0 block at the tail reached by branches, only return TRUE inline. Reproduce with `break;` for every FALSE path (set next state then break) and a single `return FALSE;` after the switch; keep `return TRUE;` inline. case-0 still falls through to case-1 (no break). Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_02069498.

patterns.title: Single-TU split-param (u8 stack arg) and a computed-reduction spill in the lowest slot can be unmatchable -> NONMATCHING
patterns.body: Two MWCC register-allocator behaviors that resist source control within ONE translation unit: (1) Split-param: a callee reads a u8 STACK param via ldrb (no narrow) while the retail caller passes the int with no narrow; with caller+callee in the SAME TU there is one prototype — u8 makes the caller narrow (lsls#24/lsrs#24 before the stack store), int makes the callee narrow for its bitfield/compare. The split-header trick (different prototype per file) does not apply. (2) A computed reduction temp (sum of several already-spilled values) can be assigned the LOWEST spill slot (sp+0x20) instead of its computation-order slot, shifting every earlier spill by +4 — not fixable by declaration order, by moving the decl, or by extracting the embedded call. When both hit one large function, wrap it as `asm` NONMATCHING and keep the file's other functions as matching C (the ROM still matches). Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_02068FC8 (a1 stack param to sub_02069308; the `sum` GameStats reduction).

patterns.title: A field-by-field cb1 in the ov01_021F1348 camera family DOES match when it copies flat data fields (no nested manager->unk4 reread)
patterns.body: Not every field-by-field cb1 is the holdout from [[camera-family-blockcopy-cb1-matches]]. The holdout reads through a NESTED pointer (work->unk7c=data->manager; ...&data->manager->unk4) which creates an aliasing/read-order schedule MWCC won't reproduce. A cb1 that just copies FLAT fields of the sub_02068D98 data into the work (work->unk18=data->unk8; work->unk14=data->unk4; work->unk10=data->unk0, in descending order) matches first try as plain field assignments. ov01_021FE4FC matched this way (it even keeps a dead `work->unk10 = sub_02068D90(param0)` store that is overwritten by data->unk0 — reproduce it verbatim; MWCC keeps the dead store). Manager-with-arrays files in this family (10x sub-objects + 10x NNSG3dRenderObj) decompile cleanly using src/field/overlay_01_021FE780.c as the template: per-file structs, local externs, NO cluster header. Jump-table address-calculators (ov01_021FE2DC/35C) show spurious objdiff SIZE diffs (data-region mapping-symbol miscount) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare. The a4-data and VecFx32 position locals in the spawn fn need position declared FIRST (first-declared = highest sp offset).

patterns.title: MWCC inline `asm` quirks: bare [rN] memory operands misassemble — use [rN, #0]; encode jump-table halfwords as `lsl rd,rm,#0`
patterns.body: Writing a NONMATCHING `asm static void f(...) {...}` block in MWCC sp2p2: (1) A bare memory operand `ldr r0, [r3]` (no offset) misassembles (observed as `ldr r0,[r3,#8]`); ALWAYS write the explicit offset `ldr r0, [r3, #0]` / `str r0, [r4, #0]`. (2) `movs rd, rm` is rejected (parsed as a label → 'unknown assembler instruction mnemonic' / 'label movs redefined'); use `lsl rd, rm, #0` instead. (3) For a Thumb `add pc, rN` jump table, MWCC inline asm does NOT support `.short label-label-2` data directives — encode each jump-table halfword as a `lsl rd, rm, #0` instruction whose machine encoding equals the offset (lsl rd,rm,#0 = 0x0000|(rm<<3)|rd, e.g. 0x0006=`lsl r6,r0,#0`, 0x0012=`lsl r2,r2,#0`, 0x000a=`lsl r2,r1,#0`, 0x0010=`lsl r0,r2,#0`), per src/battle/battle_hp_bar.c. (4) `ldr rN, =symbol` and `ldr rN, =0xVALUE` work; `bl FuncName` to externs/statics works; `.balign` is unsupported. Diagnose a wrong NONMATCHING result by disassembling the built .o (objdump) and byte-comparing; objdiff's per-function SIZE for a jump-table fn is unreliable (data-region $d/$t mapping) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare. Used to NONMATCHING ov01_02200A08 (camera-family render cb, MWCC list-scheduler tie-break on the scale-copy temp registers).

patterns.title: A file gated_by ipa-shared-headers can still be decompiled if it only CALLS the shared-header functions (no signature change)
patterns.body: The ipa-shared-headers blocker (sound.h / unk_02005D10.h family) is about CHANGING a signature in a shared header, which cascades into already-matched callers. A new file that merely CALLS those functions (e.g. PlaySE/StopSE, declared in include/unk_02005D10.h) with their existing signatures needs NO header change, so there is no cascade — just #include the existing header and call them. The triage's `gated_by: ipa-shared-headers` is conservative (flags any file sharing symbols with the blocked cluster); check whether the file actually needs to ADD/CHANGE a declaration before treating it as blocked. overlay_01_021F3114 (a PlayerAvatar turn-task calling PlaySE(SEQ_SE_DP_F209)/StopSE) matched 6/6 this way.

patterns.title: Reading arr[k] just before arr+=n: use an explicit pre-advance pointer for the address-form load
patterns.body: Source `val=arr[k]; arr+=n;` emits the short offset-form `ldr [base,#k*size]`, but retail often used the address-form `add rX,base,#k*size; ldr [rX]`. To match, write `const T *p = arr+k; arr+=n; val=*p;` -- mutating arr between p and *p stops MWCC folding *p back to an offset load. In unk_02091880 (sub_02091B8C, ECMenuBuild_Generic) this 2-byte read fixed a 68-byte branch-offset CASCADE (one early instruction-size diff shifts every later branch target). `arr[-1]` after advance also yields address-form but emits `subs` not `adds`.

patterns.title: A counter read from a u16 array but decremented must be int, not u16
patterns.body: `u16 c=arr[i]; while(c){...;c--;}` emits lsl#16/lsr#16 truncation on each `c--`; retail used plain `sub rN,#1`. Declare `int c=arr[i];` to drop the truncation. (unk_02091880 ECMenuBuild_Generic subcount.)

patterns.title: Cache an array-element offset in a local to flip a commutative-add operand order
patterns.body: `arr[base_field[idx]+k]` may emit `add rd,k,offset` (param first) where retail wanted `add rd,offset,k` (loaded value first). Caching `int off=base_field[idx]; arr[off+k]` makes MWCC emit offset-first. Swapping the SOURCE operands alone did NOT work -- the temp did. Fixed sub_02091C40/C60 in unk_02091880.

patterns.title: Indexed array access vs walking pointer changes register allocation
patterns.body: In a loop, a[i]/b[i] (indexed) vs *pa++/*pb++ (explicit walking) can yield different callee-saved register assignments. Switching a dispatch loop from a walking spec++ to indexed table[i] moved MWCC toward retail's allocation (unk_02091880 sub_020918D4: 15 to 8 byte diffs).

patterns.title: Place an early-out return as the function-end fall-through
patterns.body: `if(gate!=0){ body; return X; } return 0;` emits return 0 at the END (retail layout); `if(gate==0) return 0; body; return X;` inlines the return early. Choose the structure matching the asm block order. (unk_02091880 ECMenuBuild_Move: 27 to 0 diffs.)

patterns.title: Accumulator-vs-induction-var register tie-breaks are sometimes not source-controllable, use NONMATCHING
patterns.body: Functions can be correct C that matches every instruction except which callee-saved register the accumulator vs an induction var gets (e.g. total/walk in r4/r7, or added/i in r6/r7). Many reorderings (decl order, u32 vs int, result temps, index vs walk) may not flip it. When stuck, NONMATCHING with an asm function. unk_02091880 needed it for sub_020918D4 + ECMenuBuild_TrendySayings.

patterns.title: MWCC asm functions: ldr =VAL literal pools, blx rN, bl Name all match retail
patterns.body: static asm RET f(args){...} with ldr rX,=0xVAL / ldr rX,=symbol builds a dedup-ed literal pool placed after the function (matches retail). blx rN (indirect) and bl Name (relocated extern call) work in inline asm. Combine with known quirks: bare [rN] becomes [rN,#0]; reg-move mov rd,rm rejected (use add/lsl); no .balign. Verified on unk_02091880 sub_020918D4 (blx) + ECMenuBuild_TrendySayings (multiple bl + 2 pool words).

patterns.title: MWCC accepts forward-declared incomplete static const arrays for rodata-order forward refs
patterns.body: static const u16 X[]; (incomplete, no init) is accepted as a forward declaration; define static const u16 X[]={...}; later. Lets a pointer/struct table placed early in rodata order reference word-list arrays defined later, preserving the exact rodata layout. Used throughout unk_02091880 (a 27-entry pointer table + 12-entry dispatch struct table interleaved with ~40 word-list arrays).

patterns.title: A .text section-size diff between asm and C objects is often benign (linker re-aligns per-function)
patterns.body: MWCC emits each function into its own section; the linker aligns/places them at link time. So an objdiff `.text section size` diff, AND a per-function nm-size diff equal to a trailing `.balign 4,0` pad, do NOT necessarily mean a mismatch. unk_0202C034 had .text -10 (sub_0202C46C nm size 0x42 vs asm 0x44) yet `chiri pkg -- compare` PASSED. Always confirm with compare, never reject on section size alone.

patterns.title: MWCC's idx*stride CSE across struct-element field accesses is fragile under register pressure
patterns.body: For arr[i].fieldA, arr[i].fieldB, ... MWCC normally hoists i*stride into one register and reuses it (field-base + hoisted-index addressing). But with extra register pressure (e.g. a 5th param read from the stack mid-function) it may RE-compute i*stride per access, diverging from retail. A sibling function with fewer params can match while this one doesn't. Caching a record pointer changes the addressing form ([rec,#off]) and won't match field-base+index. -> NONMATCHING. (unk_0202C034 sub_0202C4F0 vs matching sub_0202C5E4.)

patterns.title: u16-returning function may elide the return truncation when the value is provably small
patterns.body: `u16 f(){ int x; ...; return x; }` normally truncates with lsl#16/lsr#16 on return. Retail sometimes ELIDES it when x is provably <=0xFFFF (e.g. x = i+1, i<32). If your structure doesn't trigger MWCC's range analysis you get the extra truncation; u16 local instead makes it worse (truncates on assign too). Not reliably source-controllable -> NONMATCHING. (unk_0202C034 sub_0202C318.)

patterns.title: Save-accessor structs interleave parallel arrays indexed by one record index with different strides
patterns.body: Friend/record save chunks often hold several arrays addressed by the same index but different stride/base: e.g. header[0x40] + DWCFriendData[32]@0xc (off 0x40) + BattleRecord[32]@0x38 (off 0x1c0), total 0x8c0. Model as nested struct arrays at byte offsets; accessors compute base + idx*stride + field and MWCC folds array-offset+field into one (often large, mov+lsl or ldr-pool) register offset. Jump-table get/set dispatchers map an enum to fields. (unk_0202C034, save chunk SAVE_UNK_25.)

patterns.title: MWCC inline asm CAN call soft-float runtime (_ffix/_fadd/_fflt/_fsub/_ffltu/_fmul/_ffixu) IF you add an extern prototype first (CORRECTION)
patterns.body: CORRECTION of an earlier claim. `bl _ffix`/`_fmul`/`_ffltu`/`_ffixu`/`_fsub` etc. in an `asm` function fails with 'undefined label' ONLY when the runtime symbol is not declared. Add a C prototype before the function — `void _fsub(void);` (return/arg types are irrelevant; it only needs to be a known external symbol) — and the `bl` assembles and links fine. So a NONMATCHING float function CAN be written as inline asm. The pool/bl bytes match the retail .o (both assembled by mwasmarm). Note _ffltu/_fmul/_ffixu happened to be already-known in one TU (no decl needed) while _fsub/_s32_div_f/_ffixu needed the decl — when in doubt, declare all of them. Verified: overlay_58 ov58_022379C0 (soft-float aprijuice calc) matched as inline asm after adding `void _ffltu/_fmul/_ffixu/_fsub/_s32_div_f(void);`. Writing such a function as C is still an option, but it is NOT required. See [[nonmatching-inline-asm-mwasmarm-gotchas]] for the canonical fix.

patterns.title: FX32_CONST(x) is round-half-away-from-zero (soft-float); plain x<<FX32_SHIFT is integer
patterns.body: FX32_CONST(x)=FX_F32_TO_FX32(x)=(fx32)((x>0)?x*4096+0.5f:x*4096-0.5f) -> emits _fflt/_fadd(or _fsub 0.5)/_ffix. A position computed with that rounding must use FX32_CONST; one the asm does with a plain `lsl #0xc` must use `x << FX32_SHIFT` (no float). Two sibling sprite-template builders in overlay_01_021E7FDC differed exactly this way (ov01_021E81F0 = shift, ov01_021E851C = FX32_CONST). FX32_CONST(const) folds at compile time (e.g. GX_LCD_SIZE_Y -> 0xc0000).

patterns.title: include/field/ov01_*.h often predefines the work struct + template types + signatures
patterns.body: Before modeling a field/overlay struct from scratch, check include/field/<name>.h (and the types' header, e.g. unk_02009D48.h / unk_0200A090.h for sprite-resource managers). For overlay_01_021E7FDC the header already had UnkStruct_ov01_021E7FDC (SpriteList + G2dRenderer + SpriteResourceHeaderList + GF_2DGfxResMan[6] + GF_2DGfxResObjList[6] + u16 count/heapID) and SpriteTemplate_ov01_021E81F0, plus 3 signatures to match. Enum params (GfGfxResType, NNS_G2D_VRAM_TYPE, HeapID from a u16 field) need explicit (free) casts or MWCC errors.

patterns.title: objdiff whole-file MATCH can still fail compare: per-function .text sections drop 2-mod-4 funcs' .balign trailing pad
patterns.body: objdiff masks trailing function padding, so a file can show 20/20 MATCH yet `chiri pkg -- compare` fails main.sbin. Cause: retail .s pads each function with `.balign 4,0`; a C function whose body is 2-mod-4 bytes compiles into a per-function .text section (2**2-aligned) WITHOUT that trailing 0x00 pad, so .text is short (e.g. -6 for 3 such funcs) and the linked image differs. CONTRAST [[text-section-size-diff-benign-linker-aligns]]: a section-size diff is benign only when it's section-END padding; a per-2-mod-4-function shortfall is NOT. Diagnose by comparing nm --print-size per function (asm vs C) for any function 2 bytes short. Only compare is authoritative. (unk_0203A3B0 hit this; reverted.)

patterns.title: FIX for 2-mod-4 function losing .balign trailing pad: inline-asm wrapper with trailing `lsl r0, r0, #0` (=0x0000)
patterns.body: Resolves [[objdiff-match-but-compare-fails-trailing-pad]]. When a function's matched C body is 2-mod-4 bytes and retail .s pads it with `.balign 4, 0`, MWCC's per-function .text section omits the pad. The linker does NOT always restore it: notably for the LAST function in the TU, the next object's .text needs only 2-byte (Thumb) alignment, so it slots in 2 bytes early -> `chiri pkg -- compare` fails main.sbin with .text -2 even at full 16/16 objdiff MATCH. FIX: keep the matched C under `#ifdef NONMATCHING`, and under `#else` emit the function as inline `asm` (non-static if `.public`) transcribing the matched instructions, then a trailing `lsl r0, r0, #0` which assembles to 0x0000 = the `.balign 4,0` fill, carrying the pad inside the function's own section. Proven on unk_020773AC sub_02077664 (last fn): compare went FAIL->OK. Likely un-blocks unk_0203A3B0 (apply per 2-mod-4 function). Diagnose the culprit via `nm --print-size` per function (the one 2 bytes short).

patterns.title: MWCC won't CSE a source struct field across a store into a freshly Heap_Alloc'd struct (can't prove non-alias) -> field reload or load-order tie -> NONMATCHING
patterns.body: Pattern `s = Heap_Alloc(...); s->b = a->b; ... f(a->b)`: retail loads a->b once (e.g. r2) and keeps it live across the s->b store, reusing it for the later arg. MWCC cannot prove the Heap_Alloc'd s doesn't alias a, so the store to s->b invalidates the cached a->b -> it either reloads a->b (extra ldr, +2) or, if you hand-cache it in a local, the two field loads get scheduled in the wrong order (load r2 before r0). No source form recovers retail's 'one load kept live, only s->unk0 reloaded' schedule. Resolve via NONMATCHING inline asm. Seen on unk_020773AC sub_02077604 (a0->unk0 + a0->unk4 into a fresh struct).

patterns.title: _s32_div_f (and soft-float) ARE callable from MWCC inline asm with an extern prototype (CORRECTION)
patterns.body: CORRECTION. `bl _s32_div_f` inside an `asm` function fails with 'undefined label' ONLY without a declaration. Add `void _s32_div_f(void);` (or `extern int _s32_div_f(int,int);`) before the function and it assembles/links. So functions needing signed `/` or `%` (which MWCC lowers to _s32_div_f) CAN be NONMATCHING inline asm. `/` and `%` also work fine when MWCC emits them from C. Verified: overlay_58 ov58_022379C0 called _s32_div_f from inline asm after declaring it. See [[nonmatching-inline-asm-mwasmarm-gotchas]].

patterns.title: objdiff reports spurious SIZE diffs on inline-jump-table (switch) functions — the table bytes disassemble as instructions
patterns.body: A `switch` that MWCC lowers to `add pc, rN` + an inline .short/.word offset table will show objdiff `SIZE X vs Y` mismatches even when the function is byte-identical. Two artifacts: (1) objdiff disassembles the jump-table DATA bytes as Thumb instructions (movs/lsls), so the asm .o (table rendered as .word) and the C .o (table rendered as code) appear to differ in instruction count; (2) branch targets render as ABSOLUTE addresses that differ between the two .o files (e.g. `bhi d2` vs `bhi 7e`) although both resolve to the same `+0xNN` offset. To check for REAL diffs, filter out movs/lsls/.word/.short/`+0x4>` reloc lines and compare the `+0xNN` offset suffixes; then trust `chiri pkg -- compare`. Confirmed on unk_0202D230 sub_0202D284/D308/FrontierData_BattlePointAction (all byte-matches despite objdiff SIZE diffs).

patterns.title: Single-bit extract `((u32)x<<31)>>31` folds to `& 1` (movs/ands); use a bitfield-union member to keep the lsls#31;lsrs#31 form
patterns.body: MWCC folds the 1-bit shift-extract `((u32)x << 31) >> 31` into `movs #1; ands` (i.e. `x & 1`), which mismatches retail's `lsls r0,#31; lsrs r0,#31`. MULTI-bit field extracts like `((u32)x << 27) >> 29` (3 bits) are NOT folded and match the shift form directly. Fix for the single-bit case: read it through a `union { u8 raw; struct { u8 b0:1; u8 b1:1; u8 b2_4:3; u8 b5_7:3; } bits; }` member (`f->bits.b0`) — MWCC emits the lsls/lsrs extract for bitfield reads. (unk_0202D230 sub_0202D284 case 7.) Setters in the same file used manual bic/orr masks, so don't assume a bitfield for the write side.

patterns.title: Redundant (u16) truncation before strh: drop it in a void fn, but a function that RETURNS the value keeps it via a materialized temp
patterns.body: Retail often has `lsls r0,#16; lsrs r0,#16; strh r0,[..]` — an explicit (u16) cast before a halfword store that looks redundant (strh truncates anyway). In a `void` function MWCC ALWAYS drops it, and no C form (`(u16)expr`, `u16 t=expr;field=t;`) brings it back. The tell: the asm leaves the truncated value in r0 at `pop` — the function actually RETURNS it (a `void` prototype is often a decomp error when the sole caller ignores the result). Fix: make it return the value and write `u16 t = expr; field = t; return t;` (materialize once, reuse for store AND return). Do NOT write `return field = expr;` — that stores then RELOADS the field (ldrh after strh) and shuffles regalloc. Updating the return type in a frozen header was IPA-safe here because the only caller discards the result. (unk_0202D230 sub_0202D4FC.)

patterns.title: Sparse cmp-chain switch: the fall-through (inline) case is the LAST in SOURCE order; MWCC tests in ascending VALUE order
patterns.body: For a small/sparse switch that MWCC lowers to a cmp-chain (NOT a jump table) — e.g. cases 6, 7, default with two identical bodies — MWCC always tests the case VALUES in ascending order (cmp #6 ... cmp #7 ...), but lays out the case BODIES in SOURCE order. The body placed immediately after the dispatch becomes the fall-through, reached via the last `bne default`; the other case is a forward `beq` target. If you write cases in value order (case 6 then case 7), you get `cmp6 beq L6; cmp7 beq L7; b default` — an EXTRA unconditional `b default` and both bodies as beq targets. The retail asm instead had `cmp6 beq L6(body6, placed later); cmp7 bne default; <body7 inline>` i.e. case 7 falls through. To match, write the fall-through case FIRST in source: `case 7: ...; break; case 6: ...; break; default:`. Verified in ov80_022362B8 (overlay_80_02235FC8.s): swapping case 7 above case 6 removed the spurious `b default` and matched. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: a trailing `b.n default` after the last `beq` that the retail side reaches with `bne` means you must reorder so the inline case is written first.

patterns.title: `(expr)/total + struct->field`: cache the division result in a temp to get `adds rd,result,field` (result as rn)
patterns.body: In `data->current = data->delta * data->step / data->total + data->start;` MWCC sp2p2 emitted `adds r0,r1,r0` (start as rn, division-result as rm) regardless of whether start was written on the left or right of the `+`. Retail wanted `adds r0,r0,r1` (division result as rn, loaded field as rm). Swapping the SOURCE operand order did NOT change it (consistent with [[cached-offset-flips-add-operand-order]]). Splitting into a temp fixed it: `s32 amount = data->delta*data->step/data->total; data->current = amount + data->start;` -> MWCC keeps the temp (the _s32_div_f return, already in r0) as the add accumulator -> `adds r0,r0,r1`. Lesson: when a commutative add combines a just-returned/computed value (in r0) with a freshly-loaded struct field and the operand order is wrong, hoist the computed value into a named local. Verified ov01_021FC1B4 (overlay_01_021FC05C.s).

patterns.title: A value assigned BEFORE a call (and used after) lands in a callee-saved reg + copy; assigning it AFTER is 2 bytes shorter — can break full compare even when objdiff says match
patterns.body: In `if (cond) { x = 2; foo(); } else { x = 1; } bar(x);` MWCC sets x in a CALLEE-SAVED reg before the foo() call (so it survives) then copies it to the arg reg for bar() (`movs r5,#2; bl foo; ...; adds r1,r5,#0`). Writing `if (cond) { foo(); x = 2; }` instead lets MWCC set x in a caller-saved reg AFTER the call and pass it directly (`bl foo; movs r1,#2; ...`) — 2 bytes shorter and NON-matching. Match the retail by ordering the assignment exactly as the source did (here: BEFORE the call). CRITICAL: this 2-byte size delta is inside a Thumb jump-table function, so objdiff reported the function as a SIZE artifact / the per-function check still "passed" for the others — but the overlay shrank, shifting OVERLAY LOAD ADDRESSES so OVY_2/3/4 + main.sbin ALSO failed the full SHA1. Always run chiri pkg -- compare; a -N .text section delta in objdiff that is NOT a pure jump-table artifact means a real size diff. Verified ov01_021FCE98 case 4 (overlay_01_021FCE98.s).

patterns.title: MWCC orders multiple file-scope const symbols by SIZE-ascending (ties scrambled), NOT definition order; consolidate into ONE const struct to fix rodata layout
patterns.body: When a file has several `static const` rodata objects, MWCC 2.0 emits them into .rodata sorted by SIZE ASCENDING, not source/definition/reference order (within equal sizes the order is an internal scramble you cannot control, worsened by duplicate-content entries). Symptom: objdiff reports ALL functions match but `chiri pkg -- compare` FAILS at main.sbin because the .rodata bytes are in the wrong order. Diagnose: `arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.rodata a.o x.bin` then `cmp`, and `arm-none-eabi-objdump -t x.o | grep rodata` to see the emitted order vs the target. FIX: put ALL the rodata into a SINGLE `static const struct { ... } sRodata = {...};` whose fields are in the exact target order, and reference members (`sRodata.field`, `&sRodata.arr[i]`). One symbol = fixed C struct layout = no reordering possible; the per-member literal-pool relocations differ from the original per-object symbols but resolve to the same linked addresses, so the ROM matches. Verified on unk_0208DE40 (camera VecFx32 / 16 StatPosTemplate / u8 response[11][4] / TouchscreenHitbox[11]): split-into-N gave size-sorted-but-scrambled order; the single-struct gave byte-identical .rodata and full SHA1 match.

patterns.title: A void fn that stores float-rounded values to s16 fields drops the (s16) truncation; move the rounding into a static inline helper that RETURNS s16
patterns.body: Retail often shows `bl _ffix; lsls r0,#16; asrs r0,#16; strh` (an explicit (s16) before the halfword store). In a VOID function MWCC drops that truncation for EVERY such store, no matter how you write the cast (`(s16)(s32)expr`, `(s16)expr`, an explicit temp) -> function is N*4 bytes too small (4 bytes = lsls+asrs per store). Per [[force-pre-strh-truncation-via-returned-temp]] the truncation only survives when the value is RETURNED. To keep it at MULTIPLE store sites, extract the rounding into `static inline s16 round(int diff) { ... return (s16)(...); }` and call `c->x = round(b->x-a->x);` per component. When MWCC inlines the helper (-inline on), the return-value (s16) is materialized (lsls;asrs) at EACH call site before the strh -> matches. Verified unk_0208DE40 sub_0208DFF8 (3x VecS16 component stores of FX_F32_TO_FX32((f32)diff/4096.0f/4.0f)).

patterns.title: ldrh (unsigned, imm offset) vs ldrsh (signed, reg offset) is chosen by the FIELD TYPE, not a cast at the use site
patterns.body: Thumb ldrh supports an immediate offset; ldrsh only register-offset (needs an extra movs to load the offset). For a sign-agnostic 16-bit COPY (`dst16 = src->field`) the retail build uses `ldrh [rN,#imm]`; for signed ARITHMETIC on the same field it uses `movs rK,#off; ldrsh [rN,rK]`. MWCC picks the load width from the FIELD declared type: declare the field `u16` and a plain copy emits ldrh (immediate, compact); a `(u16)` cast on an `s16` field does NOT switch ldrsh->ldrh (still ldrsh+reg-offset, +2 bytes per access). For the same field used both ways, declare it `u16` and add an explicit `(s16)` cast at the arithmetic site to force ldrsh there. Verified unk_0208DE40 sub_0208DF9C: StatPosTemplate full/base/delta as u16 -> copy branches use ldrh[#imm]; multiply branch `(s16)tmpl->base[i] + (s16)tmpl->delta[i]*stat` -> ldrsh.

patterns.title: In MWCC inline asm, ldr/str with a bare [rN] base (no offset) can be mis-encoded; write [rN, #0] explicitly
patterns.body: When transcribing standalone asm into an MWCC `asm { }` block for a NONMATCHING function, a `ldr rN, [rM]` written WITHOUT an explicit offset was assembled by MWCC as `ldr rN, [rM, #8]` (wrong immediate), producing byte diffs at exactly those instructions. The standalone mwasmarm assembler accepts `[rM]` = offset 0, but the inline-asm path does not reliably default to 0. FIX: always write the explicit `ldr rN, [rM, #0]` / `str rN, [rM, #0]` in inline asm. Seen on unk_02087284 sub_020873D4 (5 diffs, all `ldr rN,[rN]` -> needed `[rN,#0]`).

patterns.title: Reproduce push{r0-r3} arg-homing by reading args through ((u32*)&firstParam)[n] (inline, not a cached pointer)
patterns.body: When the retail prologue homes all register args with `push {r0,r1,r2,r3}` (and the `pop;pop;add sp;bx r3` epilogue) but the function takes no obvious struct-by-value address, the original took the address of its FIRST scalar param and read the rest as a contiguous array. Reproduce: access args via `((u32 *)&firstParam)[n]` written INLINE at each use (NOT via a cached `u32 *args = (u32*)&firstParam;` variable). Inline keeps each access sp-relative (`ldr [sp,#(8+n*4)]`) matching the homed frame; a cached pointer instead materialises a base register (`add r4,sp,#8`; `ldr [r4,#off]`) which diverges. The `&firstParam` address-of forces the homing. Cache a value that must survive a call (e.g. heapID for Heap_Alloc + its later field store) into a local read ONCE (`enum HeapID hid = (enum HeapID)((u32*)&p0)[1];`) so it stays in a callee reg, not reloaded. Seen on unk_02087284 sub_02087284 (got to a 1-constant scheduler diff this way; NONMATCHING only for the final movs-constant hoist position).

patterns.title: Split a pointer local: declare it early (controls callee register) but assign it late (controls load order)
patterns.body: A cached struct-field pointer whose DECLARATION position controls BOTH its callee-register number (earlier decl -> lower reg) AND its load position can conflict with the target, which wants e.g. a LOW register (r4) but the value LOADED LATE. Decouple: declare `T *p;` early (so MWCC assigns it the low register) but write `p = M_FIELD(mgr);` late (so the load lands at the target position). Verified unk_02087284 sub_020876B0 / sub_0208763C: narc (M_NARC, offset 0) needed r4 but loaded last; `NARC *narc; ...other loads...; narc = M_NARC(mgr);` produced r4 + late load and matched. Related: [[decl-order-regalloc]].

patterns.title: Cache a manager field that is read in MULTIPLE branches into one upfront local, so the base pointer dies early (avoids it being held in a spare reg and spilling another value)
patterns.body: If a function reads `M_FIELD(mgr)` inside BOTH arms of an if (so mgr stays live until the branch), MWCC keeps `mgr` in a scratch register across the body and may SPILL another value to the stack (bigger frame, pervasive regalloc shift). The retail build reads that field ONCE before the branch (its last use of mgr) so mgr dies early. Fix: hoist `int v = M_FIELD(mgr);` to the top with the other field caches and use `v` in both arms. Verified unk_02087284 sub_020876B0: M_1C read in both if-arms forced mgr->r2 and spilled the index arg (94 diffs); caching it upfront dropped to ~18. (Conversely, if the field is needed only AFTER a discriminant compare, inline it in the arms so it is the LAST mgr use and schedules after the cmp.)

patterns.title: MWCC -ipa file: first file-scope const struct pins to rodata offset 0; the REST emit in reverse definition order (anonymous local-array templates stay last)
patterns.body: Refines [[mwcc-rodata-const-struct-reverse-order]]. For N consecutive file-scope const structs, MWCC -ipa file does NOT fully reverse them: the FIRST-defined struct stays at offset 0, and defs 2..N emit in REVERSE after it. Observed in unk_02087A78 with 7 OverlayManagerTemplate: defining them in plain reverse (def1=_02102890..def7=_02102830) produced _02102890@0x00, then _02102830@0x10,_02102840@0x20.._02102880@0x60 (def1 pinned, rest reversed). To emit in forward address order _02102830.._02102890, define _02102830 FIRST then the rest in reverse: _02102830,_02102890,_02102880,_02102870,_02102860,_02102850,_02102840. A function-local array initializer (u32 arr[]={..}; copied to stack via ldmia/stmia) becomes an anonymous @NNNN rodata template that ALWAYS sorts AFTER the named const structs but, when the named block is a single const ARRAY instead of separate structs, the @NNNN template sorts BEFORE the array -> use separate const structs (not one array) when a file mixes a func-ptr template table with a local search array. Verify with chiri pkg -- compare; objdiff cannot see rodata order. nm -n the .o to read the emitted order.

patterns.title: A temp used AFTER a call must be set BEFORE the call to land in a callee-saved reg (matters for size/alignment)
patterns.body: When a local (e.g. a mood/mode flag) is assigned a constant in one if-branch and consumed by a LATER call after an intervening call, the SOURCE ORDER of the assignment relative to the intervening call controls register allocation. Setting it BEFORE the intervening call makes MWCC treat it as live-across-call -> allocates a callee-saved reg (r6) and emits movs r6,#k before the bl, then adds r1,r6,#0 to move it into the arg reg for the later call. Setting it AFTER the call lets MWCC keep it in a caller-saved reg (often the very arg reg, r1) so NO move is needed -> the function is 2 bytes shorter, which can also drop a trailing 2-byte alignment nop (4 bytes total). In a STATIC-module file this size change shifts every following file and cascades to ~all overlays (their relocations to main symbols change) -> 100+ sbin FAILs from one wrong line. Seen in unk_02067A60 sub_02067C30 case 1: must write mood=2; BEFORE FieldSystem_UnkSub108_AddMonMood(...). Diagnose via clean-build next-file address (objdump -t main.elf) not objdiff (which miscounts inline jump tables).

patterns.title: Stack local order: MWCC places the LAST-declared local at the LOWER stack address; flip declaration order to swap two locals frame offsets
patterns.body: When two same-frame locals (e.g. a VecFx32 and a Data struct) land at swapped sp offsets vs retail (objdiff shows identical instructions but different add r1,sp,#N / str [sp,#N] immediates), reorder their C declarations. MWCC -O4 assigns the LAST-declared local the LOWER sp offset. In ov01_021FF6B0 ov01_021FF74C the retail layout is position@sp+8, data@sp+0x14; got it by declaring `UnkOv01_..._Data data; VecFx32 position;` (data first so position, declared last, takes the lower offset). Diagnose by diffing the two functions disasm: same opcodes, only the sp-relative immediates differ in a consistent pairwise swap.

patterns.title: In an OVERLAY, the last functions .balign trailing pad is benign (restored by the following .rodata 4-align); contrast a STATIC-module last function
patterns.body: A 2-mod-4 LAST function leaves objdiff .text short by 2 (no trailing pad in the per-function MWCC section). In a STATIC module this can cascade because the NEXT FILEs .text needs only Thumb (2-byte) alignment and slots in early (see set-cross-call-temp-before-call / unk_02067A60). But in an OVERLAY the last function is followed by THIS objects own .rodata (4-aligned), so the linker re-adds the 2-byte 0x0000 pad and `chiri pkg -- compare` PASSES. Verified ov01_021FF6B0: ov01_021FF830 (last) + ov01_021FF6B0 + ov01_021FF724 each -2 (objdiff .text -6) yet full ROM OK. So dont reflexively NONMATCHING an overlays short last function; run compare first.

patterns.title: To control rodata order of a function-local array initializer, make it a NAMED const struct and struct-copy it (sorts with structs, not as a trailing anon @NNNN template)
patterns.body: A function-local `u32 x[]={..}` initializer becomes an anonymous @NNNN rodata template whose position MWCC controls poorly (often emitted FIRST, before named file-scope consts) -> rodata layout mismatch even when all functions match. FIX: declare a named `typedef struct { u32 v[N]; } T; static const T name = {{..}};` at file scope and copy it with a struct assignment `T local = name;` inside the function (still compiles to the same ldmia/stmia inline copy). Now `name` is a const STRUCT and sorts WITH the other const structs (before const arrays), so you can place it via declaration order. Verified ov01_021FE590: frames table {0x1000,0x1000,0x2000,0x2000,0x1000} -> retail order Template(struct), frames(struct), data(array). For 2 const structs MWCC emitted them REVERSED vs declaration, so declare them in the OPPOSITE of desired order (declare frames before Template to get Template before frames). Always check nm -n <obj> for the emitted .rodata order; only chiri pkg -- compare is authoritative.

patterns.title: An 'unmatchable' adds rN,r4,#0 hoisted before a struct store is often a TWO-arg callee keeping the prior result in r0 (read what the leftover reg holds before declaring a reorder unmatchable)
patterns.body: Symptom (overlay_01_02203A18 ov01_02203BB4, field-effect family cb1 resource-init): after 'work->X.f = call2();' the retail asm emits 'adds r1,r4,#0; str r0,[r4,#off]; adds r1,#64; bl next' — it HOISTS the next call's pointer-arg base (work) into r1 BEFORE the store, and the store's r0 (call2 result) is never reused for the address. Naive C ('next(&work->X)') instead emits 'str r0,[r4,#off]; adds r0,r4,#0; adds r0,#64; bl next' (reuses the freed r0, no hoist): a 3-byte same-SIZE reorder that resists cast-removal, decl-order, and type rewrites (tried u32 vs int arg, FieldSystem* vs void* ptr arg, node struct vs cast, 6L vs 6, local decl reorder — none moved it). ROOT CAUSE: it is NOT a scheduler tie-break. 'next' takes TWO args: next(call2_result, &work->X). r0 is RESERVED for arg0 (the just-stored value == work->X.f), which forces the &work->X address into r1 and its computation around the store. The 'hoist' is just the 2-arg ABI. DIAGNOSE: at the 'bl next', look at what r0 holds — if it still equals the value just stored (str rN,[..] does not clobber rN), the callee has a leading argument you omitted. FIX: add the parameter and pass the just-stored member: next(work->X.f, &work->X). MWCC reuses the in-register stored value for arg0 (no reload) and reproduces the asm exactly. Contrast the genuine load-delay-slot-fill holdout [[load-delay-slot-fill-scheduling-resists-c]]: there the leftover register is DEAD at the call; here it is a LIVE argument. Rule: before calling a same-size instruction reorder 'unmatchable', read what every live register holds at the call site — a 'leftover' that matches a just-computed value is a missing argument, not a scheduler quirk.

patterns.title: A field stored/read with str/ldr (word) but read as (u8) at a call is an int field, not a u8 field — the lsl#24/lsr#24 is the callee param truncation
patterns.body: When a struct field is WRITTEN with `str rX,[base,#off]` (word) from a u8-returning function and later READ with `ldr rX,[base,#off]` followed by `lsl rX,#0x18; lsr rX,#0x18`, the field is an `int`/`u32`, NOT a `u8`. A genuine u8 field would use `strb`/`ldrb` and need no shift. The lsl#24/lsr#24 pair is the truncation of the value to the callees `u8` PARAMETER (e.g. `TextPrinterCheckActive(u8)`), inserted at the call site because the argument is a wider int. Declare the field `int` (so the store stays `str` and the read stays `ldr`) and call `f(work->field)` normally; MWCC emits the shift for the u8 arg. Declaring it u8 produces strb/ldrb and breaks the match. Seen: overlay_01_021F6CFC textPrinterId@0x40 (sub_0205B5B4 u8 return stored word-wide, read for TextPrinterCheckActive).

patterns.title: An explicit return inside an if-block keeps its epilogue separate from the function fall-off return; a fall-through merges them
patterns.body: For a state handler shaped `if (!cond) { ...; X->state = N; <here> } return FALSE;` where the cond-false path skips the block: if you let `X->state = N;` FALL THROUGH to the shared trailing `return FALSE;`, MWCC merges the state=N path and the cond-true fall-off into ONE epilogue. The retail build keeps them SEPARATE — the in-block return uses `add sp,#k; mov r0,#0; pop` while the fall-off uses `mov r0,#0; add sp,#k; pop` (different instruction order), 6 bytes larger. To reproduce, add an EXPLICIT `return FALSE;` after `X->state = N;` INSIDE the if-block, leaving the final `return FALSE;` only for the cond-true (skip) path. Diagnose: objdiff shows the C is a few bytes short and the two trailing epilogues are coalesced. Seen: overlay_01_021F6CFC ov01_021F6E68 (state-3 handler, the work->state=1 path).

patterns.title: Consecutive same-stride rodata structs must be ONE static const array, not N separate static-const objects (MWCC reorders separate objects)
patterns.body: When retail .rodata has N structs of the same type laid out contiguously at a fixed stride (e.g. 5 OverlayManagerTemplate at _02101260,_02101270,... 0x10 apart), they are a single `static const T arr[] = {...}`. Writing them as N separate `static const T a; static const T b; ...` objects lets MWCC REORDER them in .rodata (it does NOT preserve source-definition order for separate const objects), so each lands at the wrong address and the link fails the SHA1 even though every function still objdiff-matches. Diagnose with `nm main.elf | grep <names> | sort` -> the symbols are at swapped addresses. Fix: collapse to one array and reference elements by index (`&arr[3]` etc.); &arr[k] relocates to base+k*stride == the retail absolute label, identical linked bytes. Seen: unk_02078834 sOverlayTemplates[5].

patterns.title: MWCC lays out switch case BODIES in source order; for an inline jump table, write cases in the retail body-address order or the table offsets diverge
patterns.body: For a dense switch compiled to an inline jump table, MWCC emits the case BODIES in the order the `case` labels appear in the SOURCE, and the jump-table .short entries are offsets to those bodies. If you write the cases in numeric order but retail laid the bodies in a different order, the function is the SAME SIZE and every instruction matches, but the jump-table entries (and the reordered bodies) differ -- objdiff EXCLUDES the $d table region so it reports MATCH; only `chiri compare` / `cmp main.sbin` catches it (diff localized to the table offset). Recover the retail body order from the asm: list the case-target labels by ascending ADDRESS and read off their case numbers. Write the source cases in that exact order. Empty cases (`case N: break;`) emit no body, so place them anywhere; include the min case (e.g. case 0) so MWCC bases the table at 0 (guard `cmp #max; bls`). Seen: unk_02078834 nested switch body order 3,1,2,6,4,5,7,10,8,12,13,14,15,9. [[objdiff-false-positive-inline-jumptable-disasm]]

patterns.title: To reproduce a retail parameter SPILL, inline a loop-invariant param*const inside the loop instead of precomputing it in a local
patterns.body: When the retail asm SPILLS a parameter to its stack home (str rP,[sp] at entry; ldr later) and then computes a loop-invariant value from it ONCE before the loop (e.g. mul = a1*10 in a callee reg used by the loop), the natural decomp `T mul = a1*10; for(...) use(mul);` does NOT match: MWCC keeps a1 in a callee reg the whole time, coalesces it with a later local, and never spills (function ends up ~4 bytes SMALLER, with the str+ldr spill/reload pair missing). The retail spill happens because the SOURCE used `a1*10` INSIDE the loop body; MWCC first allocates seeing a1 live across the loop (so it spills a1 to free a callee reg for the loop vars), THEN LICM hoists `a1*10` to a single pre-loop computation (reloading a1 once from [sp]). To match, DROP the precomputed local and write the invariant expression inline in the loop: `for(...) { ...; x = x - a1*10; ... }`. MWCC hoists a1*10 to a pre-loop reg (matching the retail single computation) AND spills a1 to [sp] (matching the str/ldr). Diagnose via objdiff: your function is a few bytes too small and lacks the `str rP,[sp]` (entry) + `ldr rN,[sp]` (pre-loop reload) pair; the param sits in a callee reg in yours but in [sp] in retail. Seen in unk_02066EDC sub_0206759C (badge-shininess reset: `shininess - a1*10` inline forced the a1 spill that a precomputed `mul` local prevented). Related: [[reassign-dead-param-to-steer-spill]], [[hoist-size-local-callee-saved]] (the INVERSE: hoist into a local to KEEP a value in a callee reg).

patterns.title: In an accumulate loop (sum ^= *p++), the pointer bump schedules BEFORE the accumulate op; split it (acc ^= *p; p++;) to get the asm order op-then-bump
patterns.body: A walking-pointer accumulate loop `for(i=0;i<N;i++) acc ^= *p++;` makes MWCC schedule the pointer increment (add p,#4) BEFORE the accumulate op (eor/add/orr). If the asm shows load, op, THEN bump (ldr r1,[r5]; eors r3,r1; adds r5,#4), split the post-increment into two statements: `acc ^= *p; p++;`. MWCC then emits the op immediately after the load and the bump last, matching. Diagnose via objdiff: 2 byte diffs that are just two adjacent instructions (the op and the add) swapped. Seen in unk_0208FB64 sub_0208FD3C (XOR checksum over a3+0x388). Related: [[downcount-copy-loop-needs-unsigned-counter-for-subs-bne]].

patterns.title: A large (>imm) field offset reused across calls may be promoted to a callee-saved reg by MWCC while retail reloads it from the literal pool each use -> NONMATCHING
patterns.body: When a function reads the SAME field `*(int*)((u8*)base + 0xBIG)` (offset too big for a Thumb ldr immediate) several times with function calls in between, MWCC may PROMOTE the offset constant to a callee-saved register once (e.g. ldr r7,=0xBIG; then ldr [r4,r7] each use) — widening the push by one reg and dropping the explicit sub-sp local. Retail sometimes does the opposite: it does NOT promote, reloading the constant from the literal pool (ldr rN,[pc,#x]; ldr rN,[r4,rN]) before EACH use and keeping only 3 callee regs (push {r3,r4,r5,r6,lr}; sub sp,#4). Symptom: every field instruction is correct but the function is ~16-20 bytes too small, your push has an extra callee reg (r7), and the success/store block computes the derived offset (0xBIG+k) once (reusing the cached reg) where retail recomputes it twice. No source form reliably suppresses the promotion (tried: explicit casts each use, array-pointer local, scoped pointer, independent vs derived second offset). The value reload is correct (calls may alias the field); only the CONSTANT caching differs. Resolve via NONMATCHING inline asm using `ldr rN, =0xBIG` (MWCC dedups the pool word, matching retail). Seen in unk_0208FB64 sub_0208FBF0 (battle-record cmd handler, field at +0x4A1C compared 3x against call results + read once for a log byte). Related: [[idx-stride-cse-varies-with-register-pressure]], [[reassign-dead-param-to-steer-spill]].

patterns.title: For `call() != field` emitting cmp with swapped operands, cache the call result in a local so it stays the FIRST cmp operand
patterns.body: A comparison `if (FrontierSave_GetStat(...) != *(u16*)(p+off))` with the call inline produced `cmp r1,r0` (field, result) where retail had `cmp r0,r1` (result, field) — same branch (bne), same registers, just swapped cmp operands (objdiff: 1 real byte diff, the cmp halfword). Swapping the C operands (`field != call()`) does NOT flip it — MWCC canonicalizes inline-call comparisons the same way regardless of source order. FIX: assign the call result to a local first, then compare the local: `u16 stat = call(...); if (stat != *(u16*)(p+off)) {...}`. The materialized local keeps the result in r0 as the first cmp operand, yielding `cmp r0,r1` to match. No extra instructions if the local stays in r0 (it does, being used immediately). Seen in overlay_80_02235900 FrtCmd_178 case 11 (the only diff in a 0x364-byte jump-table function). Diagnose by aligning the disassembly (relative branch targets, drop the inline jump-table by address range) until a single cmp operand-order diff remains.

patterns.title: objdiff can't see BL/BLX reloc TARGET diffs; signed vs unsigned div intrinsic looks identical
patterns.body: When objdiff reports a full MATCH but `chiri pkg -- compare` FAILS on an overlay (e.g. `OVY_80.sbin: FAILED`), the real diff is almost certainly a BL/BLX whose RELOC TARGET differs. objdiff normalizes call placeholder bytes and cannot compare WHICH symbol a call resolves to, so two calls to different functions look identical. Classic cause: signed vs unsigned division intrinsic. `u32 x; x/10` emits `bl _u32_div_f`; `int x; x/10` emits `bl _s32_div_f`. Same instruction bytes, different target symbol -> invisible to objdiff, fatal to the ROM. DIAGNOSTIC (no retail ROM needed): (1) flip main.lsf back to asm, `chiri pkg -- compare` (EXIT 0 -> asm overlay == retail), `cp build/heartgold.us/OVY_NN.sbin /tmp/good.sbin`; (2) flip to src, rebuild, `cp .../OVY_NN.sbin /tmp/src.sbin`; (3) `cmp -l /tmp/good.sbin /tmp/src.sbin`. A 2-byte diff is the BL/BLX second halfword (call offset). Map file offset -> vaddr: `objcopy -O binary -j .text /tmp/<name>_asm.o /tmp/t.bin`, take the first function's prologue bytes, find them in the sbin (xxd -p | python str.find), then base_vaddr = func_vaddr - found_offset; diff_vaddr = base_vaddr + diff_offset lands inside the culprit function. Fix: match the dividend's signedness to the asm's _s32_div_f / _u32_div_f. Generalizes to any BL target objdiff can't compare.

patterns.title: MWCC assigns local stack slots in REVERSE declaration order
patterns.body: When a function's only remaining objdiff difference is the immediate offsets of [sp,#N] stack accesses (same mnemonics, same sizes, different slot numbers), the locals are assigned to the wrong slots. MWCC assigns stack-slot offsets to scalar locals in REVERSE of their C declaration order: the LAST-declared local gets the LOWEST offset (just above the spilled-parameter area), the FIRST-declared gets the highest. Diagnose by mapping each var to its asm slot (objdiff --disasm, find `str r,[sp,#N]` after each var's computation), then list the asm slots low->high; declare the C locals in the REVERSE of that order so MWCC's reverse assignment reproduces it. Spilled params (a0,a1,...) occupy the lowest slots; large arrays (buffers) are placed above the scalars regardless. This fixed overlay_80_02236C9C's frame exactly (push/sub matched after reversing 6 scalar decls). Related: register allocation is NOT controllable this way — instruction scheduling/regalloc ties (e.g. MWCC delaying a store past an independent load, cascading r0<->r1) can remain and may force NONMATCHING even when stack slots and structure match.

patterns.title: static const T x; (no initializer) lands in .data zero-filled, not .bss
patterns.body: To match a retail symbol that lives in .data as zero bytes (objdiff shows .data=N asm vs .bss=N c), declare it `static const` WITHOUT an initializer. In this MWCC config, plain `T x;` or even `T x = {0};` / `T x = 0;` go to .bss (zero-init optimization), but a const-qualified uninitialized file-scope object goes to .data (zero-filled) — e.g. `static const u8 *unused_02201BA0;` in src/overlay_16_02201948.c. The pointer itself stays writable when the const is on the pointee (`const void *p[2]`): writes `p[0] = (void*)x;` add a qualifier (OK), reads cast it away explicitly `(u8*)p[0]` (MWCC allows explicit cast-away-const). Use static if no other TU references the symbol (binding doesn't affect overlay bytes — overlays carry no symbol table). Fixed ov80_0223DD38 (.data 8 zero bytes) in overlay_80_02236B78.

patterns.title: Consolidated rodata struct can't be referenced from NONMATCHING inline asm by member (ldr =sRodata+off inflates +4 -> linker reorders)
patterns.body: When rodata is consolidated into ONE `static const struct sRodata` (the fix for MWCC size-sorting, [[rodata-multi-symbol-size-sorted-use-one-struct]]), a NONMATCHING inline-`asm` function that originally did `ldr rN, =ov01_02208XXX` (a standalone rodata symbol now a struct MEMBER) has NO clean way to load that member's address. Rewriting to `ldr rN, =sRodata + 0xOFF` does NOT fold the offset into the single literal-pool word — mwasmarm emits the pool word for sRodata PLUS extra (observed: function grows +4 bytes, an align nop appears before the pool). The size change then makes the MWCC linker REORDER the per-function .text sections (e.g. the asm fn placed before the C fn that precedes it in source), cascading address shifts into OTHER files in the overlay -> compare fails at the .sbin with scattered diffs even though objdiff says MATCH. Resolution: PREFER matching such functions in C (they reference sRodata.member cleanly). If NONMATCHING is unavoidable, pull the asm-referenced arrays OUT of sRodata as separate named const symbols so `ldr =name` is a single pool word — but then re-verify .rodata lays out byte-identically (size-sort risk) via `objcopy -O binary --only-section=.rodata` + cmp. Functions with NO rodata ref NONMATCHING fine. Diagnosed on overlay_01_021FD41C (camera cb2s 7D4/838 load matrix rodata arr_ef0/arr_f14).

patterns.title: Read a struct member directly (not into a local) when the asm reloads it across calls
patterns.body: MWCC reloads a pointer-dereferenced value (e.g. a1->unk_14, fontSys->unk_60) after a function call because the call may alias it. If the C caches it in a local before the calls, MWCC keeps the local in a callee-saved register instead of reloading -> different register allocation/spills -> mismatch. Fix: read the member directly at each use (e.g. Heap_Alloc(h, 0x24 * a1->unk_14) three times, not count=a1->unk_14 once). Resolved TextOBJ_Create and TextOBJ_CopyFromBGWindow in unk_02013534. INVERSE: a value derived from a CALL RESULT (count = sub_02013BD4(...)) MUST be cached and the asm keeps it in a reg.

patterns.title: Fold multiple return-K into one trailing return via else-if to match a shared exit
patterns.body: When the asm branches (b END) from several paths to ONE shared `return K` epilogue but the drafter wrote inline `return K;` at each path, restructure to `if(a){...} else if(b){...} else {return OTHER;} return K;` (single trailing return). MWCC then emits `b END` from each fall-through to the shared epilogue. Resolved sub_02013B24 (return 0). Same idea: use a `while(cond){...}` instead of `if(!cond) return; do{...}while(cond);` to get the single trailing return (resolved sub_02013BD4, sub_02013E24).

patterns.title: NONMATCHING inline asm CAN reference =sRodata+N for a consolidated rodata struct
patterns.body: When a function references two contiguous local rodata symbols (_020F5F2C / _020F5F2D = base+1) consolidated into one `static const struct sRodata`, a NONMATCHING inline-asm fallback can load them with `ldr rN, =sRodata` and `ldr rN, =sRodata+1`. MWCC emits two correct pool words and the function does NOT inflate (verified sub_02013CD0: 164 bytes, full ROM SHA1 match). The inline-asm escape hatch when the C body matches everything EXCEPT register allocation/scheduling.

patterns.title: An assert before a tail-call with passed-through args needs an explicit return, not GF_ASSERT
patterns.body: When a function asserts then tail-calls passing its own args through unchanged (e.g. `GF_ASSERT(cmd<N); sHandlers[cmd](a0,a1,data+4,a3);`), the ternary GF_ASSERT (`(x)?(void)0:GF_AssertFail()`) falls through to the call, so a0/a1/a3 are live across the (possibly-returning) GF_AssertFail and MWCC saves them to callee-saved regs (extra push). The asm instead RETURNS on the assert path so the args aren't live: write `if (cmd >= N) { GF_AssertFail(); return; }` then the tail-call. Resolved sub_02096D60 (28 vs 40 bytes -> exact). Also: a static helper that ends in `bl X; pop` returns X's result -> must be declared returning int, not void (sub_02096D14).

patterns.title: Own header that uses String/SaveData without its deps: lock include order with clang-format off
patterns.body: clang-format (SortIncludes + Regroup) forces the file's OWN header (matching the .c name) to line 1, BEFORE global.h. If that header is not self-contained — e.g. unk_02031B0C.h uses `String *` but only `#include "save.h"`, and its chain (save.h->pm_string.h) needs `enum HeapID` (heap.h) and `String` (pm_string.h) defined first — the single-object build (no force-include) AND even the full build cascade with `declaration syntax error` / `object 'BOOL' redefined` across many system headers. FIX: a locked block at the top of the .c: `// clang-format off` then global.h, heap.h, pm_string.h, <own>.h in that order, then `// clang-format on`, then the rest. Symptom to recognize: the FIRST error is in the own header (e.g. unk_XXXX.h:NN where NN is a `String *` sig) and BOOL-redefined cascades downstream. (Discovered on unk_02031B0C.) Also: single-object `chiri build -- build/.../X.o` does NOT force-include global.h, so the .c must include it explicitly first.

patterns.title: In MWCC inline `asm` functions, a bare `[rN]` load/store mis-assembles — write `[rN, #0]` explicitly
patterns.body: When writing a whole-function NONMATCHING body as a `static asm`/`asm` function, MWCC sp2p2 mis-assembles a memory operand with NO offset: `ldr r0, [r5]` becomes `ldr r0, [r5, #8]` (a wrong non-zero offset), and likewise `ldr r1, [r4]`, `ldr r7, [r0]`.
