Curiously `[sp]` and `strh/ldrh [r1]` came out as `#0` correctly, but word `ldr/str` from r0/r4/r5 did not. Always spell the offset explicitly as `[rN, #0]` in inline asm — the existing NONMATCHING examples (e.g. src/unk_02091880.c) already do this for every operand. Diagnose: objdiff shows the function the right SIZE but with a couple of byte diffs where `[rN,#0]` reads became `[rN,#8]`. Seen porting sub_0202BCAC/sub_0202BF80 asm into unk_0202B614.c.

patterns.title: Two helper calls in one branch that both pass `(u8)id` get CSE'd (id narrowed in place); pass `id & 0xFF` to one to force a per-call recompute
patterns.body: A dispatcher branch that calls a GET helper then a SET helper, both with the same truncated index `(u8)id`, makes MWCC CSE the `(u8)id` expression and NARROW id in place (store (u8)id back into id's callee-saved reg), then reuse it for both calls. Retail instead recomputes `(u8)id` fresh per call (id stays full-width). Because the two `(u8)id` are textually identical, MWCC merges them. Fix: write the SECOND call's index as `id & 0xFF` instead of `(u8)id` — same bytes (`lsls#24;lsrs#24`) but a distinct AST node MWCC will NOT CSE, so it recomputes per call and keeps id live. Seen in unk_0202B614 FashionCase_GiveFashionItem/sub_0202BB7C/FashionCase_GiveContestBackground (4-bit GET+SET and the contest-bg check+set). Note: helpers must stay `int id` for their signed `%`/word-`(u8)((u32)id>>n)` codegen — a u8 param drops the word `(u8)` mask. Related: [[narrowing-loop-counter-int-for-fullwidth-incr-and-compare]].

patterns.title: `(u8)(id - 0x3d)` passed to an int helper truncates once; retail double-truncates — reassign `id = (u8)(id - 0x3d);` then pass `(u8)id`
patterns.body: When the asm subtracts then truncates TWICE — `subs rN,#0x3d; lsls#24;lsrs#24; lsls#24;lsrs#24` — for an index `id-0x3d` fed to an int-param helper, a plain `(u8)(id - 0x3d)` emits only ONE truncation, and `(u8)((u8)(id - 0x3d))` collapses to one (MWCC folds the redundant cast). To reproduce the double truncation, REASSIGN the int param to its own u8-cast and then cast again at the call: `id = (u8)(id - 0x3d); helper(.., (u8)id);`. The store of `(u8)(id-0x3d)` into the int `id` is trunc 1, and `(u8)id` (which MWCC no longer proves is <256) is trunc 2. Seen in unk_0202B614 sub_0202BA70/FashionCase_GiveFashionItem/sub_0202BB7C 1-bit accessory branches (id-0x3d into sub_0202B848/sub_0202B808).

patterns.title: A stack u16[] the asm keeps with redundant element-copies (strh/ldrh) but MWCC optimizes away: mark it `volatile` to force the layout
patterns.body: sub_0202BCAC builds `u16 pos[4]` from a packed u32 (`pos[0]=p; pos[1]=p>>16; pos[2]=pos[0]; pos[3]=pos[1];`) and reads `(s16)pos[2]/(s16)pos[3]` plus re-reads pos[2] for a later call. Retail keeps all four slots (strh writes, ldrh copies, ldrsh reads via a base pointer `add rN,sp,#k`) and re-reads pos[2] each use. Plain `u16 pos[4]` lets MWCC dead-eliminate pos[0]/pos[1], promote pos[2]/pos[3] to int temps, and cache reads — 47 diffs / wrong stack frame. Declaring `volatile u16 pos[4]` defeats the dead-store elimination and forces every read from memory, collapsing it to a near-match (here 2 bytes, the remaining diff being a separate register-spill reload → NONMATCHING). Use volatile when the asm clearly keeps a stack array MWCC would optimize, and the array is small/leaf.

patterns.title: Large partial-file decomp: keep functions non-static so DCE does not drop them before objdiff
patterns.body: For a huge .s file decomped incrementally (partial src/*.c, main.lsf kept on asm), C_SRCS uses rwildcard so the partial .c IS compiled (objdiff-able) without being linked. BUT MWCC -ipa file dead-code-eliminates file-local (static) functions that nothing in the partial TU references, so they never reach the .o and objdiff reports them not-found. Fix: during WIP declare/define such functions WITHOUT static (a WIP_LOCAL macro = empty) so they survive as globals; objdiff compares body bytes, identical regardless of binding. static-vs-global only changes the .o symbol-table binding, stripped from the linked overlay, NOT affecting ROM bytes/SHA1. Restore static at flip-to-src. Validated on overlay_02_02248728 (364 funcs).

patterns.title: Two adjacent words: both-loads-then-both-stores means a struct copy, interleaved means individual fields
patterns.body: MWCC schedules ldr;str;ldr;str (interleaved) for individual field assignments like *(int*)(out+0x1c)=p[0]; *(int*)(out+0x20)=p[1];. But for a struct assignment of an 8-byte type *(Pair*)out = *(Pair*)p; it emits ldr;ldr;str;str (both loads first). If the asm shows both loads then both stores for adjacent words at offset 0/4, model it as a struct copy (typedef struct {s32 a,b;}), not two scalar stores. Seen in overlay_02_02248728 ov02_0224B6D0 vs ov02_0224B350.

patterns.title: Control init emission order of two loop-setup values with a comma for-init
patterns.body: When a strength-reduced loop needs counter-init (i=0) emitted BEFORE the walking-pointer base adjustment (p += 0x10) but a separate p declaration emits the pointer first, put both in the for-init with a comma: for (i = 0, p = (u8*)data + 0x10; i < N; i++, p += stride). MWCC then emits movs i,#0 before the adds p,#0x10, matching. The index-expression form ((u8*)data + 0x10 + i*stride) can add an extra instruction (size mismatch) vs the walking pointer. Seen in overlay_02_02248728 ov02_0224D98C/DDC8.

patterns.title: Use a single trailing return so MWCC shares one epilogue instead of duplicating it
patterns.body: Two separate early `return X;` statements can each emit their own `mov r0,#X; pop` epilogue, making the function larger than the asm. If the asm branches both failure paths to ONE shared return, restructure the C so there is a single trailing `return X;` and nest the success path: if (cond) { ...; if (cond2) { ...; return TRUE; } } return FALSE; — MWCC then emits one shared epilogue both conditionals branch to. Seen in overlay_02_02248728 PlayerStepEvent_RepelCounterDecrement (52->48 bytes).

patterns.title: overlay_02_02248728 sprite creators: CreateSpriteResourcesHeader(15 args)+Sprite_Create(SimpleSpriteTemplate) layout
patterns.body: ov02_02248C10 (matched) is the per-sprite creator: builds SpriteResourcesHeader header + SimpleSpriteTemplate template as stack locals (declare header THEN template -> MWCC lays template at lower sp offset, header higher, matching). CreateSpriteResourcesHeader(&header, charId, plttId, cellId, cellAnmId, -1, -1, 0, priority, charMan, plttMan, cellMan, cellAnmMan, NULL, NULL) where the 4 GF_2DGfxResMan* come from AnimManager mgr->0x134/0x138/0x13c/0x140 (cast). template: spriteList=mgr->8, header=&header, position=*pos (struct copy), priority=drawPriority, whichScreen=NNS_G2D_VRAM_TYPE_2DMAIN(1), heapID=HEAP_ID_FIELD1. cellAnmId is set to -1 if it equals (s8)mgr->7. CreateSpriteResourcesHeader is in unk_02009D48.h. ov02_0224A33C is the variant (mode==4 branch, uses mgr->0x19c group). This unlocks the sprite cluster (ov02_02248D18 etc.).

patterns.title: Zero-init a stack VecFx32 with aggregate init {0,0,0}, not three field stores
patterns.body: For a local VecFx32 zeroed then passed by address, three separate field assignments (pos.x=0;pos.y=0;pos.z=0;) store via sp-relative offsets and can differ from the asm by a couple bytes. The original VecFx32 pos = {0, 0, 0}; makes MWCC materialize the address once (add r2,sp,#off) and store through that pointer (str r3,[r2]; str r3,[r2,#4]; str r3,[r2,#8]), matching. Seen in overlay_02_02248728 ov02_02248D18.

patterns.title: For a loop with a re-read dynamic bound, use the index form so MWCC hoists IV setup AFTER the zero-trip guard
patterns.body: When the loop bound is re-read each iteration (e.g. for(i=0;i<*countptr;i++)), MWCC emits: load count; i=0; if(count==0) goto end; THEN set up the strength-reduced walking pointer and loop-invariant constants; then the body. A comma for-init (for(i=0,p=base;...)) forces p BEFORE the guard and mismatches. Use the plain index form base+i*stride and let MWCC strength-reduce — the IV/constant setup lands after the guard, matching. (Contrast: a fixed/compile-time trip count often wants the comma-init form instead — see mwcc-for-init-ordering-comma.) Seen in overlay_02_02248728 ov02_0224D1AC.

patterns.title: Inline a loop-invariant load so it hoists after the zero-trip guard; declare the IV before the bound to match register choice
patterns.body: Two combined tricks for count-guarded search loops. (1) A loop-invariant array base (arr = mgr->off) written as a separate statement BEFORE the loop is computed before the count<=0 guard; inline the expression ((*(T**)((u8*)mgr+off))[i]) instead and MWCC CSEs+hoists it into the preheader AFTER the guard, matching. (2) The induction variable vs the loop bound get swapped registers depending on declaration order; declare int i; before int count = ...; so the IV takes the lower register like the asm. Both needed together to match overlay_02_02248728 ov02_022489F0/A24/AC8/AFC (AnimManager resource-array search + assert).

patterns.title: Explicit return in both the if-body and after it to force two separate (unmerged) epilogues
patterns.body: Inverse of the shared-epilogue trick. When the asm has the conditional BODY inline followed by its own return, and the else-branch jumps forward to a SECOND identical return (two return blocks, not merged), write an explicit return inside the if AND after it: if (cond) { body; return X; } return X;. Using if(cond){body} return X; instead makes MWCC merge into one epilogue (too small); the early-return !=cond form puts the body in the wrong position. Seen in overlay_02_02248728 ov02_0224B964.

patterns.title: bool-from-compare: use init-0-then-if-set-1, not ternary or != 0
patterns.body: To get MWCC s init-0 then conditional-set form (mov rN,#0; cmp; beq; mov rN,#1 with fallthrough), write: int x = 0; if (cond) { x = 1; }. Both x = (cond != 0) and x = cond ? 1 : 0 instead emit the branchy ternary (cmp; beq else; mov 1; b end; else: mov 0). Matters when the bool feeds a call arg. Seen in ov02_0224A418 plttId.

patterns.title: 16-byte struct assignment = two interleaved ldmia/stmia word-pairs
patterns.body: *(Blob16*)dst = *(Blob16*)src where Blob16 is 4x s32 (16 bytes) emits: ldmia r!,{r0,r1}; stmia r!,{r0,r1}; ldmia r!,{r0,r1}; stmia r!,{r0,r1} (copy 8 bytes per load/store pair, base regs auto-increment). Define a 4-word struct and assign it. Seen in ov02_02248D98 (sub_02068D98 result -> obj+0x58).

patterns.title: Empty trailing switch case emits a dead cmp then fallthrough
patterns.body: switch(x){case 0:<body>;break; case 1:break;} where case 1 is empty and equals default: MWCC emits cmp #0; beq case0; cmp #1; <falls through to end>. The cmp #1 is dead (no branch after) because both case 1 and default reach the same return point as the next instruction, so the beq is elided. Seen in ov02_0224D288/D3B4 (state==0 body, state==1 noop).

patterns.title: Keep a big offset in its own register: add it in the pointer initializer
patterns.body: When asm holds base in one reg and a large constant offset (e.g. 0x228 = 0x8a<<2) in another, recombining base+BIG+small per use: write the BIG offset into the variable initializer -- u8 *base = *(u8**)p + 0x228; then use (T*)(base + 0x24) at each call site. MWCC keeps the original pointer and the BIG constant in separate registers, reuses the constant reg, and adds the small offset per call. Writing (u8*)x + 0x228 + 0x24 instead folds to one 0x24c add (too small); &x[0x8a] recomputes 0x8a<<2 inline each time (too big). Seen in ov02_0224B7CC.

patterns.title: unk_020689C8 task launcher sub_02068B0C: caller stack-build shape
patterns.body: sub_02068B0C(UnkTaskManager *mgr, UnkTemplateBase *src, VecFx32 *pos, u32 a3, void *a4, u32 priority) is defined in unk_020689C8.c (types local to that TU). Callers in overlay_02 build pos as VecFx32 {0,0,0} (or pass a VecFx32* arg straight through), and build a small per-call struct on the stack whose address is a4 (1-6 words, populated from the caller args; unwritten words are left uninitialized and still match). priority is a small code (0x81/0x82/0x85/0x87). To decomp a caller: local-extern sub_02068B0C with a mirrored 5-word ov02_LaunchTemplate src type, extern the ov02_022534xx rodata templates, declare an anonymous a4 struct, assign its members (order them so MWCC frees arg registers in asm order), then store the return at work->offset or discard. Seen in ov02_0224B72C/AB58/B298/D58/AA44.

patterns.title: Zero-field struct init: write fields in the exact asm store order
patterns.body: When a function zero-initializes several struct fields with a shared 0 register and the asm store order is non-monotonic (e.g. 0,4,0xc,8,0x10,...), write the C assignments in that EXACT order. MWCC preserves the store sequence, so *(int*)(s+0xc)=0 before *(int*)(s+8)=0 reproduces the 0xc-before-8 ordering. Seen in ov02_0224B2CC and ov02_0224B314 (was deferred).

patterns.title: objdiff false SIZE on inline jump tables; verify via nm + normalized objdump
patterns.body: objdiff.py reports a false SIZE mismatch (asm=N, c=N+8) for functions with an inline data-in-text jump table (MWCC dense-switch cmp rN,#K; bhi default; add r0,r0; add pc; <.short table>). Cause: the asm .o marks the table with a $d ARM mapping symbol so objdiff drops those bytes from the asm-side size; the src .o (no $d) counts them. The functions can still be byte-identical. Verify: (1) arm-none-eabi-nm --print-size on both .o -- the FUNC symbol sizes must be equal; (2) objdump -d both, strip address column and normalize unresolved bl (asm f7fffffe vs src f000f800, both R_ARM_THM_CALL to the same symbol) -- instructions incl. the .short table entries must match. Seen on ov02_0224CFD8/D044 (overlay_02_02248728) facing-direction switches. Do NOT treat such functions as blocked solely on objdiff --summary.

patterns.title: Small fixed-size byte-clear loop in asm is an inlined memset, not a hand loop
patterns.body: When the asm shows a small fixed-size zero-fill as a manual loop (mov r0,#0; L: strb r0,[r2]; adds r2,#1; subs r1,#1; bne L) with NO bl memset, the source is memset(p, 0, N) — MWCC -O4 inlines small constant-size memsets to that exact store-first loop. Writing a hand do-while/for instead fails: MWCC loop-rotates the counter decrement to the TOP (subs before strb) and adds a cmp (bgt), so it never matches and cascades diffs through the rest of the function. Just use memset(). Seen on ov02_0224E074 (overlay_02_02248728), a 16-byte clear.

patterns.title: Switch emits add-pc jump table only when every dense case is explicit (incl. the default-equal case)
patterns.body: MWCC chooses an add-pc jump table over a cmp/beq chain based on how many contiguous case labels are PRESENT in source. If the asm bounds-check is cmp rN,#K; bhi <default> with a K+1-entry .short table, the C switch must list ALL cases 0..K explicitly. A case whose body is identical to the default (e.g. just returns) is still required as an explicit empty case (case K: break;) — omitting it drops the count below the table threshold and MWCC emits a comparison chain instead. Seen: ov02_0224B808 (cases 0..3, case 3 = the bhi-default return) — 3 explicit cases gave cmp/beq; adding case 3: break; produced the matching jump table.

patterns.title: Force in-place subs (not cmp) for an equality test by writing a - b == 0
patterns.body: An equality term a == b normally compiles to cmp rA,rB; bne. If the target asm instead has subs rD,rA,rB; bne — the difference written in place into one operand register (typically the loaded RHS register, which is dead after) — rewrite the term as the explicit subtract-to-zero a - b == 0. MWCC then computes the subtraction (subs rD,rA,rB) and branches on its Z flag, reproducing the in-place subs and exact register reuse. Operand order matters: a - b == 0 gives subs rD = a - b (a=minuend in the first source reg, b=subtrahend reusing its own reg as dest); swapping to b - a == 0 or b == a changes the encoding. Relational </<=/>/>= terms are unaffected (they always emit cmp). Seen ov02_0224D7B0 (vec.x==stored_x was the sole diff; vec.x - stored_x == 0 matched). Related: [[branch-or-vs-and]].

patterns.title: Walker pointer vs array[i] index changes which callee-saved reg the walker and loop counter get
patterns.body: In a for loop with a loop counter plus a pointer that advances each iteration, the SOURCE FORM steers register allocation between the walker and the counter. An EXPLICIT walker — a separate local (void **res = arr; ...; res++) or walking the parameter itself (arr++) — gets coalesced with the saved-parameter register and can land in a HIGHER callee-saved reg than the counter (e.g. walker=r6, i=r5), a pure register-swap mismatch vs the asm (walker=r5, i=r6). Using the INDEXED form arr[i] instead lets MWCC -O4,p strength-reduce it into a synthesized induction variable that is allocated AHEAD of the counter, flipping the assignment to walker=r5, i=r6. Decl-order reordering ([[local-stack-slot-order-equals-decl-order]]) only fixes locals NOT tied to a param save; the param-coalesced walker is immune, so switch walker<->indexed form. Seen ov02_0224D73C (explicit walker and param-walk both gave a 6-diff r5<->r6 swap; anmResources[i] matched). Converse of [[u8-array-loop-indexed-vs-walking]] — there indexed caused strength-reduction churn, here it FIXED the allocation; try both forms.

patterns.title: Indexed access with a large constant offset needs an explicit absolute walker (not array[i])
patterns.body: For a loop body accessing *(T*)((u8*)base + CONST + i*stride) where CONST is a LARGE constant (e.g. 0xcd0, 0x10 with a big stride), the indexed form strength-reduces to a RELATIVE induction variable (synth = i*stride, starts 0, += stride) PLUS a (base + synth) add recomputed every iteration — one extra instruction per loop, function ends up SIZE too big. The asm instead uses a single ABSOLUTE walker (base+CONST + i*stride as one induction register). Fix: declare an explicit walker u8 *p = (u8*)base + CONST; access *(T*)(p + small/reg offset); p += stride. (Contrast [[walker-vs-indexed-steers-regalloc-against-counter]]: when the indexed expression has NO constant offset, like anmResources[i], strength reduction already yields a clean absolute walker and the indexed form is correct — so the rule is offset-dependent: no constant offset -> indexed; large constant offset -> explicit walker.) Separately, the walker/counter register split (r4 vs r6) follows FIRST-USE-IN-BODY for the register but the for-init TEXT order for the emit order of the two setup instructions; put the counter first in the for-init if the asm emits movs counter=0 before completing the walker base add. Seen ov02_0224D880 (two such loops; explicit walkers + counter-first init matched).

patterns.title: A small local array initializer compiles to a byte-copy from auto-generated rodata — write the initializer, do not extern the blob
patterns.body: When a function builds a local array on the stack via a sequence of ldrb/strb (or ldmia/stmia) from a rodata symbol (e.g. 5x ldrb r,[tbl,#k]; strb r,[sp,#k]), that rodata is the COMPILER-GENERATED initializer template for a local array initializer like u8 masks[]={0x01,0x02,0x04,0x08,0x10};. Do NOT declare an extern for the rodata symbol — just write the C initializer and MWCC regenerates the same constant bytes and the same copy code. The .text references the auto-blob via a relocation that objdiff normalizes. Distinguish from a genuine struct copy (which copies from another live object, not a const template). Seen ov02_02250738 (u8 masks[]={1,2,4,8,0x10}, rodata ov02_02253A54). Corollary: a loop-invariant subscript like masks[a0-1]&a1 is hoisted above the loop, so a degenerate for(i=0;i<N;i++){if(inv==0)return TRUE;}return FALSE; matches the spin.

patterns.title: Stack-struct bitfield reads re-derive the address (ldrh has no sp-relative form) — use inline casts, not a cached pointer
patterns.body: To read packed N-bit fields from a u16/u32 on the STACK, MWCC emits a bitfield extraction lsl#(32-w-off); lsr#(32-w) (e.g. lsl#29;lsr#29 for a 3-bit field at offset 0) — NOT (x>>off)&mask (which is lsr;and). So model the packed value with a real bitfield struct (e.g. struct {u16 s0:3,s1:3,...}) and cast over the member. CRUCIALLY: because Thumb ldrh/ldrb have no sp-relative addressing, each stack-struct field read needs add rN,sp,#off; ldrh — the asm RE-DERIVES this address in every basic block. Access via an INLINE cast each time: ((struct Bits*)&s.field)->fN. Do NOT introduce a named pointer local (T *bits = ...): MWCC keeps that pointer live in a register and emits the add-sp ONCE, dropping the per-block re-derivations -> function comes out SIZE too small. Also watch the unsigned compare (bcs/bhs) — make the accumulator u32 so 3-bit field comparisons are unsigned; and steer the accumulator/code into the right registers via declaration order. Seen ov02_0224F6AC (pokeathlon best-stat picker over PokeathlonPerformanceStars.stars). Related: [[local-array-initializer-is-rodata-byte-copy]], [[local-stack-slot-order-equals-decl-order]].

patterns.title: Stack-passed param read via add-sp+ldrb means the param is u8, not int
patterns.body: When a 5th+ (stack-passed) parameter is read in the body as add rN,sp,#off; ldrb (two instructions) rather than a single sp-relative ldr, the parameter type is u8 (or s8 for ldrsb), NOT int. Thumb ldrb/ldrh have no sp-relative addressing form, so a byte/halfword stack param forces MWCC to re-derive the address (add rN,sp,#off) then ldrb. Declaring the param as int yields a single ldr rN,[sp,#off] and a SIZE that is 2 bytes short per read. Fix: declare the param u8/s8. MWCC hoists the common add rN,sp,#off before a branch when both arms read the param. Seen in ov02_0224FCE0 (5th param u8 a5, read in both flags&1 arms).

patterns.title: Dynamic-count loop: use if+do-while to keep walker init in preheader, i<count guard for bls
patterns.body: A for(i=0, walker=base; i<count; i++, walker+=stride) loop where count is a runtime value (e.g. *(u32*)(obj+off)) makes MWCC HOIST the walker init (base address computation) ABOVE the count==0 guard, into the prologue -- it runs even when the loop body never executes. The retail asm keeps the walker init in the loop preheader (after the guard). Two-part fix: (1) rewrite as i=0; if((u32)i<count){ walker=base; do{...; i++; walker+=stride;}while((u32)i<count);} -- the lexical if-block keeps the walker init from hoisting past the guard. (2) write the guard as i<count (unsigned), NOT count!=0: the < form folds (i=0) to cmp count,#0 + bls (unsigned lower-or-same, skip if 0), matching retail; count!=0 emits beq. The indexed form walker=base+i*stride is wrong (recomputes the address per use, SIZE too big). Seen in ov02_0224D0C8 (Field3dObject animation-load loop).

patterns.title: A bitfield value scaled by a power of 2 fuses the extract and the shift (lsl#X;lsr#Y)
patterns.body: When an N-bit unsigned bitfield at offset 0 is used as an array index with power-of-2 stride (e.g. bf.idx * 8), MWCC fuses the bitfield read (lsl#(32-N); lsr#(32-N)) with the *2^k (lsl#k) into a single lsl#(32-N); lsr#(32-N-k). Example: a 4-bit field *8 -> lsl#28; lsr#25 (NOT the and#0xf; lsl#3 you get from (x & 0xf) * 8). So when the asm shows lsl#28;lsr#25 for an index, model the source byte as a bitfield struct {u8 idx:4;} and write bf->idx * stride (or bf->idx as an array subscript), NOT a masked plain value. Seen in ov02_0224FF5C (a0[0x86c] low-nibble index into an 8-byte-stride array at a0+0x7e8).

patterns.title: A small-int local passed to a u8/s8 param must be declared with that exact byte type (and assigned before any intervening call)
patterns.body: A local holding a small constant that is later passed to a u8 (or s8) parameter must be declared with that exact byte type, not int. Declaring it int/s8 when the param is u8 makes MWCC emit a lsls#24;lsrs#24 (or asr for s8) truncation at the call site (+4 bytes); declaring it u8 makes the argument pass a plain register move (add r1,rN,#0). Separately, if that local must survive an intervening function call (it is used after a call), assign its constant value BEFORE the call so MWCC stages the constant in a callee-saved register ahead of the bl (e.g. mov r4,#2; bl). Assigning after the call emits the mov after the bl and may pick a caller-saved reg, diverging from retail. Seen in Task_FieldDig/Task_FieldTeleport case1: u8 mood; if(...){ mood=2; FieldSystem_UnkSub108_AddMonMood(...);} else mood=1; ov02_022507B4(fieldSystem, mood); matched, while s8 mood or assigning mood=2 after AddMonMood did not.

patterns.title: Inline pointer array at a large byte offset: index as ((T**)base)[OFF/4 + i], not raw byte-offset cast
patterns.body: When a function loops over an INLINE array of pointers stored directly at a large byte offset OFF inside a struct (the array is AT base+OFF, not behind a pointer), and the asm shows a walker register = base advancing by 4 with the field offset kept in a SEPARATE register (ldr r0,[r5,r7] where r5=base+i*4, r7=OFF), model the access as ((T**)base)[OFF/4 + i] — i.e. treat base as a T** and use the element index (OFF/4 + i). Do NOT write *(T**)((u8*)base + OFF + i*4): that biases MWCC toward a single base+OFF walker or a different coloring. The index form makes MWCC walk base+i*4 (one register) and keep (OFF/4)*4 = OFF as the offset register, with the loop counter i in its own register — matching retail. This cracked the slot-cleanup loop family. Example ov02_02249DD8: for(i=0;i<4;i++) if(((SpriteResource**)work)[0x6b+i]) sub_0200A740(((SpriteResource**)work)[0x6b+i]); matched first build (0x6b = 0x1ac/4).

patterns.title: Find-empty-and-fill slot loop: index form for the read, raw-offset form for the store-back, >= for the post-loop assert
patterns.body: Extends [[inline-pointer-array-index-form-for-slot-loops]] to loops that STORE a result back into the found slot (e.g. find first NULL slot, allocate, store, break). Use DIFFERENT forms for read vs write: the READ in the if-condition uses the index form ((T**)work)[OFF/4+i] (strength-reduces to the loop walker [r2,OFF]); the STORE uses the raw-offset form *(T**)((u8*)work + i*4 + OFF), which C groups left-to-right as (work+i*4)+OFF so MWCC recomputes work+i*4 then adds OFF as a register offset — matching retail (the walker is clobbered by the intervening alloc call, so the store recomputes). Writing the store with the index form folds it to (OFF/4+i)*4 (1 instr shorter, mismatch); writing the read with the raw form makes it recompute each iteration instead of walking. Also: a post-loop bound assert must be if(i>=count)GF_AssertFail() not if(i==count) — >= emits the blt-skip (0xdb) retail uses, == emits bne-skip (0xd1). Validated ov02_0224A4D0.

patterns.title: Block-scope a per-iteration temp (vs one shared decl) to control callee-saved register coloring
patterns.body: When several near-identical blocks each compute a temporary (e.g. a per-block call result reused within the block) and the objdiff is a systematic r4<->r5 swap between that temp and a long-lived parameter, declare the temp INSIDE each block scope ({ T *res = ...; ... }) rather than once at function top. A single top-level decl gives the temp a function-long live range, which MWCC may color to r4 and push the long-lived param to r5; a per-block decl makes it a short-lived temp colored to r4 each time, leaving the param in r5 — matching retail when the asm keeps the param in the higher callee-saved reg. Validated ov02_0224A8D4 (3 find-by-value-and-clear blocks: shared res decl = 22 r4/r5-swap diffs; block-scoped res = exact match).

patterns.title: Scope a strength-reduced loop walker to each individual loop so it colors caller-saved (not callee-saved)
patterns.body: When the asm uses an explicit absolute walker (base+i*stride, advancing by stride) in a register for a per-iteration check, and there are multiple loops separated by function calls: declaring ONE walker pointer at function scope makes its live range span the inter-loop calls, so MWCC keeps it in a callee-saved register, adding register pressure that shifts other variables (large diff). FIX: wrap EACH loop in its own block with the walker declared inside ({ u8 *p; for (i=0, p=base; ...; i++, p+=stride) {...} }). Each walker is then live only within its loop body (which crosses no call, since the found-branch uses a separately-recomputed index), so MWCC colors it caller-saved (e.g. r1) like retail. Without the explicit walker, MWCC strength-reduces to an i*stride-relative IV and adds base each check (small per-loop diff). Converted ov02_0224DF1C (3 stride-0xcc find-first-inactive loops): function-scope walker=53 diffs, no walker=6 diffs, per-loop-scoped walker=exact. Complements [[block-scope-temp-to-color-r4-vs-shared-param-r5]].

patterns.title: int* array-index manual unroll keeps a stack base pointer for struct zeroing
patterns.body: To reproduce a retail stack-struct zeroing emitted via a BASE POINTER (add rN,sp,#OFF; mov r0,#0; str r0,[rN,#0/4/8]), zero through an int* with ARRAY INDEXING, manually unrolled: int *p=(int*)&v; p[0]=0; p[1]=0; p[2]=0;. MWCC keeps p as the base pointer. FAILS: struct-member form (VecFx32 *q=&v; q->x=0; q->y=0; q->z=0;) and plain v.x=0;v.y=0;v.z=0; both FOLD to direct sp-relative stores str r0,[sp,#imm] (no base ptr) -> N-byte-short mismatch + base-ptr cascade; a real for-loop for(i=0;i<3;i++)p[i]=0 does NOT unroll (keeps i counter+cmp, +4B). Only the manually-unrolled int* array-index form gives base-ptr-without-loop. Diagnose: objdiff function a few bytes short, asm has an add rN,sp,#OFF the C lacks. This was the long-standing DAA4/D9C0/ADF0/E20 offset-zeroing class blocker.
patterns.example: ov02_02248E20 (sprite init) affineMtx zeroing matched via int *p=(int*)&affineMtx; p[0]=0;p[1]=0;p[2]=0;. Unblocks ADF0/DAA4/D9C0 deferred on this exact tie.

patterns.title: Stack-local declaration order is reverse: last-declared gets the lowest sp offset
patterns.body: When matching a function with multiple stack locals (arrays/structs), MWCC -O4 assigns stack slots in REVERSE declaration order: the LAST-declared local lands at the lowest sp offset (just above any spilled-param slots), the first-declared at the highest. If objdiff shows the right opcodes but wrong sp-relative offsets (e.g. strh [r1,#0] vs [r1,#4]; add r3,sp,#4 vs #8), reorder the C declarations rather than chasing the values. Verify against the asm: whichever local the asm accesses at the LOWER sp offset must be declared LAST.
patterns.example: ov02_0224CAB8 (overlay_02_02248728): asm has u8 out[4]@sp+4, s16 idx[4]@sp+8. Original C declared u8 out[4]; s16 idx[4]; -> MWCC put idx@4, out@12 (wrong). Flipping to s16 idx[4]; u8 out[4]; (out last) -> out@4, idx@8 (match).

patterns.title: Flip-to-src for an overlay whose rodata is size-interleaved: consolidate ALL rodata into ONE const struct + #define macros; asm-ref fields use =struct+offset; transcribe the few base+offset holdouts
patterns.body: When an overlay's retail .rodata is in ADDRESS order with interleaved object sizes (e.g. a 12B VecFx32 after a 24B table), separate C const objects can NEVER reproduce it: MWCC -O4 size-sorts separate const objects (4B,6B,8B,12B,..,bucketed; cf rodata-multi-symbol-size-sorted-use-one-struct). FIX (verified on overlay_02_02248728, 76 rodata + 2 .data symbols): (1) Define ALL rodata as ONE `static const struct { <fields in address order> } sRodata = {...};` (+ a separate non-const `static struct {...} sData` for symbols the asm places in .data — const goes to .rodata, non-const to .data). A single struct keeps fields in declaration=address order; MWCC can't reorder struct members. sizeof(sRodata) must equal the retail .rodata byte span (no padding — retail layout is naturally aligned). (2) Restore each symbol name with `#define ov02_XXXX (sRodata.fXXXX)` so function bodies are untouched. (3) For rodata symbols referenced from INLINE ASM blocks, do NOT macro them (a struct-member expr is invalid in `ldr =`); instead reference `ldr rN, =sRodata+0xOFFSET` (mwasmarm supports =sym+imm; idiom already in src/unk_02013534.c). OFFSET = retail_addr - rodata_base. (4) Disassembler-split mid-array labels (e.g. _D94/_D98 inside a VecFx32[6]) are merged into the parent array field, not separate fields. (5) Functions that index a rodata ARRAY by a variable, or copy/large-offset a struct field, get MWCC `ldr =sRodata; base+offset` codegen instead of retail's direct `ldr =symbol_addr`. For a SINGLE such reference, hoist it into a loop-invariant local pointer (`ov02_FieldTaskFunc const *t = ov02_TABLE; ... t[i]`) — forces the folded `=sRodata+off` load and matches. For TWO+ references in one function (base-CSE) or struct-copies that won't fold, pure C can't match — transcribe THOSE functions as NONMATCHING asm using `=sRodata+offset`. (6) A function-local array initializer `u8 m[]={...}` emits a SEPARATE auto-const (size-sorted to the front, shifting all rodata) — if its bytes equal a named rodata symbol, transcribe that function as asm reading `=sRodata+off` (pure-C element-copy from the const struct gets constant-folded to immediates and won't match). VERIFY: build --target main, dump sRodata/sData bytes vs the asm .o .rodata/.data blobs (tools/decomp_harness/verify_rodata.py), check sizeof==span, then flip main.lsf and `chiri pkg -- compare`. Tooling: gen_rodata_blob.py (generator), verify_rodata.py, sort_functions.py (round-trip-checked address sort of function defs, required so .text + auto-const placement match retail).

patterns.title: A register-passed arg whose callee param is u8 in the public header gets a spurious (u8) lsl/lsr #24 at the call site; use a split-header int-width local prototype
patterns.body: Mirror of [[public-header-overwidens-narrow-stack-params]] but for a REGISTER (r0-r3) arg, not a stack arg. When a shared public header declares a callee param `u8` (e.g. encounter_check.h: FieldSystem_PerformFishEncounterCheck(.., u8 rodType, ..)) but the field/value you pass is int/u32-width, MWCC narrows it at the CALL site with `lsls rN,#24; lsrs rN,#24` (+4 bytes) before the bl. The retail asm passes the full word `ldr rN,[base,#off]` with NO truncation — i.e. at match time the prototype the caller saw had an int/u32-width param (the callee reads only the low byte regardless, so int-vs-u8 prototypes are ABI-identical; only the caller's codegen differs). FIX (split-header / IPA discipline): DROP the public header include in this caller and declare a LOCAL prototype with the wider type (`BOOL FieldSystem_PerformFishEncounterCheck(FieldSystem*, int rodType, BattleSetup**);`). Safe when the header isn't transitively pulled in and you're the sole caller. Keep the public header (and the matched callee TU) frozen at u8. Diagnose via objdiff: function a few bytes too big, an extra `lsls #24; lsrs #24` (u8) or `lsls #16; lsrs #16` (u16) pair on an arg register just before a bl. Seen in overlay_01_021FC66C Task_OverworldFish (work->rodType int -> u8 param). Related: [[public-header-overwidens-narrow-stack-params]], [[ipa-split-header]].

patterns.title: A single-use stack pointer param read lazily in a branch homes to the top when declared void* + cast to a local
patterns.body: A setter whose value-pointer is the 5th (stack) argument and is dereferenced exactly once inside an if/switch branch: MWCC may load the stack arg LAZILY at the use site (ldr rN,[sp,#8] inside the branch) instead of homing it into the dead 4th-arg register at the prologue. The retail build homes it at the TOP (push; ldr r3,[sp,#8]; cmp ...). Declaring the param as u8* and copying to a u8* local (u8 *p = val) does NOT help — MWCC coalesces the same-type copy and still loads lazily. FIX: declare the param as void* and add a typed local with a CAST (void *val_ param; u8 *val = val_;). The void*->u8* cast makes MWCC materialize the pointer at the assignment point (function top) so the load is hoisted to the prologue, matching. Verified on unk_02030A98 sub_02030C6C/sub_02030E18/sub_02030FB0 (the FrontierSave bit-flag setters set(p,id,bit,unused,val) with val the 5th stack arg). The matched jump-table setters in the same file (sub_02030B30 etc.) already used void* val_ + u8 *val = val_ and matched first try. Related: [[u16-stack-param-as-int-avoids-ldrh-basepointer]].

patterns.title: Use a real 2D array field (arr[i][j]) for a matrix access so MWCC keeps the row-stride/col multiplies in the asms order; folding fs+off+i*stride+j*2 reorders the adds
patterns.body: A matrix element at fs+0xe0+row*0x40+(col)*2: writing the raw pointer expression *(u16*)((u8*)fs + row*0x40 + col*2 + 0xe0) makes MWCC schedule the two index multiplies in a different order than retail (it computed (col)*2 before fs+row*0x40, retail did fs+row*0x40 first). Using the genuine 2D array field fs->unk_0E0[row][col] (declared u16 unk_0E0[N][32], stride 0x40) reproduces retails exact instruction order (lsls row,#6; sub col; adds fs+row; lsls col,#1; add; add #0xe0; ldrh). The save_frontier.h FrontierSave matrix was declared u16 unk_0E0[5][32] (stride 0x40 correct even though dim0 size is wrong) so the index math matches regardless of the bogus first dimension. Also: for the trailing fixed-row clear, fs->unk_0E0[0x1f] FOLDS 0xe0+0x1f*0x40 into one constant (fs+0x8a0), but the retail keeps them separate (adds r,#0xe0; movs #0x1f; lsls #6; add) — write (u8*)fs->unk_0E0 + 0x1f*0x40 (pointer-decay base + offset) to stop the fold. Verified unk_02030A98 FrontierSave_GetStat/sub_02031108/sub_020311AC.

patterns.title: Packed-nibble array get/set: byte index ((u32)idx<<23)>>24, nibble shift (u8)(idx%2)*4, two separate RMWs for the writer
patterns.body: A 4-bit packed array indexed by a signed int idx (base[idx/2], nibble idx%2): the byte index is NOT idx/2 (which emits the signed round-toward-zero idiom add+asr). Retail uses ((u32)idx<<23)>>24 (lsls#23;lsrs#24) — write that literal. The nibble multiply is (u8)(idx%2)*4 (the (u8) mask makes MWCC fold (x<<24>>24)<<2 into lsls#24;lsrs#22) — idx%2 keeps the signed ror dance (lsr#31;lsl#31;sub;ror#31;add). Reader: return (base[bi] >> ((u8)(idx%2)*4)) & 0xf. Writer is TWO separate read-modify-writes (the asm re-reads after the mask store): u8 nibble=idx%2; if(nibble==0) base[bi]&=0xf0; else base[bi]&=0xf; base[bi]|=(u8)(val<<(nibble*4)); — CSE the masked nibble via a u8 local, and keep even (nibble==0) as the fall-through. A caller looping over the writer passes (u8)i (cast i to u8 at the call) even though the loop counter i stays int. Verified unk_02030A98 sub_02030BD0/sub_02030BF4/sub_02030C34.

patterns.title: A dense switch jump-table bound (cmp #maxcase; bls) needs the MAX case label present even when it maps to default — add an explicit empty case to extend the table
patterns.body: For a dense switch(u8) that emits an add-pc jump table, the range guard is cmp val,#<maxCaseLabel>; bls/bhi default. MWCC sizes the table 0..maxCaseLabel from the LARGEST case label in the source, not from the value range. If the retail table has N entries (e.g. cases 0..0x26 = 39 shorts, bound cmp #0x26) but your highest handled case is lower (e.g. 0x25), MWCC emits a smaller table and bound cmp #0x25 — one real instruction diff at the bound plus a shorter table. FIX: add an explicit empty case for the top value even though it behaves like default: case 0x26: break;  This extends the table to the retail size and sets the bound to cmp #0x26; the new entry just points at the shared break/return target (same as default). Verified ov80 overlay_80_02230B8C FrtCmd_145 (39-entry table, case 38/0x26 maps to default). Related: [[jumptable-needs-all-dense-cases-explicit]], [[objdiff-jumptable-false-size]] (the inline table data makes objdiff report a bogus SIZE/section delta — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare).

patterns.title: A u8 range check (x-lo) in [0,n] may compile to add #(256-lo) (additive inverse) not sub #lo — write (u8)(x + (256-lo)) to match
patterns.body: An if-else range test on a u8 written (u8)(x - lo) <= n compiles to sub rX,#lo; lsl#0x18;lsr#0x18; cmp #n; bhi. The retail build sometimes computes the SAME thing with an ADD of the additive inverse: add rX,#(256-lo); (u8); cmp #n; bhi (e.g. lo=2 -> add #0xfe). To reproduce the add form, write (u8)(x + (256 - lo)) <= n (e.g. (u8)(mode + 0xfe) <= 1 for modes {2,3}). Semantically identical mod 256, but the encoding (add #0xfe vs sub #2) must match. NOTE: rewriting the if-else as a real switch(x){case lo: case lo+1:} did NOT match here (MWCC generated a different/worse dispatch) — keep the if-else and just flip the subtract to the add-inverse. Also seen: a u16 local for a (read+1) value that is only COMPARED (not stored as u16) forces a spurious lsl#16;lsr#16 truncation — use int when the asm compares the full promoted value. Verified ov80 overlay_80_02230B8C FrtCmd_142 (mode-2 range) / FrtCmd_145 case 37.

patterns.title: Dense switch jump table needs an explicit case 0 even when it is a no-op
patterns.body: When the asm uses an inline jump table for a switch over a small contiguous range (e.g. dir 0-3) but case 0 does nothing, you must still write `case 0: break;` explicitly. Without it, MWCC sees cases {1,2,3} as non-contiguous-from-0 and emits a compare-chain (cmp/beq per case) instead of the `add r0,r5,r5; add r0,pc; ldrh; add pc` jump table. Adding `case 0: break;` makes it dense 0-3 -> jump table. Seen in ov01_021F8FC0 (overlay_01_021F8D80).

patterns.title: Aggregate init {0,0,0} vs field-by-field changes the zeroing store base register
patterns.body: Zeroing a stack VecFx32 with field-by-field `v.x=0;v.y=0;v.z=0;` makes MWCC emit SP-relative stores `str r0,[sp,#N]` (encoding 90xx). The aggregate initializer `VecFx32 v = {0,0,0};` instead emits `add rN,sp,#0` then `str r0,[rN,#off]` (encoding 60xx) — a register-base store. When the retail asm shows `add r1,sp,#0` before the zero stores, use the aggregate initializer to match. Cost is a 2-byte add. Seen in ov01_021F8F08.

patterns.title: do-while loop hoists a loop-invariant terminator constant; while-loop may reload it
patterns.body: A linear table search that compares against a sentinel each iteration (e.g. spriteId==0xFFFF terminator) matches better as a do-while than a while. The asm loads the 0xFFFF into a register ONCE before the loop (hoisted invariant); a head-controlled while-loop made MWCC reload/restructure it. Form: `p=table; do { if (p->key==target) return p; p++; } while (p->key != 0xFFFF); GF_AssertFail(); return NULL;`. Seen in ObjectEvent_GetGraphicsInfo (overlay_01_021F8D80).

patterns.title: Put the common return last so MWCC shares one epilogue block; early-return the rest
patterns.body: When a boolean predicate has many branches all returning, and the asm shows a single shared return-block at the end (multiple `blt/bge` targeting it) plus several inline early returns, write the source so the shared value is the SINGLE trailing return and all other paths `return` early. E.g. `return FALSE` once at the end with every TRUE case returning early — MWCC merges the FALSE epilogue to one block. Writing nested if/else with inline returns on both values prevents the merge and bloats the function (24 extra bytes in ov01_021F8FC0 before the fix).

patterns.title: MWCC size-sorts static const rodata objects too — combine into one struct to keep retail order
patterns.body: MWCC -ipa file size-sorts STATIC const objects in .rodata (smallest first), not just exported ones. A matching sibling can pass by luck when size-order == source-order. When retail order is NOT size-sorted (e.g. a 40-byte template array sits BEFORE a 24-byte config), combine the out-of-size-order objects into ONE `static const struct {...}` so they stay in field/declaration order; consumers reference members (&s.config, &s.templates[1]). Confirmed: overlay_01_022001E4 (2 cb templates + config -> one struct fixed a 6-byte rodata diff). A function-LOCAL array initializer (e.g. `int models[2]={1,0xC};`) is also an anonymous const that participates in the same size-sort (it sorted 8B ahead of the 64B combined struct, matching retail). Diagnose with: arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.rodata then cmp/xxd vs the asm .o; or nm sorted by address.

patterns.title: Two sequential guard-ifs returning the same value share one exit when written as ||-of-failures
patterns.body: When the asm shows `cmp a; bne RET; <check b>; beq CONT; RET: <return R>` (a single shared return-R exit, with the first failing condition branching to it and the last condition branching INTO the continue/then path), the source combined the checks: `if (a != A || b != B) { return R; }`. Writing them as two separate statements `if (a != A) return R; if (b != B) return R;` makes MWCC emit TWO duplicated return-R blocks (function comes out 4 bytes too large). The ||-of-FAILURES form (not the &&-of-successes form, which lowers to both-branches-bne with the then-block in the middle) reproduces the exact `bne RET; ...; beq CONT; RET; CONT` shape. Confirmed: unk_0202FBCC sub_02030154 (two 0xE281 magic checks) went from SIZE+4 to exact match; same fix corrected sub_0203018C's magic-check prologue. Related: the success path may be a return (sub_02030154 returns 0 after the guard) or a fall-through to more code (sub_0203018C continues to CRC checks) -- both work.

patterns.title: MWCC assigns callee-saved registers (r4,r5,r6,...) to locals in declaration order
patterns.body: When a function has multiple locals that all need callee-saved registers (live across calls / loop-carried) and only the register NUMBERS differ between asm and your C (identical instructions, e.g. asm uses r4=ptr/r5=counter but C uses r4=counter/r5=ptr), reorder the LOCAL DECLARATIONS to match: MWCC colors callee-saved regs r4->r5->r6->r7 in roughly source-declaration order of the variables that need them. Confirmed: unk_0202FBCC sub_02030724 had mon/entry swapped (mon=r5,entry=r4) -> declaring `Pokemon *mon;` before `u8 *entry;` flipped them to mon=r4,entry=r5 (11 byte-diffs -> 4). Caveat: this only fixes pure register-NUMBER swaps; it does NOT fix code-placement/scheduling diffs (e.g. an induction-pointer init being sunk past a zero-trip guard) or stack-slot-vs-register spill decisions. For a leaf function with no calls, the counter may land in a caller-saved reg (r0-r3) instead. Related: [[local-stack-slot-order-equals-decl-order]].

patterns.title: A function returning two values in r0:r1 (no sret) is a u64 return, not an 8-byte struct
patterns.body: When asm returns TWO values via r0 (low) and r1 (high) with the first PARAMETER still in r0 (no hidden sret pointer shifting params), the C return type is a 64-bit scalar (u64/s64/long long), NOT a 2-word struct. MWCC returns structs >4 bytes via a hidden sret pointer (param0 becomes the dest pointer, real args shift to r1,r2,... and the function grows ~2x) -- that does NOT match an r0:r1 return. A u64/s64 is returned in r0:r1 like any scalar with params unshifted. Use u64 if the high word is zeroed via `mov r1,#0` (unsigned zero-extend of a u32 value); s64 if sign-extended via `asr r1,r0,#31`. Two adjacent u32 fields returned as the pair (ldr r0,[p,#N]; ldr r1,[p,#N+4]) are a single `*(u64*)(p+N)` load. Single-value cases just `return (u32)x;` (zero-extends to r0, r1=0). Confirmed: unk_0202FBCC sub_0203088C (dispatcher; case 4 returns *(u64*)(record+0x58), other cases return a u16/u8 field). The 2-byte struct-return form (sub_02026DE0 returns struct{u8 lo,hi} in r0) is different -- structs <=4 bytes DO return in r0, but >4 bytes go via sret.

patterns.title: Give derived base-pointers used across calls explicit locals (+ break to a shared return) to avoid an MWCC stack spill
patterns.body: When a function repeatedly accesses two sub-regions of a buffer (e.g. base+0x84 descriptor, base+0xe8 payload) across several function calls and the asm has NO `sub sp` (keeps everything in callee-saved regs + ip), but your C emits `sub sp,#N` and spills: capture the derived pointers in explicit locals once (`u8 *payload = base+0xE8; u8 *descriptor = base+0x84;`) and use them. This makes MWCC keep them in r4/r5 across the calls and pushes a leftover scalar param into ip (r12) instead of the stack, eliminating the frame. Also: if a switch-case does work then `return CONST` and another case/default returns the SAME const, change the case to `break;` and put a single `return CONST;` after the switch -- MWCC then shares one return exit (matching `b <shared_ret>`) AND this often fixes an r0/r1 swap in the tail (the shared return forces the canonical register choice). Confirmed: unk_0202FBCC sub_0202FE14 (was SIZE+24 with sub sp,#4 -> exact match after payload/descriptor locals + break-to-shared-return-0). Related: [[shared-return-via-or-of-failures]], [[mwcc-callee-saved-alloc-follows-decl-order]].

patterns.title: MWCC lays out switch case bodies in SOURCE textual order; reorder cases to match the asm body layout (objdiff jump-table FP can hide this)
patterns.body: MWCC emits switch case BODIES in the order the `case` labels appear in the C source, while the jump table indexes them by case VALUE. When the asm places a higher-valued case body BEFORE a lower one (e.g. case 1 body at a lower address than case 0), you must write the cases in that same textual order in the source (`case 1:` before `case 0:`) so MWCC emits the bodies in the matching order and the jump-table offset words come out identical. CRITICAL: objdiffs jump-table SIZE false-positive (asm .o renders the table as .word data, C .o as instructions) can MASK this -- objdiff reports the function as a clean FP while the linked bytes actually differ in the table-offset words AND the swapped bodies. Only `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) catches it. Confirmed: unk_0202FBCC sub_02030A24 (getter) needed case 1 (3-bit bitfield) before case 0 (1-bit) -- a 6-byte diff that objdiff missed; the sibling SETTER sub_02030978 was already in case-0-first order and matched. ALWAYS run chiri compare, never trust an objdiff jump-table FP alone. Related: [[switch-jumptable-density]], [[objdiff-bl-placeholder-falsepos]].

patterns.title: External const rodata: MWCC size-sorts per TU; wrap in #pragma section begin/end and SPLIT the TU where the retail layout breaks size-ascending order
patterns.body: SOLVES ext-data-section-split (pilot: battle_arcade_game_board_data, full ROM SHA1 OK 2026-07-02). Facts established by experiment: (1) MWCC 2.0 sp2p2 emits file-scope EXTERNAL const objects sorted by SIZE ASCENDING regardless of -ipa file (with -ipa: one .rodata section per symbol, in size order; without: mostly-merged, same order) — the old 'mwldarm reorders size-bucketed' theory was WRONG; mwldarm just places sections in the object's emission order. (2) Wrapping the const definitions in '#pragma section PARENT begin' ... '#pragma section PARENT end' (any section name from nitro/section.h; const data ignores the custom target) makes MWCC emit ONE merged .rodata section, PACKED — required for odd-address neighbors (7/8-byte u8 arrays back-to-back) which per-symbol sections break with pad bytes. (3) Since emission is always size-ascending, a retail layout that is NOT size-ascending overall must be SPLIT into multiple TUs at each point where the next symbol's size drops (battle_arcade: data.c = 0x0223F900..0x0223F9BC sizes 4,7,8,16,16,20,28,28,28,32,40; data2.c = 9E4,9E8,9F8 = 4,16,16). Add the extra 'Object src/<name>2.o' right after the first in main.lsf — mwldarm concatenates in lsf order. (4) EQUAL-size ties emit in a deterministic scramble of definition order — fix empirically per bucket by reordering definitions and checking placed addresses (arm-none-eabi-nm main.elf): observed 3-element bucket [A,B,C] emits [C,A,B] (so define [B,C,A] to get [A,B,C]); 2-element buckets emitted in-order in one TU and swapped in another (alignment-related; just test). Iterate build/nm/permute — 2-3 cycles. Verify ONLY with chiri pkg -- compare (objdiff cannot see section order). Related: [[rodata-multi-symbol-size-sorted-use-one-struct]] (the single-struct fix for INTERNAL/static rodata), [[asm-bss-space-may-be-ovt-alignment-fiction]], [[exported-const-fnptr-array-section-reorder]].

patterns.title: An unreferenced .bss '.space N' in a data-only asm file may be split-time FICTION from the OVT bss_size — mwldarm dead-strips it even from the asm .o; the C decomp must NOT define it
patterns.body: battle_arcade_game_board_data.s ends with '_0223FA20: .space 0x20' (.bss). The green asm-linked build's xMAP proves mwldarm DEAD-STRIPS this unreferenced .bss section — it is absent from the link, and retail's OVT bss_size=0x20 for OVY_84 is just the sibling battle_arcade_game_board.o's 2-byte static bss rounded up to the overlay's 32-byte section alignment (BSS_END alignment). The .s label was evidently reconstructed at ROM-split time from that OVT field. Defining 'u8 _0223FA20[0x20];' in C (kept alive via lcf FORCE_ACTIVE) inflated OVT bss_size to 0x40 -> rom.sha1 FAIL with exactly ONE differing ROM byte (the OVT entry). Diagnosis kit: all sbins pass main.sha1 but rom.sha1 fails -> cmp -l the good vs bad ROM (single byte in the y9/OVT region), then compare '# .OVY_NN.bss' blocks in build/<ver>/main.elf.xMAP between green and candidate builds. Also learned: '#pragma force_active on' around a C definition does NOT survive to mwldarm, but injecting 'FORCE_ACTIVE { symbol }' into the generated .lcf (alongside the existing KEEP_SECTION gsed in common.mk:225) DOES keep an unreferenced section alive — available if a file ever genuinely needs one, but first check the green xMAP: the retail-matching build may simply not contain the section at all.

patterns.title: -ipa file: sampled codegen is byte-IDENTICAL without it; removal is blocked by DATA emission differences, not codegen — and always objdiff a no-ipa recompile before blaming IPA
patterns.body: ROADMAP T0.5 experiment (2026-07-02). (1) CODEGEN: recompiling matched TUs WITHOUT -ipa file produced byte-identical functions — unk_0200B150 11/11 and unk_0202FBCC 39/39 objdiff MATCH (incl. their NONMATCHING inline-asm fns). -ipa is NOT unconditionally load-bearing for codegen; the cascade-prone behavior is narrower than assumed (IPA-only optimizations like the literal-pool/large-offset CSE in unk_0200FA24, and recompilation sensitivity to declaration changes). NEW DIAGNOSTIC: before attributing any mismatch to an IPA cascade, recompile the affected TU with the same command minus '-ipa file' and objdiff — if identical, IPA is innocent. (2) Tree-wide flag removal (old 'strategy (d)') is still non-viable: rodata emission differs without -ipa (external consts get a different .rodata section structure — see ext-const-split-tu-size-ascending-recipe experiments), so overlay/module layout shifts even where .text matches; data files like unk_data_020FD978.c were matched against the -ipa emission shape. (3) CAUTION on experiment hygiene: the first no-ipa full build 'failed the front end' at frontier_cmd_arcade.c int->enum — that turned out to be a LATENT breakage present in BOTH modes (see stale-object-masks-broken-tu), not an ipa effect. Keep the split-header discipline as cheap insurance.

patterns.title: Deleting .d files during build recoveries erases header dependency tracking — a header change can leave a TU that no longer compiles hidden behind its stale cached .o for WEEKS; run periodic full clean rebuilds
patterns.body: Found 2026-07-02 via the T0.5 clean rebuild: commit c3c4576ee (2026-06-21, overlay_80_02229EE0 decomp) added 'void ov80_0222A474(FrontierTrainerData*, u16, enum HeapID, NarcId)' to include/frontier/overlay_80_02229EE0.h; existing caller frontier_cmd_arcade.c passed raw int literals (0xb, 0xcc) which is an ERROR under -W error ('illegal implicit conversion from int to HeapID'). Every 'full ROM compare' between 2026-06-21 and 2026-07-02 silently PASSED because the stale frontier_cmd_arcade.o predated the header change and the routine 'find build -name *.d -delete' recovery steps had erased the header dependency edges that would have forced its recompile. Consequences: (a) after any .d purge, only a tidy/clean rebuild re-verifies header-consumer compilability; (b) when a decomp adds typed decls (enum params) to a shared header, grep for existing callers passing raw literals and fix them with the proper enumerators in the same commit (enum int: zero codegen change — frontier_cmd_arcade.o recompiled byte-identical); (c) ROADMAP T1.6 verify_matched.sh should schedule clean rebuilds, not just per-TU objdiff.

patterns.title: Inside 'if (x == CONST)', pass the CONST literal (not x) to a callee whose arg equals x — MWCC reuses the compare's constant register (zero arg-setup insns) and the switch dispatch temp shifts off r0
patterns.body: PlayCryEx (unk_02005D10) chatot branch: retail's case body starts 'add r1,r5,#0; bl PlayCry' with NO r0 setup — r0 still holds the =0x1B9 pool constant from 'cmp r4,r0', and since we are inside if(species==0x1B9), that IS the species value. Writing 'PlayCry(species, form)' made MWCC (a) rematerialize species from r4 ('adds r0,r4,#0', +2 bytes) and (b) allocate r0 as the jump-table dispatch temp ('ldr r0,[sp,#4]') because r0 looked dead; retail dispatches via r1. Writing 'PlayCry(0x1B9, form)' fixed BOTH in one stroke: the literal's value is live in r0, so no setup insn is emitted and the dispatch temp avoids r0. Symptom pair to recognize: an extra 'adds r0, rN' at a case-body head PLUS an r0-vs-r1 (or similar) switch-dispatch register swap in the same function. Later uses of x in the same body may still use the variable (retail: 'add r0,r4' for the next call) — only the FIRST call after the compare gets the literal. Sibling lesson from the same file: after 'mov rA,#K; str rA,[sp,#N]' (a stack call-arg), retail derives related constants FROM rA (e.g. 'sub r1,r1,#2' turning the stored 1 into -1) — read such sequences as literal args (…,-1,…,1) rather than (…,1,…) when drafting.

patterns.title: compile_one.sh standalone MWCC compile is byte-identical to make's output (483/483 proven)
patterns.body: tools/decomp_harness/compile_one.sh compiles a single src TU with common.mk's exact MWCFLAGS minus DEPFLAGS (-gccdep -MD) and produces byte-identical objects to the make build — proven by recompiling all 483 matched TUs and cmp'ing against build/heartgold.us/src/*.o (2026-07-02). Use it as the decomp inner loop (~1.4s warm vs 45-120s full link); .d files are never emitted so the Wine .d-corruption class is gone from the loop. CWD caveat: MWCC/Wine embed the shell's logical $PWD as the DWARF build dir — the script uses pwd -L, and to byte-reproduce a given make build you must invoke from the same (possibly symlinked) directory it used; the difference is .debug_* only and never affects .text/.rodata or the ROM. Final gate unchanged: objdiff AND chiri pkg -- compare.

patterns.title: objdiff.py raw-ELF extraction + real reloc masking supersedes objdump-text parsing (jump-table false-SIZE class dead)
patterns.body: objdiff.py (2026-07-02 rewrite) slices function bytes directly from the ELF per-function .text sections (MWCC emits one section per function — nm-value schemes across a merged .text cannot work) and masks exactly the relocated fields from the reloc tables (THM_CALL/PC24/CALL/JUMP24/ABS32/REL32...). Consequences: (1) the jump-table false-SIZE class is gone — do not hand-wave SIZE mismatches anymore, they are real; (2) legacy text parsing under-counted size for 77% of functions by dropping literal-pool .word lines, so any pre-rewrite logged sizes/verdicts from asymmetric compares are unreliable; (3) benign trailing .balign 4,0 shows as ' PAD ' (body match), distinct from OK; (4) --summary exits 1 on any MISS/SIZE/DIFF/SECT (scriptable), --legacy keeps the old path; (5) data sections are still compared raw without reloc masking (T1.3) — chiri pkg -- compare remains authoritative.

patterns.title: objcopy -O binary to /dev/stdout returns EMPTY on macOS under subprocess capture — never pipe objcopy binary output
patterns.body: On macOS, `objcopy -O binary --only-section=X <obj> /dev/stdout` produces 0 bytes when stdout is a captured pipe (Bad file descriptor class), for both host and arm-none-eabi objcopy. Consequence discovered 2026-07-02: objdiff.py's data-section (SECT) check had been silently comparing empty-vs-empty since inception — every historical 'data sections MATCH' verdict was a no-op. Fixed by reading section bytes via the in-file ELF parser (objdiff.Elf.section_bytes / elf_data_section), now also reloc-masked. Rule: on macOS never pipe objcopy -O binary to stdout; write to a temp file or parse the ELF directly. The --legacy objdiff path intentionally retains the objcopy behavior for historical verdict reproduction.

patterns.title: decomp-permuter under MWCC -ipa file: fast native scorer inside, full-TU sibling gate at win time
patterns.body: Under -ipa file a candidate C edit can perturb already-matched sibling functions in the same TU, so a permuter that scores only the target will 'fix' one function by silently breaking others. Working architecture (T1.4): (1) seed = full TU with ONLY the target's #ifdef NONMATCHING C branch promoted, siblings kept on their #else asm; (2) per-job compile.sh splices the permuter's candidate function back into that full TU and compiles the WHOLE unit with make-equivalent flags, so scored bytes are real -ipa bytes; (3) target.o = the full retail-matching TU, so in the permuter's whole-object objdump diff the siblings cancel and score 0 <=> target matches retail; (4) every reported win must pass gate_win.py -> score_candidate.py, which recompiles the full TU and exits 5 if any baseline-matching sibling regressed. base.c (single-function pycparser view) is parse-only and never fed to MWCC. Pilot proof: sub_02014CBC, 2264 iters/40 min, base 485 -> 435, gate accepted with 18/18 siblings byte-identical. Upstream wart: randomizer typemap only registers defined functions; passes touching calls to declared-only siblings raise KeyError (counted as permuter failures, harmless at ~0.2%).

patterns.title: MWCC soft-float ABI: single float in one reg; double as (r0=lo,r1=hi)/(r2=lo,r3=hi); pool words are lo-then-hi
patterns.body: Master register reference for the MWCC soft-float runtime (_f*/_d*). SINGLE FLOAT (f32): arg1=r0, arg2=r1, result=r0 (e.g. _fadd/_fsub/_fmul/_fdiv(r0,r1)->r0; _fflt/_ffltu(int r0)->f32 r0; _ffix/_ffixu(f32 r0)->int r0). DOUBLE: each double occupies a register PAIR, arg1=r0:r1, arg2=r2:r3, result=r0:r1, where the LOW 32-bit word is the EVEN reg and the HIGH word (sign+exp) is the ODD reg. Verified in overlay_01_021F3378 ov01_021F33B8: the double 9011.2 (0x40C19999_9999999A) is loaded as ldr r0,=0x9999999A (LOW) then ldr r1,=0x40C19999 (HIGH) before bl _dadd -> r0=lo, r1=hi. In the literal pool the two .word appear LOW first then HIGH (memory order = little-endian double). Decode a pool double with python struct.unpack(">d", bytes.fromhex(HI+LO)). Conversions: _dflt/_dfltu(int r0)->double r0:r1; _dfix/_dfixu(double r0:r1)->int r0; _f2d(f32 r0)->double r0:r1; _d2f(double r0:r1)->f32 r0. Verified against overlay_01_021F3378, overlay_96, overlay_02_02248728.

patterns.title: Soft-float compares (_fgr/_fls/_fleq/_fgeq, _dgr/_dls/_dleq/_dgeq, _feq/_fneq) are followed by UNSIGNED branch mnemonics — signedness is NOT inferable from the branch
patterns.body: MWCC lowers a float/double relational operator to a compare helper that sets CPSR, consumed by an UNSIGNED conditional branch (bhi/bls/bhs/blo) that SKIPS the true block. So you cannot read operand signedness from these branches (unlike integer blt/bge vs bcc/bhs). The helper takes the two operands in the normal soft-float arg regs (float: r0,r1; double: r0:r1,r2:r3). Comparing against 0.0f uses mov r1,#0 (0.0f bit pattern); double against 0.0 uses mov r2,#0. Verified mapping (helper -> C op -> skip branch that jumps PAST the if-body): _fgr/_dgr = (a>b) -> bls skip; _fls/_dls = (a<b) -> bhs skip; _fleq/_dleq = (a<=b) -> bhi skip; _fgeq/_dgeq = (a>=b) -> blo skip; _feq/_deq = (a==b) -> bne skip; _fneq/_dneq = (a!=b) -> beq skip. Verified _fgr/_fls/_fleq in overlay_92, _dgr/_dls/_dleq/_dgeq in overlay_96 (e.g. bl _dgr; bls target). float const 4096.0f in these compares = pool word 0x45800000. When decompiling a float compare, write the C comparison operator matching the table above; the emitted unsigned branch is automatic.

patterns.title: How MWCC materializes float/double constants: 0.5f/1.0f via mov+lsl, larger via literal pool; double = two pool .words lo-then-hi
patterns.body: Soft-float constants are NOT always pool loads. MWCC materializes small single-float bit patterns whose low 24 bits are zero with mov+lsl: 0.5f=0x3F000000 -> mov rN,#0x3f; lsl rN,#0x18; 1.0f=0x3F800000 -> mov #0x3f,#... (0x3F80 needs mov#0x7f;lsl#0x17 or pool); 0.0f -> mov rN,#0. Verified 0.5f as mov#0x3f;lsl#0x18 feeding _fadd/_fsub in the round-half-away idiom (overlay_49). Float constants that dont fit mov+lsl come from the literal pool as one .word (e.g. 4096.0f=0x45800000, seen in FX32 float compares). DOUBLE constants are ALWAYS two consecutive pool .words, LOW word first then HIGH word in memory (little-endian); loaded LOW->even arg reg, HIGH->odd arg reg. Examples verified from pools: 9011.2 = lo 0x9999999A / hi 0x40C19999; 10.0 = lo 0x00000000 / hi 0x40240000 (so 10.0 shows up as mov r2,#0 + ldr r3,=0x40240000). Decode: python struct.unpack(">d", bytes.fromhex("HIWORD"+"LOWORD")). Write the exact decimal literal in C and MWCC re-encodes the identical bit pattern. Verified overlay_01_021F3378, overlay_49, overlay_96.

patterns.title: Soft-float int<->fp conversion helpers encode source/result signedness: _fflt vs _ffltu, _dflt vs _dfltu, _ffix vs _ffixu, _dfix vs _dfixu
patterns.body: The MWCC conversion helper name tells you the exact C cast and the signedness, which pins the variable type when decompiling. int->float: _fflt = (f32)(signed int), _ffltu = (f32)(unsigned int). int->double: _dflt = (double)(signed int), _dfltu = (double)(unsigned int). float->int: _ffix = (s32)f32, _ffixu = (u32)f32. double->int: _dfix = (s32)double, _dfixu = (u32)double. float<->double: _f2d = (double)f32 (promote), _d2f = (f32)double (demote, narrows). 64-bit int->float: _f_lltof / _fl_ltof style (s64->f32) and _f_ulltof (u64->f32) appear where a long long is converted. The zero/sign extension feeding the helper corroborates signedness: a value loaded with ldrb/ldrh (zero-extended) or masked then passed to _ffltu is UNSIGNED; one reached via ldrsb/ldrsh or asr sign-extend then _fflt is SIGNED. So if the asm calls _ffltu, the C source expression must have unsigned type (e.g. u8/u16/u32 field) BEFORE the (f32) cast. Verified names present in workload asm (overlay_96 uses _ffltu on ldrb/ldrh loads; overlay_01_021F3378 uses _dflt on signed int).

patterns.title: Dividing a float by an UN-suffixed decimal literal promotes the whole expr to double: emits _f2d, _ddiv, _d2f — not _fdiv
patterns.body: An un-suffixed decimal literal (10.0, 2.0) has type double in C, so `f32val / 10.0` promotes f32val to double, divides in double, then narrows back. MWCC emits: _fflt/_ffltu (int->f32) ... _f2d (f32->double) ; load 10.0 double (mov r2,#0; ldr r3,=0x40240000) ; _ddiv ; _d2f (double->f32). Verified overlay_96 ov96: `bl _ffltu; bl _f2d; ldr r3,=0x40240000; mov r2,#0; bl _ddiv; bl _d2f` = `(f32)((double)(u..) / 10.0)`. If instead you see plain _fdiv with a pool 0x41200000 (=10.0f), the literal was suffixed `10.0f` and stays single precision. Rule when decompiling: a lone _f2d/_ddiv/_d2f sandwich around one float operand and a double constant means the divisor/operand was written WITHOUT the f suffix. Match by copying that: `x / 10.0` (double literal) vs `x / 10.0f` (float literal) changes the entire helper chain. Verified overlay_96.

patterns.title: 64-bit integer helpers: _ll_mul (FX_Mul core), _ll_sdiv/_ll_udiv, _ull_mod — operands are r0:r1 / r2:r3 pairs; FX_Mul = sign-extend, _ll_mul, +0x800, >>12
patterns.body: MWCC lowers 64-bit (long long / s64 / u64) integer math to _ll_*/_ull_* helpers using the same register-pair ABI as doubles: arg1=r0:r1 (lo:hi), arg2=r2:r3 (lo:hi), result=r0:r1. _ll_mul = signed 64x64->64 multiply; _ll_sdiv/_ll_udiv = signed/unsigned 64-bit divide; _ull_mod = unsigned 64-bit modulo (signed mod would be _ll_mod). The dominant use is the inlined FX_Mul / FX_MulInline: `((s64)a * (s64)b + 0x800) >> 12`. Verified idiom (overlay_91, overlay_02_02248728): `asr r1,r0,#0x1f; asr r3,r2,#0x1f; bl _ll_mul` sign-extends both 32-bit factors to 64-bit (r0:r1, r2:r3), multiplies, then `mov r2,#2; lsl r2,#0xa` (=0x800) `add r0,r0,r2` and an asr/lsr #0xc combine the 64-bit product and shift right 12 -> the fx32 rounded product. So a bl _ll_mul flanked by two asr #0x1f and a +0x800/>>12 tail IS FX_Mul(a,b) (equivalently `(s64)a*b` in a VecFx32 dot/scale). For 64-bit divide/mod helpers, the C source has an s64/u64 operand. Verified overlay_91, overlay_02_02248728.

patterns.title: First C file in an all-asm overlay: declare its .public functions in the .c (MWCC -W pedantic 'function has no prototype')
objdiff CANNOT see wrong ordering/content in relocated .rodata (function-pointer vtables) — it masks relocs and reports MATCH
patterns.body:
objdiff masks relocated words before comparing data sections. A const struct made ENTIRELY of function pointers (a callbacks vtable / jump table of handlers) therefore compares as all-zero-vs-all-zero and reports MATCH **no matter what order the objects were emitted in, or which pointers they hold**. Real case: src/overlay_83_022479E4.c has three 16-byte `GridCallbacks` vtables; MWCC emitted them ROTATED (declared 500,510,520 -> linked as 510,520,500), and objdiff printed `20/20 functions + data sections MATCH` for a build whose ROM was broken. `chiri pkg -- compare` failed with only `OVY_83.sbin: FAILED` and no further detail.

DIAGNOSE (no reference .sbin needed): (1) `arm-none-eabi-nm build/heartgold.us/main.elf | grep ovXX_` and check each symbol lands at the address encoded in its own name (ovXX_AABBCCDD must link at 0xAABBCCDD) — this rules .text placement in or out in one step, and is how I proved a `.text -4` objdiff delta was benign padding rather than the cause. (2) If .text is clean, dump the linked overlay directly: overlay base = lowest ovXX_ symbol address (also visible as the OVY_XX section vaddr in `objdump -h main.elf`); file offset = addr - base; `xxd -s $((offset)) -l N build/heartgold.us/OVY_XX.sbin`. Decode the pointer words and compare against the retail `.word ovXX_...` list in the .s — remember the linker sets the Thumb bit, so expect addr|1.

COROLLARY: `objdiff --summary` claiming "data sections MATCH" is NOT sufficient for any file whose .rodata contains function pointers. Only compare (or a direct sbin dump) is authoritative. Related: [[objdiff-usage]], [[objdiff-bl-placeholder-falsepos]], [[section-mapping]].

patterns.title: MWCC .rodata is size-ascending, but equal-size TIE order is not a simple rule — determine it empirically per size class
patterns.body:
MWCC emits file-scope const objects size-ascending, so declaring them in retail address order usually works when retail's layout is itself size-ascending (check first: list each rodata object's size in address order). The TIE order for equal-size objects is NOT a single rule — do not assume declaration order, reverse, or first-use. Measured in one file (src/overlay_83_022479E4.c, 13 objects across 8 size classes):
- 20-byte pair (TouchscreenHitbox[5], int[5] — different types): declaration order PRESERVED.
- 28-byte pair (int[7], int[7] — same type): declaration order PRESERVED.
- 32-byte pair (DpadMenuBox[4], TouchscreenHitbox[8] — different types): REVERSED.
- 16-byte run of three (all GridCallbacks — same type): ROTATED LEFT by one (first declared landed last).
No hypothesis tested (same-vs-different type, alignment, first-reference order, reverse) explains all four. So: declare in retail address order, build, then CHECK EACH SIZE CLASS and permute only the classes that came out wrong. Two size classes needed fixing in that file; the other six were right first time.
CRITICAL: verify with `chiri pkg -- compare` or a direct OVY_XX.sbin dump, NOT objdiff — if the tied objects are function-pointer tables, objdiff masks the relocations and reports MATCH regardless of order (see [[objdiff-blind-to-relocated-data-order]]). Related: [[section-mapping]].

patterns.title: Four micro-shape tells that pin C source form from Thumb bytes: branch polarity, cmp operand order, bcc-vs-blt, and value-returning early exits
patterns.body:
When a function is logically correct but off by a handful of bytes, the codegen usually names the exact source form. All four confirmed in src/overlay_01_021E8744.c (27/40 -> 29/40 by applying them):

1. **Branch polarity = which arm was written first.** `return a0 ? a0->obj : NULL;` emits `cmp r0,#0; beq L; ldr; bx lr; L: mov r0,#0; bx lr` (non-NULL arm first). Retail had `cmp r0,#0; bne L; mov r0,#0; bx lr; L: ldr` -> the source was an explicit `if (a0 == NULL) { return NULL; } return a0->obj;`. A ternary and an if/return are NOT interchangeable for matching.

2. **`cmp` operand order mirrors source operand order**, and is often asymmetric across a single `&&` chain. Retail: `cmp r4,r2` (r4=param id, r2=field) for one test but `cmp r2,r5` (r2=field, r5=param) for the next -> source was `... && id == aux[i].id && aux[i].a1 == a1 ...`. Writing both field-first left 7 byte diffs; fixing just the one operand order made the whole first 0x3E bytes match.

3. **`bcc`/`blo` vs `blt` = unsignedness of the compared value.** `GF_ASSERT(idx < 6)` with `s32 idx` emits `blt`; retail's `bcc` means the parameter was unsigned -> change to `u32 idx`. One-byte diff, one-word fix.

4. **`movs r0,#0` before an early `pop` means the function RETURNS A VALUE even if a frozen header says `void`.** ov01_021E8970 set r0=0 at every early exit and r0=1 on the success path: it is `BOOL`, and the header's `void` was simply wrong (24 bytes of missing returns). See [[ipa-header-return-type-widening-can-be-safe]] for how to land that fix.

What these do NOT explain: pure register-allocation swaps (retail r2=index/r1=pointer vs emitted r1=index/r2=pointer in a second loop). Those need structural experimentation, not an operand tweak.

patterns.title: Changing a shared header's return type void->BOOL can be IPA-safe when all callers discard the result — TEST it, don't assume a cascade
patterns.body:
IPA discipline says treat every shared-header edit as a cascade risk, and the default fix is the split/_internal.h pattern. But a RETURN-TYPE widening where every caller discards the value is worth testing first, because it is the semantically correct fix and costs one build to settle.

MEASURED: `include/field/map_prop_animation.h` declared `void ov01_021E8970(...)` but the asm sets r0=0 at every early exit and r0=1 on success — it is `BOOL`. That header is included by 4 TUs (overlay_01.h, field_system.h, field/area_data.h, field/map_load_manager.h chains) with 3 already-matched call sites (legend_cutscene_camera.c x2, overlay_03/shop_menu.c), ALL of which ignore the return value. Changing void->BOOL and running `chiri pkg -- compare` gave `pokeheartgold.us.nds: OK` — NO cascade.

ISOLATION TRICK: to test a header edit without a finished .c, revert main.lsf to the asm object and keep ONLY the header change, then run compare. The asm object ignores the C prototype, so a pass isolates the header edit as IPA-safe and banks that answer for later. If it fails, fall back to [[frozen-prototype-header-split]].

Does NOT generalize to: adding/removing parameters, narrowing a param type (see [[frozen-callee-proto-for-narrowed-args]] — that DOES change call sites via integer narrowing), or any caller that USES the returned value.

patterns.title: Swapped-register diffs: hoist locals to a C89 block and order them so the LOWER-register one is declared first (stack slots read out in reverse)
patterns.body:
Sharpens [[regalloc-order]] into a repeatable recipe. Symptom: the function is structurally identical to retail -- same instructions, same order, same size -- but N of them differ, and every difference is two registers exchanged (retail i=r5/slot=r4, emitted i=r4/slot=r5).

MWCC assigns registers to INTERFERING locals in source declaration order, first-declared getting the lower register. C99 mid-block and in-for declarations therefore give a different assignment than retail's C89 top-of-function block. Recipe: hoist every local to a declaration block at the top and order them so the variable retail puts in the LOWER register is declared FIRST.

Reading retail's order off the object: stack SLOTS are assigned in REVERSE declaration order (last declared gets the lowest sp offset). For a function with spilled locals, sort the spill offsets descending and you have the source declaration order directly -- no guessing.

SCOPE LIMIT: only locals whose live ranges INTERFERE. Two counters in sequential loops do NOT interfere; MWCC coalesces them into one register whether they are one variable, two variables, or declared in either order, and declaration order changes nothing (see [[loop2-induction-pointer-regalloc]]).

MEASURED (src/overlay_01_021E8744.c): ov01_021E8D10 (slot before i), ov01_021E8C60 (i before ret), ov01_021E8970 (i before fileId), ov01_021E8BE8 (i before freeIdx). Each went from a multi-instruction DIFF to an exact match with no other change. Related: [[loop2-induction-pointer-regalloc]], [[u8-stack-param-ldrb-vs-hoisted-ldr]].

patterns.title: Early 'return CONST' folded into a shared boolean tail -- write the other return as 'cond ? TRUE : FALSE'
patterns.body:
When a function has an early `return CONST;` and a later `return <boolexpr>;` whose boolean materializes in a register OTHER than r0, MWCC merges the early return into the shared `mov r0, rN` tail (`movs r1,#0; b L`) instead of emitting its own `mov r0,#0; bx lr`. Same size, 2 diffs.

Why the register matters: MWCC does the AND in place on the value's register and uses the constant register as the boolean. For `(a0 & 1) == 1` the value is a0 (already r0), so the boolean lands in r1 and a final `add r0,r1,#0` is needed -- that move is what the early return gets folded into. For `((a0 >> 1) & 1) == 1` the shift needs a temp (r1), the constant goes to r0, the result is already in r0, no move is needed, and both returns stay separate on their own. So the merge only bites when a move is required.

FIX: `return (a0 & 1) == 1 ? TRUE : FALSE;`
DOES NOT WORK: explicit `BOOL ret` temp, if/else, `1 == (a0 & 1)`, `(a0 & 1) != 0` (changes cmp to `cmp #0`, +4 bytes), u32 param, `return 0` vs `return FALSE`.

MEASURED: ov01_021E8864 in src/overlay_01_021E8744.c; its sibling ov01_021E887C matched without the ternary for exactly the reason above.

patterns.title: Two sequential loops over one array: retail's SECOND loop puts the induction pointer in a lower register than the index
patterns.body:
Observed in retail across four functions in one file: loop1 has index < pointer, loop2 has index > pointer, every time. The naive `for (i...) arr[i]` form emits index < pointer in BOTH loops, so the second loop is always a register-swap mismatch.

Declaration order does NOT fix this. The two counters have disjoint live ranges, so MWCC coalesces them into a single register regardless -- verified over six declaration permutations plus int-vs-s32. This is the documented exception to [[c89-decl-order-fixes-swapped-registers]].

WHAT WORKS: declare the induction pointer as a real local and split the addressing the way retail does -- pointer deref in the CONDITION, index form in the BODY:
    for (j = 0, p = arr; j < N; j++, p++) {
